# Container lifecycle tracking in delegation

> Surface `container_id` in delegation console output, Discord notifications, and Worklog audit comments so operators can trace delegated work to the container that ran it, replacing PID references when container dispatch is used.

## Problem statement

The delegation orchestrator (`ampa/delegation.py`) propagates `container_id` from `DispatchResult` into the `delegate_info` dict, but none of the downstream outputs -- console/stdout, Worklog audit comments, or Discord notifications generated within `delegation.py` -- surface the container identifier. Operators and automated audits still see only process IDs (or nothing), making it difficult to trace delegated work to the container that ran it.

## Users

- **Operators** monitoring delegation status via Discord notifications or console output want to see which container is running a given work item so they can inspect, restart, or terminate it.
  - _As an operator, I want delegation console output and Discord notifications to show the container name when work is dispatched to a container, so I can correlate running containers with delegated work items._
- **Automated audits** (the scheduler audit loop) read delegation results and write Worklog comments; these comments should reference the container to provide a traceable record.
  - _As an auditor reviewing Worklog history, I want audit comments to include the container identifier so I can trace which container executed each piece of delegated work._
- **Developers** debugging delegation failures need container context in logs and reports to quickly identify which container failed.
  - _As a developer investigating a failed delegation, I want the failure report to show "container: N/A" when container dispatch was attempted but no container_id was returned, so I can distinguish container failures from process-mode dispatches._

## Success criteria

1. When `delegate_info["container_id"]` is non-None, delegation console output (stdout from `run_idle_delegation` and `execute`) displays the container name/id instead of the process ID.
2. When `container_id` is non-None, Discord notification messages built by `_build_delegation_discord_message` / `_build_dry_run_discord_message` (or the notification calls in `delegation.py`) include the container name/id instead of the process ID.
3. When `container_id` is non-None, any Worklog comments written by the delegation orchestrator include the container name/id instead of the process ID.
4. When `container_id` is None and dispatch succeeded (process mode via `OpenCodeRunDispatcher`), existing PID-based output is unchanged -- no container references appear.
5. When dispatch fails and `container_id` is None, outputs show an explicit "container: N/A" marker rather than silently omitting the field or producing empty strings/KeyErrors. Detection: if `ContainerDispatcher` was used (i.e., `AMPA_DISPATCH_MODE=container` or equivalent), the absence of `container_id` indicates a container failure; if `OpenCodeRunDispatcher` was used, `container_id` is expected to be None and no container reference should appear.
6. Unit tests cover at minimum three scenarios: container dispatch (container_id shown, pid hidden), process dispatch (pid shown, no container reference), and failed container dispatch ("container: N/A").

## Constraints

- Scope is limited to `ampa/delegation.py` and its direct test files. Changes to `ampa/engine/core.py` (dispatch audit record, `EngineResult.summary()`, engine log messages, and engine-level Discord notifications) are out of scope and will be tracked in a separate sibling work item.
- The `delegate_info` dict must remain backward-compatible: `pid` is always present regardless of whether `container_id` is set. `container_id` is additive.
- Display preference: when `container_id` is present, show container_id only (hide pid from user-facing output). When `container_id` is absent, show pid as before.
- Both `SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E` (Container-aware DispatchResult) and `SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX` (ContainerDispatcher implementation) must be completed before this item can be implemented. Both are currently in `in_review` stage with all acceptance criteria met.

## Existing state

- `DispatchResult` dataclass (`ampa/engine/dispatch.py`) already carries an optional `container_id: str | None` field (default `None`).
- `run_idle_delegation()` in `delegation.py` already copies both `pid` and `container_id` from `DispatchResult` into the `delegate_info` dict (lines ~398-401).
- Delegation report functions (`_build_dry_run_report`, `_build_delegation_report`) list candidates and skip reasons but do not currently include `pid` or `container_id`.
- Discord notifications built by `_build_delegation_discord_message` / `_build_dry_run_discord_message` summarize the delegation report but do not include `pid` or `container_id`.
- Delegation test files (`test_delegation_output.py`, `test_delegation_dispatch.py`, `test_delegation_report_comprehensive.py`, `test_delegation_report_dedup.py`) construct mock `DispatchResult` objects with `pid` but without `container_id`.
- Integration tests in `test_scheduler_integration.py` (lines 242-297) already verify `container_id` propagation into `delegate_info` for both None and present cases.

## Desired change

- Update delegation console output formatting in `delegation.py` to display `container_id` (when present) instead of `pid`. When `container_id` is None in process mode, display `pid` as today. When `container_id` is None after a failed container dispatch, display "container: N/A".
- Update Discord notification message construction in `delegation.py` to include `container_id` when present, replacing `pid` in the user-facing message.
- Update any Worklog comment writing in `delegation.py` to reference `container_id` when present.
- Add or update unit tests to cover:
  - Container dispatch: output shows container name, pid hidden
  - Process dispatch: output shows pid, no container reference
  - Failed container dispatch: output shows "container: N/A"
- Preserve backward compatibility of `delegate_info` dict (both `pid` and `container_id` always present).

## Related work

- SA-0MLYZUKT30VDY7KF -- "Use containers in the delegate flow" (parent epic)
- SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E -- "Container-aware DispatchResult" (dependency, completed/in_review)
- SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX -- "ContainerDispatcher implementation" (dependency, completed/in_review)
- SA-0MM3CPC3Y1E3XIYP -- "Container teardown on completion" (sibling under parent epic)
- SA-0MM3CPS020F89UZZ -- "Stale container watchdog" (sibling under parent epic, blocked)
- SA-0MLYOP9XN1I6P8MX -- "Revisit delegation architecture" (open, related architecture item)
- `ampa/delegation.py` -- Primary implementation file
- `ampa/engine/dispatch.py` -- DispatchResult dataclass (container_id field)
- `tests/test_delegation_output.py` -- Delegation console output tests
- `tests/test_delegation_report_comprehensive.py` -- Report formatting tests
- `tests/test_scheduler_integration.py` -- Integration tests with container_id propagation

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Scope creep into engine/core.py.** This item is scoped to delegation.py only. Opportunities to add container_id to engine dispatch records, EngineResult.summary(), and engine-level notifications should be tracked as a separate sibling work item, not expanded here. Mitigation: create the sibling item as part of this intake.
- **Risk: Dispatch mode detection ambiguity.** Determining whether a None container_id means "process mode" vs "container dispatch failed" requires knowing which dispatcher was used. Mitigation: use the presence of dispatch mode configuration (e.g., AMPA_DISPATCH_MODE env var) or inspect the dispatcher type in delegate_info if available. If neither is feasible, document the limitation and default to silent omission for the "N/A" case.
- **Risk: Discord message length limits.** Adding container_id to Discord messages could push them over character limits for long container names. Mitigation: truncate container names to a reasonable length (e.g., 40 chars) in notification messages.
- **Assumption:** Both dependency items (SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E and SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX) will be merged before implementation begins. Both are in_review with all AC met.
- **Assumption:** delegation.py's Discord notification functions are the correct place to add container_id for operator-visible notifications; engine/core.py notifications are handled separately.

## Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E** -- "Container-aware DispatchResult" (completed, in_review). Direct dependency: adds the `container_id` field to `DispatchResult` and propagates it into `delegate_info`. This item's changes build on top of that propagation to surface `container_id` in user-facing outputs.
- **SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX** -- "ContainerDispatcher implementation" (completed, in_review). Direct dependency: implements the dispatcher that populates `container_id` on `DispatchResult`. Without this, `container_id` is always None.
- **SA-0MMLS6O0Y1DFCZWH** -- "Container-id tracking in engine dispatch records and notifications" (open, idea). Sibling item created during this intake to cover the engine/core.py gaps that are out of scope here (dispatch audit record, `EngineResult.summary()`, engine-level Discord notifications, and log messages).
- **SA-0MM3CPC3Y1E3XIYP** -- "Container teardown on completion" (open). Sibling under parent epic; teardown logic may need to reference the same `container_id` in its notifications/reports, making consistent formatting established here reusable.
- **SA-0MM3CPS020F89UZZ** -- "Stale container watchdog" (blocked). Sibling that detects orphaned containers; will benefit from the dispatch-mode detection pattern established in this item's "container: N/A" handling.
- **SA-0MLYOP9XN1I6P8MX** -- "Revisit delegation architecture" (open). Architectural item that may restructure where delegation reports are generated; changes here should remain localized to delegation.py to minimize rework if the architecture is revised.
- **SA-0MLGE81WY17PH696** -- "Delegation runner stuck -- opencode child processes not returning" (completed). Prior critical bug about delegation process tracking; relevant for understanding failure modes where `container_id` might be None after a container dispatch attempt.
- `ampa/delegation.py` -- Primary implementation file. Contains `run_idle_delegation()`, `execute()`, Discord notification builders, and Worklog comment writing. All changes in this item are confined here.
- `ampa/engine/dispatch.py` -- `DispatchResult` dataclass with `container_id: str | None` field. Read-only dependency; no changes needed in this file.
- `tests/test_scheduler_integration.py` -- Integration tests (lines 242-297) already verify `container_id` propagation into `delegate_info` for both None and present cases. New tests in this item should complement, not duplicate, these.

## Summary

Ensure containers are torn down when delegated work completes (success or failure). Add a teardown_container() method and integrate it with the delegation completion flow. Release the pool claim so the container slot becomes available for reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- teardown_container(container_id) stops and removes the container via podman/distrobox CLI

- Pool claim is released after teardown (pool-state.json updated, container slot freed)
- Teardown timeout is configurable via AMPA_CONTAINER_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT (default: 60 seconds)
- Teardown is idempotent: calling it on an already-removed container does not raise an error
- No orphaned containers remain after normal delegation completion
- Negative case: if teardown times out, error is logged and container is marked for watchdog cleanup (not silently ignored)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add teardown_container() function in ampa/engine/dispatch.py (or a new teardown module)
- Shell out to podman stop + podman rm (or distrobox rm) with configurable timeout
- Integrate teardown call into delegation completion flow in delegation.py
- Release pool claim by updating pool-state.json or calling wl ampa finish-work
- Add idempotency check (handle already-removed containers gracefully)
- Add unit tests with mocked subprocess calls

- ampa/engine/dispatch.py — teardown_container() method
- ampa/delegation.py — delegation completion flow

## Summary

Update the `wl next` sorting/re-sort algorithm to apply score boosts for items and parents that have active work in progress. This ensures that ongoing work streams are prioritized for completion before new work is started.

## User Story

As an agent or operator, when I ask `wl next` for the next item to work on, I want items that are already in_progress (or whose children are in_progress) to be ranked higher so that I focus on completing active work before picking up new tasks.

## Current Behavior

The `wl next` re-sort algorithm ranks items by priority, dependency status, and optionally recency, but does not consider whether an item (or its children) is already in_progress. This means a high-priority open item may be recommended over a sibling that is already partially complete.

## Desired Behavior

Apply the following multiplier boosts to the item's computed score during re-sort:

1. **Direct in_progress boost (1.5x):** If an item has `status: in-progress`, multiply its score by 1.5.
2. **Parent of in_progress boost (1.25x):** If any direct child of an item has `status: in-progress`, multiply the parent item's score by 1.25.

These boosts stack with existing priority and dependency scoring but should be applied as multipliers after the base score is computed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: When an item has `status: in-progress`, its re-sort score is multiplied by 1.5 compared to an otherwise identical item with `status: open`.
- [ ] AC2: When an item has at least one direct child with `status: in-progress`, its re-sort score is multiplied by 1.25 compared to an otherwise identical item whose children are all open.
- [ ] AC3: The boosts are multiplicative with the existing base score (priority, dependencies, etc.), not additive flat values.
- [ ] AC4: If an item is itself in_progress AND has in_progress children, only the direct boost (1.5x) applies (do not double-stack both boosts on the same item).
- [ ] AC5: The boost does not apply to items with `status: completed` or `status: closed` — those items are already excluded from `wl next` results.
- [ ] AC6: Unit tests verify scoring with and without in_progress status for both direct items and parent items.
- [ ] AC7: `wl next --no-re-sort` continues to skip re-sort entirely and is unaffected by this change.

## Implementation Notes

- The re-sort algorithm is in the Worklog source (likely `src/commands/next.ts` or a shared scoring module).
- The boost should be applied during the re-sort scoring phase, after base score computation but before final ranking.
- Parent-child lookup is already available via `parentId` fields; the algorithm needs to check children's statuses when scoring a parent.
- Consider performance: for large worklogs, pre-compute a set of parent IDs that have in_progress children rather than scanning children per-item.

## Risks

- Risk: Double-stacking boosts could over-prioritize items. Mitigation: AC4 explicitly prevents this.
- Risk: Performance impact on large worklogs from child status lookups. Mitigation: Pre-compute parent set in O(n) before scoring loop.

## Related

- `wl next --help` documents current flags including `--no-re-sort` and `--recency-policy`
- sortIndex field on work items reflects the last re-sort output
data.title: Sorting algorithm: boost in_progress items and their parents

Problem statement

Create an `auto-delegate` scheduler command that periodically runs `wl next --json` and automatically delegates the recommended work item to the GitHub Copilot coding agent when the recommended item is in `plan_complete` stage and has `high` or `critical` priority.

Users

- Project operators (PMs) — want high-priority, planned work to begin implementation without manual delegation.
- Automated agents / GitHub Copilot — receive delegated items to begin code implementation.

User stories

- As a PM, I want plan-complete high/critical items to be auto-delegated so implementation starts promptly.
- As an operator, I want the scheduler to log delegation decisions and notify the team when delegation fails.

Success criteria

- The scheduler command runs on the configured cadence (every 30 minutes by default) and calls `wl next --json`.
- When `wl next` returns a work item with `stage == plan_complete` and `priority` in (`high`, `critical`), the command runs `wl gh delegate <id>` targeting the GitHub Copilot coding agent and records the action in the scheduler logs.
- If `wl gh delegate` fails, the command retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff; persistent failure posts a Discord notification with the error and work item id.
- The command is configurable in `scheduler_store_example.json` and can be disabled by default in operator deployments.

Constraints

- Use existing scheduler infrastructure (`ampa/scheduler.py`, `ampa/scheduler_helpers.py`, `ampa/scheduler_store.py`) and delegation helpers in `ampa/delegation.py` where appropriate.
- Do not require LLM availability for this command (`requires_llm: false`).

Existing state

- Scheduler framework exists in `ampa/scheduler.py` and supports registration of command types; helper functions for auto-registration and Discord notifications exist in `ampa/scheduler_helpers.py` and `ampa/notifications.py`.
- Delegation primitives and orchestration live in `ampa/delegation.py`.

Desired change

- Implement a new runner `ampa/auto_delegate.py` with `AutoDelegateRunner` that invokes `wl next --json`, checks stage/priority, and calls `wl gh delegate <id>` when criteria match. Integrate into `Scheduler.start_command()` and add a command entry in `ampa/scheduler_store.py` / `scheduler_store_example.json`.

Related work

- ampa/scheduler.py — scheduler machinery and `start_command()` routing
- ampa/delegation.py — existing delegation orchestration and helpers
- SA-0MLXEM41U1VIK3TB — "Extract delegation orchestration and report generation from scheduler into ampa/delegation.py" (completed)
- SA-0MLX8HGUW0718XI5 — "Scheduler integration: replace hard-coded delegation with engine" (completed)

Open questions

- Rollout: should the command be added enabled by default? (Currently configured to run every 30 minutes; disabled by default is recommended for safe rollout.)
data.title: Auto-delegate scheduler command: run wl next and delegate plan-complete high/critical items

# Resolve stale container-dispatch branches and close associated work items

> **Headline:** Delete the already-merged container-aware DispatchResult branch, rebase and fix the ContainerDispatcher branch into a PR, and close the associated stale-branch review work items.

## Problem statement

Two stale feature branches from the "Use containers in the delegate flow" epic remain unmerged and are diverging from main. One branch's work (container-aware DispatchResult) was already merged via PR #440 but the branch was never deleted. The other branch (ContainerDispatcher implementation) contains unmerged work with a partial acceptance criterion. Both branches and their associated work items need resolution to unblock the container dispatch epic and reduce branch clutter.

## Users

- **Operators/maintainers** who manage the repository and need a clean branch state to avoid confusion about what work is merged and what is pending.
  - As a maintainer, I want stale branches removed so I can trust that existing branches represent active, unmerged work.
- **Developers working on the container dispatch epic** who need clarity on which features are in main and which still need work.
  - As a developer, I want the ContainerDispatcher branch rebased and submitted as a PR so I can review and merge the implementation without rewriting it from scratch.

## Success criteria

- The stale branch `feature/SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E-container-aware-dispatch-result` is deleted (local and remote) since its work is already in main via PR #440 (commit f017aac).
- Work item SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E ("Container-aware DispatchResult") is closed with a note referencing PR #440.
- The stale branch `feature/SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX-container-dispatcher` is rebased onto current main, the partial acceptance criterion #5 (subprocess timeout enforcement) is fixed, tests pass, and a PR is created.
- Work item SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX ("ContainerDispatcher implementation") is updated to reflect the PR and any fixes made.
- The sibling stale-branch review work item SA-0MM8SJX140G614QO is closed as subsumed by this work item.

## Constraints

- The ContainerDispatcher rebase must not introduce regressions — all existing tests must pass after rebase and fixes.
- The timeout enforcement fix (acceptance criterion #5) must be completed before the PR is submitted.
- Branch deletion for the already-merged branch must cover both local and remote refs.

## Existing state

- Branch `feature/SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E-container-aware-dispatch-result` has 1 commit (71a8206) that was merged into main as commit f017aac via PR #440. The branch is purely stale.
- Branch `feature/SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX-container-dispatcher` has 2 commits (71a8206, ce0ce02). The first commit is the already-merged DispatchResult change; the second (ce0ce02) adds ~750 lines implementing ContainerDispatcher, including tests. This work has NOT been merged into main. Acceptance criterion #5 (AMPA_CONTAINER_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT enforcement on subprocess) is only partially met — the timeout is parsed from environment but not applied to the spawned subprocess.
- Work item SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E is status: completed, stage: in_review, needsProducerReview: true. All 5 acceptance criteria met per audit.
- Work item SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX is status: in-progress, stage: in_review. 7 of 8 acceptance criteria met.
- Sibling work item SA-0MM8SJX140G614QO covers the ContainerDispatcher branch review separately but will be subsumed by this item.

## Desired change

1. **Delete the already-merged branch:** Remove `feature/SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E-container-aware-dispatch-result` locally and from origin. Close SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E with a reference to PR #440.
2. **Rebase, fix, and PR the ContainerDispatcher branch:** Rebase `feature/SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX-container-dispatcher` onto main, fix the subprocess timeout enforcement (criterion #5), ensure all tests pass, and create a PR. Update SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX accordingly.
3. **Close the sibling review item:** Close SA-0MM8SJX140G614QO as subsumed by this work item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Rebase conflicts.** The ContainerDispatcher branch has diverged significantly from main (~49 files changed in the gap). Rebasing may surface non-trivial merge conflicts. Mitigation: inspect the branch's own diff (4 files, ~750 lines) against current main before rebasing; if conflicts are extensive, consider cherry-picking only the ContainerDispatcher commit (ce0ce02) onto a fresh branch from main.
- **Risk: Timeout fix may require design decisions.** Acceptance criterion #5 (subprocess timeout enforcement) was left partial. The correct timeout semantics (hard kill vs. graceful shutdown, timeout on dispatch vs. on completion) may not be obvious. Mitigation: review the existing AMPA_CONTAINER_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT env var usage and the OpenCodeRunDispatcher's timeout handling for precedent before implementing.
- **Risk: Scope creep.** Fixing the ContainerDispatcher branch could surface additional issues or desired improvements beyond timeout enforcement. Mitigation: record any discovered opportunities as separate work items linked to this item rather than expanding scope.
- **Assumption:** PR #440 (commit f017aac) fully represents the work from the container-aware DispatchResult branch; no additional commits or changes were lost when the branch was superseded.
- **Assumption:** The ContainerDispatcher tests on the branch are still valid and compatible with the current main codebase after rebase.

## Related work

- **SA-0MM3CMKBQ1454E0E** — "Container-aware DispatchResult" (completed, in_review). The feature whose branch is stale but already merged.
- **SA-0MM3CMZZD1K61ETX** — "ContainerDispatcher implementation" (in-progress, in_review). The feature whose branch needs rebase and fix.
- **SA-0MLYZUKT30VDY7KF** — "Use containers in the delegate flow" (in-progress epic). Parent epic for both features.
- **SA-0MM8SJX140G614QO** — "Review and resolve stale branch: container-dispatcher" (open, critical). Sibling stale branch review item to be subsumed.
- **SA-0MM4LOAAP1M3QQLC** — "Migrate installer/tests away from webhook to bot/token model" (completed). The discovered-from item.
- `ampa/engine/dispatch.py` — DispatchResult dataclass, Dispatcher protocol, ContainerDispatcher class.
- `ampa/delegation.py` — DelegationOrchestrator, delegation result propagation.
- `tests/test_dispatch.py` — Dispatch unit tests.
- `tests/test_scheduler_integration.py` — Integration tests for dispatch propagation.

## Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MM8SKERY18C1EQN** — "Review and resolve stale branch: stash-0-install-ampa" (open, critical). Another stale-branch review item following the same pattern. Resolving it alongside or after this item would reduce overall branch clutter in a single pass.
- **SA-0MLBZOB061YHNV8Q** — "Rebase PR branch on main" (completed). Establishes precedent for the rebase workflow needed in desired change #2; useful as a reference for conflict resolution approach.
- **SA-0MLAJNXE11LPQV66** — "Add scripted routines for cleanup skill" (completed). The cleanup scripts (`prune_local_branches.py`, `cleanup_stale_remote_branches.py`) in `scripts/cleanup/` may be usable for the branch deletion step rather than manual git commands.
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — The authoritative cleanup skill specification. Defines the 9-step cleanup workflow including branch inspection, pruning, and remote deletion. May be invoked directly to handle the branch deletion portion of this work.
- `scripts/cleanup/cleanup_stale_remote_branches.py` — Script that lists/deletes remote branches older than N days, with merge-status checks and dry-run support. Directly applicable to the stale branch deletion step.

Problem statement

Add a reliable CI job that runs the project's Python test suite on pull requests so contributors get fast, deterministic feedback and the repository avoids merging regressions.

Users

- Contributors submitting pull requests (developers) — they need quick validation that tests pass before review/merge.
- Repository maintainers / release engineers — rely on green CI to gate merges and reduce manual checks.

Example user stories

- As a contributor, when I open or update a pull request, I want the full test suite to run so I can see whether my changes break existing tests.
- As a maintainer, I want a CI check that runs on pull requests so I can require the check for merging protected branches.

Success criteria

- A GitHub Actions workflow runs pytest on pull_request events and completes successfully on a representative PR within the expected time budget (target: similar to current test job runtime).
- The workflow installs project dependencies reliably (pip -e .[dev] or equivalent) and exits non-zero on test failures, producing pytest output.
- Test artifacts (pytest output) are available as job logs; optionally, junit/coverage artifacts are uploaded when configured.
- The workflow is configurable to be required as a branch protection status check (maintainers can enable this after rollout).

Constraints

- Must use GitHub Actions (repository already uses .github/workflows/ci.yml).
- Keep the initial job simple: install deps and run pytest; avoid long-running/integration tests in the PR job unless scheduled or split to a separate workflow.
- No credentials or secrets required for basic test runs; if later needed, use repository secrets and document access.

Existing state

- There is an existing workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that already runs on `push` and `pull_request` and includes a `test` job which sets up Python 3.10, installs `.[dev]`, and runs `pytest`.
- There is an `integration-isolation` job in the same workflow that runs a specific integration test file.
- Worklog contains related items about validation/tests and integration CI (see Related work below).

Desired change

- Ensure the `test` job (or a dedicated PR job) reliably runs the full pytest suite on `pull_request` events, produces clear failure logs, and is easily enabled as a required status check.
- Optionally: document how to mark the job as required in branch protection and how to extend the workflow with matrix/python versions or artifact uploads.

Related work

- .github/workflows/ci.yml — existing CI workflow that already runs `pytest` on push and pull_request (file in repo).
- SA-0MLWQI6HO031F4I3 — "Validation & tests: schema, state machine, integration tests" (completed) — contains references to adding CI-driven tests and previous test runs.
- SA-0MLUDW1XP00DCUJT — "Integration tests: per-project isolation (ampa)" (completed) — describes CI workflow job running integration tests on pushes and PRs.
- SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O — "Podman development container for SorraAgents" (completed) — relevant for containerized test environments and reproducible dev setups.

Notes / open questions

- Confirmed scope: run full Python test suite (`pytest`) on pull requests only. Should this job become a required status check after rollout? (Yes/No)
- Any target Python versions or matrix to include now (e.g., 3.10 only, or 3.10 & 3.11)? User earlier selected running full pytest and PRs only; leave matrix optional for follow-up.

Branch protection / required check

- The PR CI job should be documented and configured so repository admins can mark it as a required status check in branch protection. Default rollout plan: create and validate the workflow, then enable it as a required check for the `main` branch once stable.
- Acceptance criteria updated: the workflow can be enabled as a required status check and maintainers have a short checklist to enable it (Settings → Branches → Add rule → Require status checks and select the CI job).

Risks & assumptions (short)

- Risk: Long-running tests in the PR job cause slow feedback and block merges. Mitigation: keep PR job focused on unit/fast tests; run longer integration tests in a scheduled or separate workflow.
- Risk: Flaky tests produce noise and failing required checks. Mitigation: record flaky tests as separate work items and exclude them from required PR gating until fixed.
- Assumption: No credentials/secrets are required for basic test runs; if they become necessary, they will be provisioned via repository secrets.
- Scope-creep mitigation: any requested additional features (multi-Python matrix, coverage upload, container smoke tests) will be recorded as separate work items linked to this item rather than added to the initial scope.

Problem statement
Periodically scan open pull requests in this repository, check CI status, and notify stakeholders when a PR becomes ready for review or when CI fails; create a critical Worklog work item for failing CI.

Users
- Developers with open PRs who want automated readiness notifications (example: "When my branch's checks are all green, notify me so I can request reviews").
- Repo maintainers who want to be alerted about broken CI across open PRs (example: "If CI is failing on any open PRs, create a critical work item so we can triage").

Success criteria
- The scheduled command runs on an hourly cadence and evaluates all open PRs in the repository.
- For a PR with all required checks passing, the command posts a Worklog comment and a GitHub PR comment indicating "ready for review"; evidence: Worklog comment created and PR receives a comment.
- For a PR with failing required checks, the command posts a Worklog comment and creates a critical Worklog work item linking to the PR; evidence: critical work item exists and references the PR URL.
- Authentication uses the `gh` CLI (or configured repo token) and the job runs successfully in the target environment; evidence: successful authenticated API calls recorded in logs.

Constraints
- Runs in this repository (single-repo scope) by default; making it org-wide is out of scope for this item.
- Authentication: primary plan is to use the `gh` CLI available in the runner/container. If `gh` is not available, the job should accept a repo secret token (e.g., GITHUB_TOKEN or PR_BOT_TOKEN).
- Evaluate readiness using GitHub's required checks: a PR is "ready for review" only when all required status/checks are passing.
- The command should not auto-merge or modify PR branches; it only reports and creates work items/comments.

Existing state
- A work item exists: `SA-0MMJY1K3W15RI0F4` — title: "Create a scheduled command that will look for open PRs". Current description: "Periodically look for open PRs, check the status of the CI. If it passes then notify the user that it is ready for review. If it fails create a critical work item to fix the failures." (assignee: Map, status: in-progress).
- The repository contains helpful docs and skills that reference PR handling, CI audit, and the `gh` CLI availability (see Related work below).

Desired change
- Implement a scheduled command (cron job / GitHub Action / repo job) that:
  1) Runs hourly and enumerates all open PRs in the repo.
  2) For each PR, determines required check runs/status and whether they are passing.
  3) If all required checks pass and no previous "ready" notice exists, post a Worklog comment and a GitHub PR comment marking it "ready for review".
  4) If required checks fail, post a Worklog comment and create a critical Worklog work item linking to the PR and the failing checks.
  5) Record run results and errors to logs for observability and retries.

Related work
- .config/opencode/skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md — contains guidance for fetching and handling PR review comments and conflict handling.
- .config/opencode/skill/cleanup/SKILL.md — examples of summarising open PRs and branch handling; useful for PR enumeration patterns.
- .config/opencode/docs/triage-audit.md — guidance on including PR links in triage/audit reports.
- .config/opencode/docs/workflow/examples/01-happy-path.md — shows PR lifecycle examples and relevant checks.
- Worklog: `SA-0MLRHQJ5R1L7SA1F` — "gh cli is not available in the sandbox container" — important to verify availability of `gh` in the target runner.
- Worklog: `SA-0MMJY1K3W15RI0F4` — current item being drafted.

Notes / open questions
- Confirm preferred runtime for the scheduled command: GitHub Actions, a repository cron job, or an external scheduler. (Recommended: GitHub Action.)
- Confirm the authentication method if `gh` is not available: which repo secret name should be used (e.g., `PR_BOT_TOKEN`)?
- Should the command deduplicate repeated notifications? e.g., avoid posting "ready" repeatedly for the same PR.

Related work (automated report)
- SA-0MLRHQJ5R1L7SA1F — "gh cli is not available in the sandbox container": documents environments where `gh` may be missing; relevant to choosing runtime and auth fallback.
- .config/opencode/skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md: contains guidance for fetching PR comments and handling conflicts; useful patterns for posting comments and avoiding noise.
- .config/opencode/skill/cleanup/SKILL.md: shows examples of enumerating open PRs and summarising branch/PR state; useful for PR enumeration and reporting.
- .config/opencode/docs/triage-audit.md: includes examples of including PR links in triage reports and audit evidence; useful for formatting Worklog items created for failing CI.

Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Repeated or noisy notifications — if the job posts "ready" on every run it may spam PRs and users. Mitigation: post once per PR or only when status flips (note: this is an implementation detail to capture in the plan).
- Risk: `gh` CLI or required token may be unavailable or lack scopes; Mitigation: validate `gh` availability at startup and fail early with a clear log message; accept a repo secret token as fallback.
- Risk: GitHub API rate limits or transient errors could cause missed notifications. Mitigation: add retry/backoff and log failures; consider tracking last-run timestamps per PR.
- Assumption: The repository's required checks are configured correctly in branch protection rules; the job will use those settings to evaluate readiness.
- Scope-scope creep mitigation: Additional features (org-wide scan, auto-labeling, auto-assign) are out of scope for this work and should be added as separate linked work items if discovered.

Final headline
Hourly job (repo-scoped) that scans all open PRs, posts a "ready for review" comment when required checks pass, and creates a critical Worklog item when CI fails.

# Intake Draft: Report and force-run disabled commands (SA-0MMLTUHMK1EATTAG)

Problem statement
-----------------
When an operator manually invokes a scheduled command that is stored as disabled (`metadata.enabled=false`), the CLI currently starts a scheduler instance and quietly skips execution without a clear operator-visible explanation. Operators need explicit, immediate feedback when a manual run is short-circuited and a safe way to override the disabled flag for one-off runs.

Users
-----
- Operators / maintainers who run scheduler commands by hand and need to understand why a command did not run (example user story: "As an operator, when I run a command manually I want a clear message if it is disabled so I don't waste time debugging a silent no-op").
- Automation authors who rely on predictable CLI behaviour when invoking scheduled commands manually.

Success criteria
----------------
1. Manual invocation prints a clear, human-readable message when the target command is disabled (e.g., "Command <id> is disabled: use --force to override"), and exits with a non-zero status to indicate no action was taken.
2. Add a one-off override flag `--force` to manual invocations that bypasses the disabled metadata and runs the command immediately without modifying stored metadata.
3. When `--force` is used, the CLI logs the override decision (stdout/stderr and scheduler logs) and still records the run in scheduler state/history as a forced/manual run.
4. The default behaviour for scheduled runs remains unchanged: commands respect `metadata.enabled` when run by the scheduler cadence.
5. Unit tests and an integration test cover (a) short-circuit message and exit code when disabled, (b) `--force` override path, and (c) no persistent mutation of the stored `metadata.enabled` flag.

Constraints
-----------
- Do not change stored command metadata by default: `--force` must be a non-persistent override only.
- Keep scheduled/cadenced execution behaviour unchanged (the gate still applies to automatic runs unless store metadata is edited separately).
- Follow existing scheduler and CLI error/exit code conventions; prefer returning a non-zero exit code when a manual invocation is short-circuited.
- Preserve idempotence: re-running the same manual invocation without `--force` should consistently produce the same message and exit code.

Existing state
--------------
- `ampa/scheduler.py` contains scheduler startup and command execution logic; the scheduler currently checks `spec.metadata.get("enabled")` in some command handlers (e.g., `auto-delegate`) and may return early without a user-visible explanation.
- Commands are auto-registered via helpers in `ampa/scheduler_helpers.py` and defaults often set `metadata.enabled=false` for safe rollout.
- Work items already touching related UX and gating behaviour include: `SA-0MMLTVIYX1GJVPA2` (Split ampa list by enabled state) and `SA-0MM8QJO8J1HS273Q` (Auto-delegate scheduler command — registered disabled by default).

Desired change
--------------
1. CLI change: when a user invokes a command manually and the stored command metadata indicates it is disabled, print a short, clear message to stdout/stderr and exit with a non-zero status. Message example: `Command '<id>' is disabled (metadata.enabled=false). Use --force to run once.`
2. Add `--force` flag to the manual invocation path which: a) bypasses the `metadata.enabled` gate for that run only, b) logs the override decision to scheduler logs and stdout/stderr, and c) records the run in the scheduler run history as a forced/manual run (without changing stored `metadata.enabled`).
3. Emit an operator-visible log entry for both the short-circuit and the forced-run paths; do not send notifications by default for the short-circuit, but preserve the current notification behaviour for actual runs. (If operators want additional notification behaviour later, open a follow-up work item.)

Related work
------------
- `ampa/scheduler.py` — Scheduler start, selection, and invocation logic (key location for the short-circuit + --force handling).
- `ampa/scheduler_helpers.py` — Command registration and metadata defaults (shows `metadata.enabled` patterns used by auto-registered commands).
- `ampa/auto_delegate.py` — Example runner used when auto-delegate is enabled; demonstrates existing guarded-run pattern.
- Work item: `SA-0MMLTVIYX1GJVPA2` — "Split ampa list by enabled state" (make disabled commands visible in listings) — related UX work that complements this change.
- Work item: `SA-0MM8QJO8J1HS273Q` — "Auto-delegate scheduler command" (registered disabled by default) — an example of commands that operators will want to force-run occasionally.

Notes / open questions
---------------------
- This draft implements the operator choices: `--force`, clear stdout/stderr message and non-zero exit on short-circuit, and scope limited to manual invocations. If you want scheduled runs to accept the override as well, we should discuss safety and persistence rules.

---
Drafted for work item: SA-0MMLTUHMK1EATTAG

Risks & assumptions
-------------------
- Risk: Operators may misuse `--force` to run commands that were intentionally disabled for safety; mitigation: make `--force` explicit and document it.
- Assumption: Stored `metadata.enabled` semantics are consistent across commands (true for auto-registered commands).

Final headline summary:
When a manually-invoked scheduled command is disabled, show a clear short-circuit message and add a one-off `--force` override to run it without changing stored metadata.

Headline

AutoDelegateRunner announces each successful delegation in Discord with the work item ID, GitHub link, and runner metadata so operators can follow auto-delegate activity without digging into logs.

Problem statement

Operators currently have no visibility into successful auto-delegate actions, so they cannot tell which work items were handed to the GitHub Copilot agent and when.

Users

- Project operators (PMs) — need confirmation that auto-delegation completed and the tooling knows which work item was handed off.
- Paired automated agents and implementers watching the delegation channel — want concise summaries of what was delegated and why.

User stories

- As a PM, I want the auto-delegate command to announce every successful handoff so I can track implementation progress.
- As an operator observing the delegation channel, I want the message to include the work item, GitHub issue link, and runner metadata so I can understand why the delegation happened without reading logs.

Success criteria

- Every time AutoDelegateRunner successfully delegates a work item, a Discord notification posts via the existing notifier so it appears in the same channel as other delegation-related alerts.
- The notification contains the work item ID, the GitHub issue URL created by `wl gh delegate` (when available), and runner metadata such as stage and priority (retries are not recorded).
- The payload notes the action taken and the destination link so operators can immediately follow up on the work item or open the issue in GitHub.
- Unit tests mock the notifier and assert that `notify` is called with the new success payload (in addition to existing failure notification coverage).

Constraints

- Reuse the existing notifier infrastructure (`ampa/notifications.notify` or injected notifier) so the message lands in the same Discord channel and message type as other scheduler alerts.
- Keep the existing success/failure semantics of AutoDelegateRunner (don’t change eligibility, retry, or back-off logic in this work).

Existing state

- `ampa/auto_delegate.py` already runs `wl next --json`, filters by stage/priority, and handles retries with a failure notification when every attempt fails.
- The scheduler populates runner metadata via `CommandSpec.metadata` and the `AutoDelegateRunner` is wired into `ampa/scheduler.py`.
- Tests in `tests/test_auto_delegate.py` cover candidate selection, delegation retries, and failure notification behavior.

Desired change

- After the existing `wl gh delegate` call succeeds, add a notifier invocation that crafts the success message with the work item ID, GitHub issue link, and runner metadata (stage, priority). Keep the ability to inject a notifier for tests.
- Update the related unit tests to verify that the notifier is invoked for successful delegations and that the payload includes the new fields.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: scope creep if the success message grows to include more runner telemetry; Mitigation: treat additional report requests as separate Worklog items instead of expanding this notification work.
- Assumption: GitHub issue link is available immediately after `wl gh delegate` succeeds without additional lookup latency.

Improve the Discord notifications emitted by the PR monitor so they contain useful status information.

Problem: When the PR monitor runs it currently posts a Discord notification but the message contains almost no useful information. Engineers cannot tell whether CI has run or passed, who opened the PR, whether the PR is ready for review, or other quick status details without navigating to the PR.

Goals/User stories:
- As an engineer I want PR monitor notifications to summarize the PR status so I can triage quickly from Discord: e.g. CI status (not run / running / passed / failed), author, title, labels, reviewer requests, draft status, mergeability, and link to the PR.
- As a reviewer I want the notification to highlight whether the PR is ready for review (not draft, no WIP labels, CI passed) so I know if I should open it.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The work creates or updates the PR monitor's Discord message payload to include at minimum: PR title, PR number, author (login), PR URL, CI status (enum: not_run, running, passed, failed), draft status, labels, requested reviewers (if any), and a short human-readable status line (e.g. "CI: passed — Ready for review")
2. The notification format is concise and readable in Discord; use embeds or rich formatting where available.
3. If CI status is unknown, the notification should indicate it clearly and include a link to CI details if available.
4. Unit and/or integration tests where feasible for the code that builds the Discord payload.
5. Update any relevant documentation or README describing the notification behaviour and configuration (webhook, tokens, etc.)

Implementation notes:
- Inspect the PR monitor code (likely where GitHub webhooks or scheduled checks run) to find the message-building logic; update it to query/check required PR & CI fields. Use GitHub checks API or statuses API to get current CI result if not already present.
- Preserve existing behaviour (still send notifications) for backwards compatibility.
- Add logging for the new fields so operators can debug message content.

Reference: reported by operator on "When the pr-monitor runs it issues a discord notification (good) but the notification has no real information in it. Improve it to provide a status description (Has the CI run? Does it pass? Who created the PR? Is it ready for review? etc.)"

# LLM-driven PR Review Action for pr-monitor

**Headline:** Automate PR review for CI-passing PRs by dispatching an LLM audit agent in a container, presenting results in Discord with one-click merge approval.

## Problem Statement

When all CI checks pass on a PR, the pr-monitor currently posts notifications but takes no further action. The operator must manually review the PR against its work item's acceptance criteria and merge it. This creates a bottleneck and delays merges, particularly when multiple PRs are ready concurrently.

## Users

- **Operators** managing the AMPA project lifecycle. They want to receive an automated audit summary in Discord so they can approve or reject merges without manually reviewing every change against the work item.

**User story:** As an operator, when a PR passes all CI checks, I want the pr-monitor to dispatch an LLM agent to audit the PR against its work item's acceptance criteria and present the results in Discord with Approve/Reject buttons, so I can merge with a single click or ignore it if I disagree.

## Success Criteria

1. When `auto_review` is enabled and a PR passes CI, the pr-monitor dispatches an LLM audit via `ContainerDispatcher` on the first eligible run, tracks the dispatch via the work item state, and does not re-dispatch on subsequent runs.
2. On subsequent runs, when an audit result is found in the work item (dated after the PR's last modification), the pr-monitor sends a Discord embed with audit summary, PR details, and Approve Merge / Reject buttons.
3. Clicking Approve Merge routes through `_route_interaction()` to `conversation_manager.resume_session()`, which triggers merge (via `gh pr merge`), work item close, and branch deletion -- all executed directly in the daemon process.
4. Clicking Reject records the decline, posts a PR comment, and closes the session without merging.
5. If no approval or rejection occurs, the pr-monitor re-sends the full audit embed with buttons on each subsequent run until the operator acts or the PR is otherwise closed.
6. When `auto_review` is not set or is false, behaviour is unchanged (backwards compatible, opt-in).
7. Audit dispatch failures are logged and recorded as work item comments but do not block the rest of the pr-monitor run.
8. If no work item ID can be extracted from a PR, the auto-review is skipped for that PR and a debug-level log is emitted (no error).

## Constraints

- **Container dependency:** The audit runs inside a distrobox container via `ContainerDispatcher`. Container pool availability limits concurrency; dispatch must handle "no container available" gracefully.
- **Asynchronous multi-run model:** The audit is dispatched on one pr-monitor run and results are collected on a subsequent run. The pr-monitor does not wait synchronously for audit completion.
- **Audit storage dependency:** Audit results will be stored as structured data within the work item itself (likely via a forthcoming extension to `wl update` or similar Worklog command). This feature is blocked on that capability being available.
- **Work item identification:** The pr-monitor must reliably extract the work item ID from the PR (branch name `wl-<id>-*`, PR body marker, or linked GitHub issue). If no work item can be identified, the auto-review should be skipped for that PR.
- **Merge executes in daemon:** The merge-and-cleanup step (Phase 4) runs directly in the daemon process via shell commands, not inside a container.
- **No approval timeout:** Approval buttons remain active indefinitely. The pr-monitor re-notifies every run until the operator acts.
- **Opt-in via metadata:** The `auto_review` metadata flag (default `false`) gates the entire feature, preserving backward compatibility.

## Blocking Dependency

This feature requires a child work item defining the minimum viable Worklog audit storage capability needed by the pr-monitor. This capability will likely be an extension to `wl update` (or a similar existing Worklog command) rather than a new `wl audit` command. The child item should specify: how the audit agent writes results into the work item, how the pr-monitor queries for audit results and their timestamps, and the minimum data schema (pass/fail per criterion, summary, concerns).

## Existing State

- `PRMonitorRunner` in `ampa/pr_monitor.py` handles CI-passing PRs by posting a GitHub comment (with `_READY_COMMENT_MARKER` dedup), a Worklog comment, and a Discord notification. No automated review or merge.
- `ContainerDispatcher` in `ampa/engine/dispatch.py` provides container pool dispatch (claim, spawn, timeout, teardown). Fully implemented.
- `discord_bot.py` handles button interactions via `process_interaction()` -> `_route_interaction()`. Non-test interactions currently hit a `# Future:` placeholder that logs but does nothing.
- `conversation_manager.py` provides `start_conversation()` (records pending prompt, sets `waiting_for_input`) and `resume_session()` (validates state, emits event, transitions to `running`). Fully implemented.
- `responder.py` provides `resume_from_payload()` mapping `accept`/`decline` actions to `conversation_manager.resume_session()`. Fully implemented.
- `scheduler_helpers.py` registers `pr-monitor` with `metadata={"dedup": True, "max_prs": 50}`. No `auto_review` field yet.

## Desired Change

### Phase 1: Audit dispatch
- Add `_dispatch_review()` to `PRMonitorRunner` that extracts the work item ID, composes a review prompt, and dispatches it via `ContainerDispatcher`.
- The audit agent uses the forthcoming Worklog audit capability to write structured audit results into the work item.
- Track dispatch state via the work item (not via PR comment markers). On subsequent runs, check the work item for audit state to avoid re-dispatching.

### Phase 2: Audit result collection and presentation
- On subsequent pr-monitor runs, check the work item for audit results dated after the PR's last modification time.
- When results are found, compose a Discord embed with audit summary, PR metadata, and Approve Merge / Reject buttons.
- Use `conversation_manager.start_conversation()` to record the pending approval as `waiting_for_input`.
- Re-send the full embed on every subsequent run until the operator acts.

### Phase 3: Interaction routing
- Extend `_route_interaction()` in `discord_bot.py` to handle `pr_review_approve_*` and `pr_review_reject_*` custom_ids.
- On approve: call `responder.resume_from_payload()` with `action=accept`, triggering merge-and-cleanup.
- On reject: call with `action=decline`, posting a PR comment and closing the session.

### Phase 4: Merge and cleanup (on approval)
- Execute directly in the daemon process: `gh pr merge`, `wl close`, branch deletion.
- Post confirmation to Discord and Worklog.

### Configuration
- Add `auto_review: false` to the pr-monitor metadata defaults in `scheduler_helpers.py`.
- Supported metadata keys: `auto_review` (bool), `auto_review_prompt_template` (optional string), `auto_review_container_timeout` (optional int).

### Files likely to change
- `ampa/pr_monitor.py` -- `_dispatch_review()`, `_handle_ready_pr()` update, work-item-ID extraction, audit-result presentation
- `ampa/scheduler_helpers.py` -- metadata defaults
- `ampa/scheduler.py` -- inject `ContainerDispatcher` into `PRMonitorRunner`
- `ampa/discord_bot.py` -- extend `_route_interaction()`
- `tests/test_pr_monitor.py`, `tests/test_discord_bot.py`, `tests/test_scheduler_run.py` -- new tests

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Scope creep:** The four-phase design touches multiple subsystems (pr-monitor, Discord bot, conversation manager, scheduler). Mitigation: record additional feature ideas and refactorings as separate work items linked to this one rather than expanding scope.
- **Container pool exhaustion:** If multiple PRs pass CI simultaneously, audit dispatches may fail due to limited pool size (3 containers). Mitigation: dispatch failure is already handled gracefully (log + comment, no block); consider a queue-based retry in a follow-up item.
- **Discord notification flooding:** Re-sending the full audit embed every pr-monitor run (default 60 min) could create noise if the operator is away. Mitigation: acceptable for now; a lighter reminder mode can be a follow-up item.
- **Audit quality variance:** LLM audit results may vary in quality or miss subtle issues. Mitigation: the human-in-the-loop approval gate ensures no merge without operator review.
- **Stale audit results:** If a PR receives new commits after the audit was dispatched but before approval, the audit results become stale. Mitigation: the pr-monitor checks that audit results are dated after the PR's last modification time; new commits invalidate old audits and trigger a new dispatch.

### Assumptions
- The Worklog audit storage capability (likely via `wl update` extension) will provide a way to write structured audit data into the work item and query it with timestamps.
- The `ContainerDispatcher` API will not change significantly before this feature is implemented.
- The `conversation_manager` and `responder` APIs are stable and sufficient for the approval flow without modification.
- The `_route_interaction()` placeholder in `discord_bot.py` can be extended without breaking existing test-button functionality.
- The operator has `gh` CLI configured with sufficient permissions to merge PRs and delete branches.

# Audit Result Storage via Work Item Comments

## Problem
The LLM-driven PR review feature (SA-0MMN9YNS41N1B77L) needs a way for the audit agent to write structured audit results into a work item and for the pr-monitor to query those results with timestamps.

## User Story
As the pr-monitor, when I dispatch an LLM audit of a PR, I need the audit agent to store its results in the work item so I can retrieve and present them on a subsequent run.

## Approach
Use structured work item comments with a known marker format as the storage mechanism. This avoids needing a new wl command or schema extension.

### Comment Format
The audit agent writes a comment with a structured JSON block:
```
<!-- ampa-pr-audit-result -->
{"audit_result": {"overall": "pass|fail|partial", "criteria": [{"name": "...", "pass": true, "notes": "..."}], "summary": "...", "concerns": ["..."], "audited_at": "ISO-8601", "pr_number": 42, "pr_sha": "abc123"}}
```

### Dispatch State Tracking
A second marker comment tracks dispatch state:
```
<!-- ampa-pr-audit-dispatch:42 -->
{"dispatch_state": {"pr_number": 42, "dispatched_at": "ISO-8601", "container_id": "...", "work_item_id": "..."}}
```

### Query Mechanism
The pr-monitor queries the work item comments via wl show --json, parses comments looking for the markers, and extracts the JSON payload. Timestamps in the payload are compared against the PR's last modification time.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Define the _AUDIT_RESULT_MARKER and _AUDIT_DISPATCH_MARKER constants in pr_monitor.py.
2. Implement _extract_work_item_id() that extracts the work item ID from a PR's branch name (pattern: feature/<id>-*, bug/<id>-*, wl-<id>-*) or PR body.
3. Implement _get_audit_dispatch_state() that queries work item comments for dispatch markers for a given PR number.
4. Implement _get_audit_result() that queries work item comments for result markers dated after a given timestamp.
5. Implement _post_audit_dispatch_marker() that posts a dispatch state comment to the work item.
6. All methods are unit tested with mock wl_shell responses.
7. Work item ID extraction handles edge cases: no work item, multiple patterns, missing branch name.

## Files to Change
- ampa/pr_monitor.py -- add markers, extraction and query methods
- tests/test_pr_monitor.py -- unit tests

# Phase 1: Audit Dispatch in PRMonitorRunner

## Problem
When auto_review is enabled and a PR passes CI, the pr-monitor needs to dispatch an LLM audit via ContainerDispatcher and track the dispatch state.

## User Story
As an operator with auto_review enabled, when a PR passes all CI checks, I want the pr-monitor to automatically dispatch an LLM agent to audit the PR against its work item acceptance criteria, so the review process begins without manual intervention.

## Approach
1. Add auto_review metadata flag support (default false).
2. In _handle_ready_pr(), after posting the ready comment, check if auto_review is enabled.
3. Extract the work item ID from the PR (using _extract_work_item_id from the storage child).
4. Check if a dispatch has already been made (using _get_audit_dispatch_state).
5. If not already dispatched, compose a review prompt and dispatch via ContainerDispatcher.
6. Post a dispatch marker comment to the work item.
7. Handle dispatch failures gracefully (log + comment, no block).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. When auto_review is enabled and a PR passes CI, _dispatch_review() is called after _handle_ready_pr().
2. _dispatch_review() extracts the work item ID, composes a review prompt referencing the PR and work item, and dispatches via ContainerDispatcher.
3. Dispatch state is tracked via a work item comment with the dispatch marker.
4. On subsequent runs, if a dispatch marker exists for the same PR number, no re-dispatch occurs.
5. If no work item ID can be extracted, auto-review is skipped with a debug log.
6. If ContainerDispatcher dispatch fails (e.g., no container available), the failure is logged and recorded as a work item comment but does not block the rest of the run.
7. When auto_review is false or absent, behaviour is unchanged.
8. PRMonitorRunner accepts an optional dispatcher parameter for ContainerDispatcher injection.
9. All new code paths are unit tested.

## Dependencies
- Depends on SA-0MMO06N4U06626G3 (audit storage markers and extraction methods)

## Files to Change
- ampa/pr_monitor.py -- add _dispatch_review(), update _handle_ready_pr(), add dispatcher param
- ampa/scheduler.py -- inject ContainerDispatcher into PRMonitorRunner
- ampa/scheduler_helpers.py -- add auto_review to metadata defaults
- tests/test_pr_monitor.py -- new dispatch tests

# Phase 2: Audit Result Collection and Discord Presentation

## Problem
After an audit is dispatched, the pr-monitor needs to check for results on subsequent runs and present them to the operator in Discord with Approve/Reject buttons.

## User Story
As an operator, after an LLM audit completes on a CI-passing PR, I want to see the audit summary in Discord with Approve Merge and Reject buttons, so I can make a merge decision with a single click.

## Approach
1. On each pr-monitor run, for CI-passing PRs with auto_review enabled:
   a. Check if a dispatch was made (dispatch marker exists).
   b. If dispatched, check for audit results dated after the PR's last modification.
   c. If results found, compose a Discord embed with audit summary, PR details, and buttons.
   d. Use conversation_manager.start_conversation() to record the pending approval.
   e. Send the embed via the notifier with Approve/Reject button components.
2. If no approval/rejection has occurred, re-send the full embed on every subsequent run.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. When audit results are found in the work item (dated after PR last modification), a Discord embed is sent with: audit summary, pass/fail per criterion, concerns, PR URL, and Approve Merge / Reject buttons.
2. Buttons use custom_ids: pr_review_approve_{pr_number} and pr_review_reject_{pr_number}.
3. conversation_manager.start_conversation() is called to record the pending approval state.
4. If the operator has not yet responded, the full embed with buttons is re-sent on each subsequent run.
5. If audit results are older than the PR's last modification (stale), they are ignored and a new dispatch is triggered.
6. All new code paths are unit tested.

## Dependencies
- Depends on SA-0MMO06N4U06626G3 (audit storage query methods)
- Depends on SA-0MMO072KH19N2N1R (Phase 1: audit dispatch)

When an operator clicks Approve Merge or Reject in Discord, the discord_bot needs to route these interactions through the conversation manager to trigger the appropriate actions.

As an operator, when I click Approve Merge on a PR review embed in Discord, I want the system to merge the PR, close the work item, and clean up the branch. When I click Reject, I want a PR comment posted explaining the decline and the session closed.

# Phase 4: Merge and Cleanup on Approval

## Problem
When an operator approves a PR review, the system needs to merge the PR, close the work item, delete the branch, and post confirmations.

## User Story
As an operator, after I approve a PR review in Discord, I want the system to automatically merge the PR, close the associated work item, delete the feature branch, and confirm the actions in Discord and Worklog.

## Approach
1. After responder.resume_from_payload() processes an accept action, the conversation manager emits a resumed_with_input event.
2. The pr-monitor (or a callback) handles this event by executing merge and cleanup:
   a. gh pr merge --merge {pr_number}
   b. wl close {work_item_id} --reason 'PR #{pr_number} merged via auto-review approval'
   c. git push origin --delete {branch_name}
3. Post confirmation to Discord and Worklog.
4. On reject: post a PR comment explaining the decline and close the conversation session.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. On approve: gh pr merge is executed in the daemon process for the correct PR number.
2. On approve: wl close is called for the associated work item with a descriptive reason.
3. On approve: the feature branch is deleted from origin.
4. On approve: a confirmation Discord notification is sent with merge details.
5. On approve: a confirmation Worklog comment is added to the work item.
6. On reject: a PR comment is posted explaining the decline.
7. On reject: a Worklog comment is added recording the rejection.
8. Merge failures (e.g., conflicts) are logged and reported to Discord, not silently swallowed.
9. All merge/cleanup operations are unit tested with mock shells.

## Dependencies
- Depends on SA-0MMO07RQW1PEPYT6 (Phase 3: interaction routing must work)

## Files to Change
- ampa/pr_monitor.py -- add _merge_pr(), _reject_pr(), _cleanup_branch()
- tests/test_pr_monitor.py -- merge and cleanup tests

Headline: Ensure 'in-progress' reports are idempotent (AMPA ingestion)

Problem statement
in-progress reports are currently not suppressed when identical reports are emitted, causing duplicate candidate selection and noisy delegation behaviour. Verify the observed non-idempotence and implement conservative deduplication at AMPA ingestion so identical reports are ignored.

Users
- Operators and on-call engineers: avoid duplicate alerts and noisy notifications when the same work-item repeatedly appears as "in-progress".
- AMPA scheduler and delegation code: receive a de-duplicated candidate stream so downstream selection and notifications are stable.
- Developers writing automation that consumes `wl next`/in-progress reports: get consistent behaviour and easier debugging.

User stories
- As an operator, when the same in-progress report is emitted multiple times, I want only one effective report so I don't get duplicate notifications.
- As the AMPA scheduler, I want to ignore duplicate reports so the delegation flow doesn't repeatedly attempt the same work item.

Success criteria
- AMPA selection/scheduler suppresses exact-duplicate in-progress reports (same content + metadata) during candidate ingestion; duplicates are not presented as separate candidates.
- Unit tests cover the dedupe behaviour for the common WL JSON shapes (list, results wrapper, single item) and pass in CI.
- A small reproducible log or test fixture demonstrates previously duplicated reports are now collapsed to a single candidate.
- No changes to WL CLI required for this fix (implementation at AMPA ingestion), and existing compatibility fallback behaviour in `ampa.selection` is preserved.


Constraints
- Do not modify Worklog (wl) unless explicitly coordinated; implement dedupe in AMPA ingestion (selection/scheduler) only.
- Solution must respect existing compatibility codepaths in `ampa.selection` that handle multiple WL JSON shapes.
- Keep runtime overhead small: dedupe checks should be O(1) per candidate (e.g., hash lookup) and bounded memory for the short-lived scheduler process.

Existing state
- Current work item: SA-0MMOLJEAS1H73NO8 — title: "in_progress result is idempotent"; description notes that in-progress reports are not idempotent and should be verified and fixed.
- Code paths of interest: `ampa/selection.py` (normalizes `wl next` payloads and selects candidates) and `ampa/scheduler.py` (scheduler that runs commands and may emit `wl-in_progress` style commands).
- `ampa.selection` already normalizes varied WL output shapes (`results`, `items`, wrappers like `workItem`) and dedupes by work-item id in some normalizations; no current content-level dedupe exists for report messages.


Desired change
- Implement an exact-report dedupe at AMPA candidate ingestion: compute a deterministic hash over the report payload (message + relevant metadata) and ignore reports whose hash already exists in the scheduler's recent candidate set.
- Add unit tests for `ampa.selection.WLNextClient`/normalization and for the dedupe behaviour using representative WL payload shapes (list, results wrapper, single top-level item). Include tests for the case where the same work item has differing messages (these should not be deduped under the exact-report rule).
- Ensure CI runs these tests and preserves existing fallback behaviour for older WL implementations.

Risks & assumptions
- Risk: Scope creep — implementing a broader work-item-level dedupe or changing candidate ordering could unintentionally alter scheduler behaviour. Mitigation: keep the change limited to exact-report hashing and add follow-up work items for broader dedupe needs.
- Risk: Memory growth if the scheduler retains too many recent hashes. Mitigation: use a sliding window / bounded-size set (e.g., LRU or time-based expiry) to limit retention.
- Risk: Hash collisions (unlikely with a modern hash like SHA256) could suppress distinct reports. Mitigation: include deterministic serialization of message+metadata and use a strong hash; add unit test to assert collisions are not produced in expected inputs.
- Assumption: The relevant metadata to include in the hash is message content, work-item id (if present), timestamp may be excluded since identical reports should match; confirm with stakeholders if timestamp must be included.

Notes
- Implementation should be conservative: do not change candidate ordering or work-item-level dedupe behaviour unless requested; if broader dedupe is desired later, create a follow-up work item.


Related work and docs
- Potentially related docs:
  - `command/intake.md` — describes the intake flow and where draft briefs are stored; useful for traceability.
  - `ampa/selection.py` — candidate normalization and `wl next` client (primary change location).
  - `ampa/scheduler.py` — scheduler orchestration; references commands like `wl-in_progress`.

- Potentially related work items:
  - SA-0ML63W2DD1NKSMXU — "Wire detection into /plan: idempotent dependency creation" (related idempotence approach and patterns).
  - SA-0ML6D6UJ21D9XTNU — "Add dependency commands to wl CLI (dep-add/dep-list/dep-remove)" (mentions idempotence expectations for CLI commands).
  - SA-0MLQ8YP2X0I2XJ0M — "Prerequisite Validation and Error Handling" (references wl in_progress use and compatibility fallbacks).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Confirmed dedupe rule: report-level exact dedupe (suppress only when entire report content+metadata matches). (User-selected)
- Confirmed fix location: AMPA scheduler/selection — dedupe on ingestion. (User-selected)
- Confirmed acceptance: unit tests + CI passing. (User-selected)

Notes
- Implementation should be conservative: do not change candidate ordering or work-item-level dedupe behaviour unless requested; if broader dedupe is desired later, create a follow-up work item.

Final summary
- AMPA will deduplicate exact-duplicate in-progress reports on ingestion using a deterministic hash (message+metadata); unit tests will validate behaviour and CI must pass.

Related work (automated report)
- SA-0ML96LPVC19CD40C — Scheduler: issue triage (automatic wl in-progress audits): implements scheduled triage/audit flows and documents differences between `in_review` vs `in-progress` selection; relevant for cooldown/selection patterns.
- SA-0ML63W2DD1NKSMXU — Wire detection into /plan: idempotent dependency creation: outlines idempotence patterns and safe creation; useful precedent for idempotence behaviour.
- ampa/selection.py — code implementing WL payload normalization; primary change location for ingestion-level dedupe.

Problem statement

Currently the AMPA installer (`skill/install-ampa`) does not verify whether the AMPA container pool is initialized after installation. New installs (or upgrades) therefore require the operator to discover and run `wl ampa warm-pool` manually, causing the first `wl ampa start-work` to suffer a slow template build/clone. The installer should detect pool readiness and ensure the pool is pre-warmed when possible.

Users

- Operators who run AMPA on a host (interactive and scripted installs). Example user story: "As an operator, after running the AMPA installer I want the pool seeded so my first `wl ampa start-work` is fast."
- CI / automation that run AMPA installs in developer environments where promptless operation is required (may prefer no automatic long-running jobs).
- Maintainers of the AMPA plugin who need predictable post-install behaviour and clear operator messaging.

Success criteria

1. After a successful install (or upgrade) the installer either ensures the AMPA pool is warmed automatically when Podman and Distrobox are available, or prints a one-line actionable message describing how to warm the pool manually.
2. The installer does not abort or fail the install if prerequisites (Podman/Distrobox) are missing; it exits successfully but marks the pool as not-ready in output and instructs the operator how to proceed.
3. Default pre-warm pool size is 3 and is configurable via `WL_AMPA_POOL_SIZE` env var or an installer `--pool-size` option; the installer respects this configuration when running warm-pool.
4. Installer output includes a short progress summary when running warm-pool and one-line actionable errors if warm-pool fails (do not treat warm-pool failure as a hard install failure).
5. README and installer help are updated to document the automatic warm-pool behaviour, the prerequisites, and how to override pool size or skip warming.

Constraints

- Installer must not attempt to install Podman or Distrobox automatically (no privileged or host-level changes). The installer will only detect presence and either run `wl ampa warm-pool` or produce instructions.
- Warm-pool can be slow on first run (image build + template creation); installer must run it non-blocking or show progress with clear messaging so users understand time cost.
- Respect global pool-state changes already present in the repo (global AMPA dir at `~/.config/opencode/.worklog/ampa/`); warm-pool must read/write the global path.

Existing state

- `wl ampa warm-pool` (alias `wp`) command exists and builds the image, creates a template, and fills the pool (see `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` and `.worklog/plugins/ampa.mjs`).
- README contains warm-pool instructions and notes about prerequisites (Podman/Distrobox) and global pool-state path (`README.md:50-70`).
- Several related work items exist for global install paths, pool-state paths, scheduler warm-pool jobs, and docs coordination (see Related work below).

Desired change

- After successful install, installer checks for `podman` and `distrobox` on PATH.
  - If both are present: automatically run `wl ampa warm-pool` (non-interactive), respecting configured pool-size; show a short progress summary and print one-line actionable errors if warm-pool fails. Warm-pool failures should not abort the installer.
  - If either is missing: print a one-line actionable message with links and the command to run manually (example: "Podman or Distrobox missing — install them and run: wl ampa warm-pool") and skip trying to warm the pool.
- Expose configuration for pool size via `WL_AMPA_POOL_SIZE` env var and an optional `--pool-size` flag for the installer; default to 3.
