Headline

Make agents work in feature branches locally, push feature branches into dev when ready, and use a semi-automated dev→main release process where CI runs tests and a human reviewer triggers the merge to main.


Problem statement

Agents currently create PRs that target main or otherwise propose merges to main. This increases risk of accidental direct main changes and makes coordination of releases harder. We need a safer flow where agents produce feature branches, push to a 'dev' integration branch, and a gated release process promotes tested changes to main.


Users

- Producers and maintainers who rely on `main` being always releasable.
- Agent developers and operators who author work via agents and need a predictable promotion flow.
- Reviewers and release managers who validate test results and approve merges to main.

Example user stories

- As an operator, I want agents to push completed feature branches into dev so I can review integrated changes before they reach main.
- As a reviewer, I want CI to run test suites on dev and provide a clear report so I can approve a safe merge to main.
- As a release manager, I want a human-reviewed merge from dev to main after CI verifies the candidate so releases are controlled.


Success criteria

1. Agents create feature branches (pattern: wl-<work-item-id>-short-desc), push them to origin, and push the branch's head into a shared dev branch (or open a PR targeting dev) as the integration step.
2. CI validates dev on every change and produces a test report (at minimum smoke + critical tests; full test-suite runs pre-merge as configured). Test commands and required checks are documented in the work item.
3. A human reviewer inspects CI results and triggers the merge from dev → main (semi-automated). The work item must include the exact review checklist and the merge trigger procedure.
4. A documented branch naming and conflict-resolution policy is present (default pattern above; on conflicts agents create a merge-conflict work item and fail the push). The policy must be adhered to by agent automation.
5. All related documentation is updated (README, agent guidance files such as agent/ship.md), and the work item lists the files changed. (Mandatory)
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (Mandatory)
7. Agents must `git pull origin dev` after switching to the `dev` branch, ensuring they always work from the HEAD of `dev`. This applies to every `git checkout dev` action in the agent workflow.


Constraints

- Agents must not push directly to main.
- Feature branches must be created per-work-item and be non-destructive by default (no force-push, no history rewriting).
- The semi-automated merge requires an explicit human approval step before dev→main merge.
- Migration or large infra changes (new cloud providers, secrets rotation) are out of scope and must be separately approved.


Existing state

- Current practice: some agents may create PRs targeting main or are not consistent about branch naming. agent/ship.md currently instructs: "Use a git branch + PR workflow; do not push directly to `main`."
- Repository artifacts referencing dev/release flows: docs/prd/PRD_Automated_PM_Agent... (release ops), command/review.md (container review lifecycle), tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs (claim/release dev containers), and several work items related to dev containers and branch workflows.


Desired change

- Standardise agent behaviour: agents work in local feature branches and push those branches to origin.
- Agents should then push the feature branch into `dev` (either by pushing a merge commit into dev or opening a PR targeting dev) as the integration step.
- CI runs validation on `dev`; once CI reports are green a human reviewer triggers merge to `main` according to the documented checklist.
- Implement branch naming rules, conflict handling policies, and update agent guidance (agent/ship.md and any relevant agent docs).


Related work

Potentially related docs (file paths)
- agent/ship.md — DevOps agent guidance and existing branch/PR policy
- command/review.md — review container lifecycle and release notes
- docs/prd/PRD_Automated_PM_Agent_-_end-to-end_project_overseer_(SA-0ML5E2A2V1YILTVR).md — release & operations guidance
- tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs — dev container claim/release tests

Potentially related work items
- SA-0MLQ904LV1D1V8ZW — Unit Tests and Manual E2E Script (mentions branch name generation)
- SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O — Podman development container for SorraAgents
- SA-0MLQ8YD0Z1C1FP07 — Containerfile for Distrobox Dev Container


Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Agent → dev workflow" — Answer (user): "D: agents work in feature branches locally and push into dev when done." — Source: interactive reply. Final: accepted.
- Q: "Release process (dev → main)" — Answer (user): "B: Semi-automated: CI runs tests and creates a release candidate; a human reviews results and triggers the merge." — Source: interactive reply. Final: accepted.
- Q: "Permissions, naming, and conflict policy" — Answer (user): "A: Allow all agents to push to dev (trusted)." — Source: interactive reply. Final: accepted.

Notes on idempotence

- This draft is intended to be idempotent. Re-running the intake will reuse SA-0MP1TP1QM009M34K and update the description rather than creating duplicates. Existing Appendix entries were appended with explicit final: accepted notes.

    ## Description
    
    Problem statement
    
    Update the audit skill so it can operate on either a Worklog (WL) work item or a GitHub PR. When a PR is provided, the agent should resolve the associated WL item from the PR title or description (or prompt / offer to create one), check out the PR branch, run the audit against that branch, and report results. If the audit passes (and the code is built and full test suite passes) the agent should present an explicit offer to merge the PR branch into main and push; if the audit fails, it should report gaps and remain on the PR branch to allow follow-up.
    
    Users
    
    - QA engineers and AMPA operators who run audits: "As a QA, I want the audit agent to verify PRs directly so I can validate implementation on the PR branch without manual checkout."
    - Developers authoring PRs: "As a developer, I want the audit to run against my PR branch and to link the results to the corresponding WL item so acceptance criteria are traceable." 
    - Release managers: "As a release manager, I want the agent to offer merging only when tests/build and the audit are green so I can maintain branch protection policies."
    
    Success criteria
    
    - The audit skill accepts either a WL id or a PR reference (GitHub PR URL or owner/repo#pr). When a PR is given, it resolves the WL id from the PR title/body or asks the user to provide/create one. (Measurable: 90% of PRs where a WL id exists in title/body are resolved automatically in tests.)
    - The agent checks out the PR branch, runs the audit against the code on that branch, and records a structured audit report on the WL item. (Measurable: wl update --audit-text is called and returns success in integration test.)
    - On audit pass AND after successful local build and full test run, the agent presents a clear, explicit offer to merge the PR into main; it does not auto-merge without confirmation. (Measurable: offer created and requires explicit confirmation in test harness.)
    - On audit fail, the agent posts the audit report to the WL work item, remains on the PR branch, and reports the remaining unmet acceptance criteria with file:line evidence. (Measurable: audit-fail flow produces audit_failed stage and tags.)
    - All new behavior is covered by unit/integration tests; full project test suite passes. (Measurable: CI run passes with new tests added.)
    - Documentation updated: README/skill docs and triage-audit docs reflect PR-flow and GitHub-only support.
    
    Constraints
    
    - Initial provider support: GitHub only (user choice). Support for other providers may be added later.
    - The agent must not auto-create merges without explicit confirmation from an authorized actor. Default behaviour: offer to merge and wait for confirmation.
    - When auto-resolving WL items from PR content fails, the agent prompts the operator and offers to create a WL item for the PR; it must not create WL items automatically without confirmation.
    - Must respect repository branch protection rules and only *offer* merges when local build and tests pass; if CI status checks are required by policy, the offer should include a note that CI checks must pass separately.
    - Implementation must be idempotent and not duplicate appendix entries in the WL work item on repeated runs.
    
    Existing state
    
    - The repository contains an existing audit skill (skill/audit/SKILL.md) and multiple docs related to audit polling and handlers (docs/triage-audit.md, docs/workflow/engine-prd.md). Current audit skill expects a WL work item and runs against the currently checked-out code base.
    - There are several completed WL items and design docs implementing descriptor-driven audit handlers and scheduler integration (see Related work).
    
    Desired change
    
    - Extend the audit skill to accept a PR reference (GitHub PR URL or owner/repo#pr).
    - Implement logic to attempt WL id resolution from PR title/body and, if unresolved, interactively prompt the operator to supply or create a WL item (with a drafted title/description pre-filled from PR).
    - When given a PR, fetch/checkout the PR branch (safely, preserving the current working tree), run build and test steps, then run the audit against that branch. Record the structured audit output back on the WL item via wl update --audit-text and an audit comment.
    - On success (audit passes and build/tests pass), present a non-destructive offer to merge the PR branch to main and push; do not auto-merge. Offer command should note preconditions (tests/build/audit pass) and branch protection caveats.
    - On failure, record gaps in the WL item and remain on the PR branch; the agent should not attempt to merge.
    
    Related work
    
    Potentially related docs:
    - skill/audit/SKILL.md — current audit skill spec and output format. (Primary reference)
    - docs/triage-audit.md — audit poller and AMPA handlers; explains structured audit markers and parser.
    - docs/workflow/engine-prd.md — workflow stages and audit-based transitions (close_with_audit, audit_result).
    - docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md — examples of audit invocation templates referencing PR-based audit usage.
    
    Potentially related work items (wl search "audit"):
    - Audit integration & lifecycle updates: call audit skill and update work items (SA-0MLWQI6DC09TF7IY) — completed; historic integration work.
    - Implement descriptor-driven audit command handlers (SA-0MLYEOF5J1CXPAJV) — completed; relevant for handler semantics.
    - Audit detection & polling flow (SA-0MLYEOG9V107HE1D) — completed; describes poller selection.
    - AMPA unidirectional delegation, audit, and lifecycle management (SA-0MLPYRLRY0ODG6YH) — completed; broader context.
    
    Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
    
    - Q: "Which git hosting providers should the PR-flow support initially?" — Answer (user): "A (GitHub only)". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
    - Q: "When the agent cannot auto-resolve a work item from the PR title/description, what should it do?" — Answer (user): "A (Prompt the user for the work-item id and offer to create a new WL work item)." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
    - Q: "On a successful audit of the PR branch, what merge behaviour is desired?" — Answer (user): "A (Do NOT auto-merge; present an explicit offer to merge). Additional constraint: assume the code is built and all tests pass before offering merge." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
    
    Notes and open questions
    
    - Open question: Which exact build/test commands should the agent run for each repository (e.g., make test, npm test, tox)? Recommendation: detect project type (node/python) and run canonical commands; confirm any repo-specific build steps if necessary.
    - Open question: Should the agent consult remote CI status (GitHub checks) before offering merge, or is a successful local build + test run sufficient? Current default behaviour: local build + tests + audit must pass; include note that CI checks may still be required by branch protection and the offer will reflect that.

Headline summary: Remove framework-specific "opencode/OpenCode" wording from agent, command, and skill materials, and replace with the neutral term "the agent framework" where safe so repository guidance is framework-neutral. Keep behavior and intent unchanged while avoiding edits that would break technical identifiers.

## Problem statement
Several repository instructions and guidance files use framework-specific naming (for example, "opencode" / "OpenCode") in places that should be framework-neutral. This creates inconsistent guidance and can reduce portability of agent instructions, commands, and skills.

## Users
- Maintainers of agent/command/skill definitions.
- Contributors implementing or following workflow commands.
- Operators who rely on framework-neutral documentation.

User stories:
- As a maintainer, I want guidance text to be framework-neutral so it remains reusable across environments.
- As an operator, I want consistent terminology so command/skill behavior is easier to understand.

## Success criteria
1. In-scope files no longer contain framework-specific "opencode/OpenCode" wording where a neutral phrasing is appropriate; replacements use "the agent framework" unless a technical identifier must remain unchanged.
2. Agent, command, and skill instructions continue to preserve original intent and workflow behavior after text updates.
3. A verification search command and results are recorded in implementation notes/comments, demonstrating removal in scope.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Scope preference from stakeholder: repo-wide replacement where safe.
- Do not change technical identifiers that would break behavior (for example package names, schema URLs, or required command literals) unless separately approved.
- Keep edits conservative and minimal; preserve author intent.
- Respect ignore boundaries (`.gitignore` and repository ignore policies).

## Existing state
- Work item Review all agents, commands and skills for mention of opencode (SA-0MP3XB9YZ0019U7C) exists with a short seed description but no measurable acceptance criteria yet.
- Repository scans show many "opencode/OpenCode" mentions across commands, skills, agents, docs, tests, examples, scripts, and configs.
- Prior work exists around naming concerns but does not define this exact cleanup scope.

## Desired change
Define a clear, implementation-ready work item for neutral terminology cleanup:
- Primary target: `agent/**`, `command/**`, `skill/**`.
- Secondary target (per stakeholder scope): broader repo updates where safe.
- Preferred replacement term: "the agent framework".
- Track exceptions explicitly when wording cannot be safely changed.

## Related work
- command/intake.md — intake process template currently contains framework-specific references and temp-path conventions.
- command/plan.md, command/doc.md — similar instruction text with framework-specific language.
- skill/author-command/SKILL.md — explicitly framework-branded command authoring guidance.
- agent/forge.md — framework-specific wording and paths in agent-authoring guidance.
- Stop bots using the name Opencode (SA-0ML8GSSHX1HKBNLI) — related naming concern, treated as related (non-blocking), not duplicate.

## Risks and assumptions
- Risk: Scope creep due to repo-wide search touching many unrelated files. Mitigation: keep this item focused on neutralization; record additional opportunities as linked follow-up work items instead of expanding this item's scope.
- Risk: Replacing text in technical identifiers could break tooling. Mitigation: preserve required identifiers and log explicit exceptions.
- Assumption: "where safe" means semantic/documentation wording updates are in scope, but required technical tokens may remain.

## Summary
Create a dedicated `ralph` skill that runs an iterative **code-generation feedback loop** for a target work item:

1. delegate implementation work,
2. run audit,
3. feed audit failures back into implementation,
4. repeat until all acceptance criteria are met,
5. offer merge only after explicit operator confirmation.

This replaces the current partial ralph behavior in the `implement` skill with a focused, auditable orchestration skill.

## User stories
- As a developer, I want ralph to drive repeated implementation + audit cycles so I can converge on working code with less manual coordination.
- As QA/AMPA, I want structured audit output and traceable loop history so I can verify readiness quickly.
- As a release manager, I want merge to remain non-automatic and explicitly confirmed to respect branch protections and approval controls.

## Scope
- Input scope: the provided work item ID and its direct children.
- Loop behavior: implement -> audit -> remediate -> re-audit.
- Exit conditions: all relevant items reach `in_review` and audit passes, max attempts reached, or operator cancels.

## Non-goals
- Automatic merge without explicit confirmation.
- Operating on grandchildren or unrelated work items.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `ralph <id>` validates input and targets only `<id>` + direct children.
2. Precondition enforced: fail fast with clear guidance if target stage is not `plan_complete`.
3. Delegated implementation runs in sub-agent context and continues until target scope is `in_review` (or cancelled / max-attempts reached).
4. Audit runs after each implementation pass, and structured audit output is recorded on the target work item (`wl update --audit-text`) with an AMPA-style comment.
5. On audit failure, the next implement pass is instructed with concrete remediation based on prior audit findings.
6. On audit + build/test success, ralph presents a non-destructive merge offer; merge executes only after explicit confirmation (e.g., `--confirm-merge`).
7. Re-running ralph is idempotent: no duplicate appendix/audit records for identical content.
8. Unit + integration coverage added for happy path, retry path, cancellation, max-attempt stop, and confirmation gating.
9. Docs updated for usage, flags, operator controls, and observability.
10. Full local test suite passes.

## Constraints
- User supplies the target work item ID.
- Use existing `implement` and `audit` skill mechanics for delegation and traceability.
- Merge must remain operator-confirmed.

## Related references
- `docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
- Related completed item: Audit skill PR-based audits (SA-0MP3VTJ4M005AO6Q)

## Clarifications captured
- Relevant scope = provided item + direct children.
- Merge behavior = explicit offer, no auto-merge.
- Audit integration = invoke the `audit` skill and record structured output.

# Intake Draft: Ralph loop auto plan if necessary (SA-0MPAV1H9W001CCHJ)

## Problem statement

When a work item reaches intake_complete the ralph orchestrator currently proceeds directly to implementation. There is no lightweight auto-planning step to compute effort and risk and decide whether the item should proceed straight to implement or run a planning activity first. This leads to either unnecessary planning overhead for small tasks or missed planning for larger, riskier work.

## Users

- Product Managers: want predictable triage so small work skips planning while larger items get a plan.
- Engineers: want clear signals about whether to implement or plan, and a short, automated estimate to reduce back-and-forth.
- Release/QA: need to know when work items have been planned vs directly implemented.

Example user stories

- As a PM, I want the orchestrator to auto-run an effort-and-risk check and only run planning when the result exceeds configured thresholds, so small tasks can move faster.
- As an engineer, I want the system to attach a quick effort/risk estimate to the work item so I can prioritise and scope my work before implementing.

## Success criteria

1. When a work item is at `intake_complete`, the ralph loop runs an effort-and-risk check automatically and records the result on the work item.
2. If effort/risk are below configured thresholds, the ralph loop proceeds directly to implementation without invoking the full /plan flow.
3. If effort or risk exceed thresholds, the ralph loop invokes `/plan <id>` and waits for plan completion before continuing to implement.
4. The computed effort (t-shirt) and risk (level and score) are stored on the work item and visible in a human-readable comment.
5. Re-running ralph is idempotent: no duplicate effort/risk comments, no duplicate plan work items created.
6. All related documentation and tests are updated to reflect the new decision path.

## Constraints

- The decision thresholds (small/medium/large; low/medium/high) must follow the effort_and_risk skill outputs (option A chosen).
- If the effort_and_risk skill fails or returns ambiguous data, default to running `/plan` (safety-first).
- If ralph runs `/plan` it will proceed to implementation automatically when the plan completes (automation allowed per choice A).
- Must preserve idempotence and avoid duplicate comments or child work items.

## Existing state

- Work item: SA-0MPAV1H9W001CCHJ (title: "Ralph loop auto plan if necessary") contains a feature description requesting an optional initial step. The item is currently set to stage=idea and in-progress (assignee Map).
- Related ralph orchestrator code and docs exist (skill/ralph, docs/ralph.md). There are existing related work items for ralph loop plumbing, audit integration, and idempotence.

## Desired change

- Add an optional pre-implementation step to the ralph loop that:
  1. Calls the `effort-and-risk` skill for the target work item.
  2. If effort/risk fall below the agreed thresholds, proceed to the normal implement→audit loop.
  3. If effort/risk meet or exceed thresholds, invoke `/plan <id>` and continue to implementation only after the plan completes.
  4. Persist the effort and risk fields on the work item and add a human-readable comment with the estimate.
  5. Ensure the flow is idempotent and logs decisions clearly.

## Related work

Potentially related docs and work items discovered by search:

- SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW — Create a ralph loop (completed)
- SA-0MPAE7H8A0098NIX — Register an agent skill for the Ralph loop (open)

- SA-0MP8MFH5C009B196 — Idempotence & Appendix handling (completed) — ensures repeated runs don't duplicate appendix entries
- Docs: docs/ralph.md — current ralph skill usage and flags

(Notes: search executed with keywords: ralph, loop, auto plan, effort-and-risk)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Failure / ambiguity handling — if effort_and_risk fails or returns ambiguous/empty data, what should ralph do?" — Answer (user): "A" (Treat as unknown → run /plan by default). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Automation scope & permissions — when ralph decides to run /plan, what should it do next?" — Answer (user): "A" (Run the /plan command automatically and when plan completes continue to implementation). Source: interactive reply.

The ralph orchestrator currently invokes the /plan command via the opencode CLI ("opencode run \"/plan {id}\"") in its auto-plan and cached-decision paths. We need to validate whether this is still outstanding and, if so, implement the change, update tests and docs, and preserve existing gating and idempotence.

- Operators who run ralph for work-item automation.

1. ralph invokes /plan via the Pi agent runtime (using the pi binary invocation used elsewhere in ralph) for both the auto-plan path and the cached-decision path, instead of invoking `opencode run "/plan <id>"`. This must be observable in runtime calls and in unit tests.

Related feature work (autoplan) exists: SA-0MPAV1H9W001CCHJ (Ralph loop auto plan if necessary) and its implementation children are marked done. # Ralph loop should be non-interactive

Ralph should run end-to-end without interactive prompts during normal execution. It should stop only when it reaches the configured maximum attempts or when the LLM cannot identify a safe way to proceed without explicit producer input.

## Problem statement
Current wording for this item is too brief to drive implementation and review: it does not define measurable acceptance criteria or what "cannot proceed" means. This intake brief defines concrete boundaries for non-interactive behavior and explicit stop conditions.

## Users
- **Operators/Producers** running ralph automation in long-running unattended sessions.
- **Engineers** relying on deterministic implement→audit loops that do not pause for ad-hoc questions.

### Example user stories
- As an operator, I want ralph runs to avoid interactive pauses so unattended runs can complete predictably.
- As a producer, I want ralph to stop with a clear reason only when policy/scope decisions require human input.
- As an engineer, I want deterministic stop conditions so loop behavior is testable and debuggable.

## Success criteria
- Ralph executes without interactive prompt/confirmation requests during default loop execution.
- Ralph exits only under defined conditions: `max_attempts` reached, explicit cancellation, or "no safe path" requiring producer input.
- When stopping for "no safe path", ralph emits a structured, actionable reason describing the missing producer decision.
- Automated tests validate non-interactive behavior and stop-condition semantics.
- Full test suite remains green after implementation.

## Constraints
- Keep scope distinct from broader ralph enhancements; this item remains separate and should not be merged into existing items.
- Preserve existing explicit merge-gating behavior (`--confirm-merge`) and do not introduce new interactive prompts.
- Respect current dependency graph for related ralph hardening work.
- Scope-creep mitigation: any additional opportunities/refactors discovered during implementation must be tracked as linked work items rather than added to this item.

## Existing state
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` already contains deterministic loop controls (`max_attempts`, cancel-file handling, and fatal command failure behavior).
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` covers cancellation, max-attempt behavior, and retry/remediation flow.
- Related in-progress dependency: **Ralph: prevent CLI from exiting when delegated wl or other commands fail (add configurable fail-open & retry) (SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7)**.
- Current work item description lacks measurable acceptance criteria and explicit semantics for "cannot proceed".

## Desired change
Refine ralph loop behavior and/or messaging so "non-interactive" is explicit and verifiable. "Cannot proceed" is defined as: **the LLM can see no safe way of proceeding without input from the producer**. Ensure loop exits in that case with a clear, auditable reason instead of implicit or ambiguous behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Ralph loop execution is non-interactive by default: no user/producer prompts are issued during normal implement→audit iterations.
2. Ralph stops only when one of the following occurs:
   - configured `max_attempts` is reached,
   - explicit cancellation signal is detected,
   - the LLM determines there is no safe path to continue without producer input.
3. For the "no safe path" condition, output includes a clear machine- and human-readable reason that identifies the producer decision needed.
4. Tests are added or updated to validate all stop conditions above, including the "no safe path" branch.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Related work
### Potentially related docs
- `docs/ralph.md` — canonical behavior/flags for ralph loop, including retry and stop behavior.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — implementation of loop control and exit conditions.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — unit coverage for loop exits and retry flow.
- `skill/ralph/tests/test_fail_open_retry.py` — targeted fail-open/retry behavior tests.

### Potentially related work items
- **Create a ralph loop (SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW)** — foundational implementation; useful baseline semantics.
- **Allow ralph to run on in_progress items (SA-0MPEN9ZJ4006G1PZ)** — recent stage-gating behavior update.
- **Ralph: prevent CLI from exiting when delegated wl or other commands fail (add configurable fail-open & retry) (SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7)** — directly related resilience behavior.
- **Add line breaks to ralph output (SA-0MPAVWCEA0080NUH)** — dependent formatting task.
- **Ralph loop should output summary of work (SA-0MPB08LUB003OJJI)** — dependent reporting task.

## Related work (automated report)
- **Create a ralph loop (SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW)** establishes the core implement→audit state machine and is the closest precedent for loop stop semantics.
- **Allow ralph to run on in_progress items (SA-0MPEN9ZJ4006G1PZ)** confirms recent precondition and flow adjustments, reducing risk of conflicting stage assumptions.
- **Ralph: prevent CLI from exiting when delegated wl or other commands fail (add configurable fail-open & retry) (SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7)** is directly related to failure behavior and should be treated as a primary technical dependency.
- **docs/ralph.md** and **skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py** are the canonical implementation + behavior references and should be updated in lockstep with any change in stop-condition semantics.

## Risks & assumptions
- **Risk:** Ambiguity around "safe to proceed" could produce inconsistent behavior.  
  **Mitigation note:** Require explicit reason output when producer input is needed.
- **Risk:** Overlap with fail-open/retry dependency may cause duplicate logic or conflicting semantics.  
  **Mitigation note:** Reuse and align with SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7 behavior where possible.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into broader orchestration redesign.  
  **Mitigation note:** Record additional ideas as linked follow-up work items instead of expanding this item.

### Assumptions
- "No safe path" decisions can be represented as explicit branch outcomes and tested.
- Existing loop controls (`max_attempts`, cancel handling) remain valid and should be preserved.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Scope/duplicate check: should Ralph loop should be non-interactive (SA-0MPAVKVD4001DWBO) remain a distinct item, or be treated as duplicate of existing work (especially Create a ralph loop (SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW) and/or Ralph: prevent CLI from exiting... (SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7))?" — Answer (**user**): "A" (keep distinct). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "For this item, what exactly counts as ‘cannot proceed’?" — Answer (**user**): "D - the LLM can see no safe way of proceeding without input from the producer." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should this item explicitly require that Ralph never prompts interactively during loop execution (other than optional --confirm-merge behavior outside default flow)?" — Answer (**user**): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

Ralph should surface the exact `pi` and `wl` commands it delegates in both normal console output and JSON output so runs are easier to audit and debug. The change should stay narrowly focused on `pi` and `wl` delegation and preserve existing loop behavior.

## Problem statement

Ralph currently logs delegated command details inconsistently, and the default operator-facing output does not always show the exact command that was executed. That makes it harder to understand what the orchestrator ran, especially when troubleshooting `pi` or `wl` failures.

## Users

- Operators running Ralph and reading its console output.
- Maintainers debugging delegation failures or reviewing logs.
- Reviewers who need traceable evidence of the exact command path taken by the loop.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I want to see the exact `pi` or `wl` command Ralph is about to run so I can understand the run without enabling extra debugging.
- As a maintainer, I want the same command visible in JSON output so automated tooling can inspect it reliably.

## Success criteria

1. When Ralph delegates a `pi` command, the exact command string is shown in normal console output before execution.
2. When Ralph delegates a `wl` command, the exact command string is shown in normal console output before execution.
3. When Ralph is run with `--json`, emitted JSON output includes the exact `pi` and `wl` command strings in a machine-readable form.
4. The change applies only to delegated `pi` and `wl` commands; other subprocess categories remain unchanged.
5. Tests cover both console and JSON output behavior for `pi` and `wl` command logging, including at least one failure-path case.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Scope is limited to delegated `pi` and `wl` commands only.
- Preserve existing orchestration behavior, retries, and command execution semantics.
- Keep output changes additive and deterministic so existing automation can continue to parse Ralph output.
- Avoid expanding this item into broader logging or observability work; capture any such ideas as separate work items.

## Existing state

- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` already logs delegated commands in debug form, but the current output is not consistently surfaced to normal console output or JSON output.
- `docs/ralph.md` documents verbose mode and structured logging, but not verbatim command output for the default operator experience.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` already exercises verbose logging and delegation behavior, so it is the natural place to extend coverage.

## Desired change

- Add a deterministic command-rendering path for delegated `pi` and `wl` invocations.
- Emit the rendered command in normal console output and in JSON mode so both human operators and automation can inspect it.
- Keep the implementation narrowly focused on `pi` and `wl` delegations and preserve the current loop flow.

## Related work

### Potentially related docs

- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — current delegation and logging implementation.
- `docs/ralph.md` — Ralph usage, verbose output, and observability docs.
- `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — operator-facing Ralph invocation notes.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — existing unit coverage for delegation and verbose output.

### Potentially related work items

- **Create a ralph loop (SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW)** — foundational orchestrator work with related logging and output semantics.
- **Ralph loop should be non-interactive (SA-0MPAVKVD4001DWBO)** — adjacent Ralph output/loop-behavior item; useful for keeping operator-facing output changes consistent.

### Related work (automated report)

- `Create a ralph loop (SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW)` established the core Ralph orchestration loop and its delegated-command logging conventions. This item is the nearest implementation precedent for changes to how Ralph surfaces execution details.
- `Ralph loop should be non-interactive (SA-0MPAVKVD4001DWBO)` is adjacent because it changes operator-facing loop behavior and output expectations. It should remain separate, but its documentation and tests are a useful reference for output clarity.
- `docs/ralph.md` and `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` are the canonical documentation and implementation references for Ralph output and delegation. They are the primary places where verbatim command rendering will need to be described and implemented.

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: printing exact delegated commands may increase output noise or expose more detail than intended.

- Risk: JSON consumers may rely on the current schema.

- Risk: scope creep into broader logging/observability refactors.

### Assumptions

- “Verbatim command executed” means the exact delegated command string as executed by Ralph, rendered consistently for both console and JSON output.

Problem:
Ralph (skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py) sometimes aborts the orchestration loop when delegated subprocess commands (notably 'wl' invocations) return a non-zero exit. This causes the entire loop to stop and can leave work items or branches in intermediate states. We should add a configurable fail-open behaviour and retry logic for delegated commands so automation is more robust.

Background:
Ralph delegates many commands (wl, opencode, git, other skill scripts). Currently failures generally raise RalphError and terminate. In many automation scenarios it is preferable to log the failure, attach audit, and continue or retry, with granular control over which commands are fatal (e.g. merge/push should remain fatal unless explicitly allowed).

Goal:
Add a work item in SorraAgents to implement configurable fail-open and retry behaviour for Ralph's delegated subprocess calls, add tests, and document the behaviour. Default behaviour should remain fail-fast unless the new flags/options are used.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add CLI flags (or config) to ralph (--fail-open, --retry N, --retry-delay S) to control behaviour when delegated commands fail.
- Allow certain command categories to be marked fatal (merge/push), others non-fatal by default.
- Add unit tests mocking runner to simulate wl/tool failures and assert ralph respects fail-open/retry settings.
- Add an integration test exercising the loop with a mocked failing wl.
- Update docs/AGENTS.md or ralph README describing behaviour and recommended usage.
- Implementation lives in skill/ralph and updates ship in a PR with tests passing.

Suggested implementation approach:
1. Add flags to build_parser and a small config section for command categories that are always fatal.
2. Modify _run_json/_run_pi to return structured error info instead of raising unconditionally; let run() decide to retry/continue based on flags.
3. Add tests under skill/ralph/tests that mock the runner to return failing CompletedProcess objects.
4. Keep default behaviour unchanged; enable fail-open only when explicitly requested.

Notes:
- This item should be implemented in SorraAgents so changes to the ralph orchestrator and any shared agent tooling are tracked together.
- If desired, the fallback behaviour can record an extensible "failed-delegation" audit field on the work item to assist triage.

Headline summary

Ralph should tolerate user-facing preamble text produced by the `audit` skill by extracting and persisting only the structured audit block beginning with `Ready to close: Yes|No`, preventing false failures during the implement→audit loop.

Problem statement

Ralph currently fails to persist audit results when the audit skill's user-facing display text includes an introductory preamble before the required structured audit header `Ready to close: Yes|No`. This causes `ralph` loops to exit with a Worklog validation error even when a structured audit exists.

Users

- Primary user: operators running the `ralph` orchestrator (developers/automation engineers). Example user story:
  - As an operator running `ralph <work-item-id>`, I want the loop to complete reliably after `/audit` so that formatting in assistant display text does not cause false failures.
- Secondary users: maintainers of the `ralph` skill and the `audit` skill who will implement and review the fix.

Success criteria

- Ralph completes the implement→audit loop without failing when `/audit` returns a display preamble before the structured audit block (preamble + valid report case).
- `wl update --audit-text` is invoked with text whose first non-empty line is `Ready to close: Yes` or `Ready to close: No` for the cases where Ralph writes audit text.
- Ralph does not overwrite or fail when the audit skill already persisted structured audit metadata (detect and skip duplicate write path).
- Automated tests are added and pass that cover: preamble + valid report, already-persisted-audit, and malformed-report (no header) paths. Tests should be added/updated in `tests/test_ralph_loop.py`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, docs/ralph.md, and skill/audit/SKILL.md if needed.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

Constraints

- Cannot change the Worklog `audit` structured format or the `Ready to close:` contract; the fix must sanitise/parse the assistant display text prior to `wl update --audit-text`.
- Prefer non-destructive behaviour: avoid overwriting a previously persisted structured audit unless the new audit is explicitly different and represents a clear revision.
- Keep changes local to `skills/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` and tests where possible; avoid wide refactors unless necessary.

Existing state

- Current implementation in `skills/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` forwards the assistant's display text from `audit` directly to `wl update --audit-text` and can fail when the text contains extra lines before `Ready to close:`.
- There are unit tests in `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` that cover several audit scenarios including `AUDIT_PASS`, `AUDIT_FAIL`, and partial results; these tests provide examples to extend.
- Documentation (docs/ralph.md and skill/audit/SKILL.md) describes the `Ready to close:` contract.

Desired change

- Add a sanitizer/parser in `ralph_loop.py` that: trims any leading content before the first line starting with `Ready to close:`, extracts the structured block, and passes only the structured block to `wl update --audit-text`.
- If no `Ready to close:` header is found, `ralph` should fail with a clear error message containing a short excerpt of the raw audit output (so the operator can triage), and a unit test should assert this failure.
- Add or update unit tests in `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` to cover preamble, already-persisted, and malformed-report cases.
- Update docs/ralph.md and skill/audit/SKILL.md (if needed) to note that ralph sanitises `audit` display text prior to persisting.

Related work

Potentially related docs:
- docs/ralph.md — explains ralph loop semantics and includes debug examples that reference `Ready to close:` and raw audit output handling.
- skill/audit/SKILL.md — specifies the strict audit output contract: the very first character of the report must be the `R` of `Ready to close:`.
- tests/test_ralph_loop.py — existing tests that exercise audit handling logic and examples to reuse or extend.

Potentially related work items:
- SA-0MP8MFH5C009B196 — Orchestrator: implement→audit loop (completed) — contains general orchestrator behavior and audit handling examples.
- SA-0MP8MF8VJ000FHGT — Idempotence & Appendix handling (completed) — related to how ralph handles repeated runs and appendix/audit deduplication.
- SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7 — Prevent CLI from exiting when delegated wl or other commands fail (open) — related to making the CLI more fail-open tolerant.
- SA-0MPAVDON7006813S — Running /plan from within ralph loop uses opencode (open) — related to planning & auto-plan interactions.
- CG-0MP3XQBL4008QK8S — referenced in original work item description (related-to). Review this item for historical context.

Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Audit output format may vary or include unexpected markup/preamble; mitigation: sanitise only by locating the first `Ready to close:` line and reject if absent, logging a short excerpt for operator triage.
- Risk: Overwriting an already-persisted audit may lose operator-provided context; mitigation: detect existing `workItem.audit` metadata and skip or append with explicit revision flow.
- Risk: Scope creep if the fix expands into reworking audit generation or the audit skill; mitigation: record any additional feature/refactor opportunities as separate linked work items rather than expanding scope of this item.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Source: Worklog `wl show SA-0MPD6WRQ5007XB5V` (description), docs/ralph.md, skill/audit/SKILL.md, tests/test_ralph_loop.py. Final: yes.

Summary

Ralph crashes reading persisted audit when workItem.audit is an object: the ralph loop assumes the persisted audit is a plain string and calls "splitlines()", causing an AttributeError when Worklog persists the audit as an object. Fix by normalizing extraction to use `audit.text` when `audit` is an object while preserving backward-compatible handling for string payloads.

Problem statement

Ralph (the implement→audit orchestration loop) crashes with an AttributeError when it attempts to parse a persisted audit stored on a work item. The code assumes the persisted audit is a string and calls splitlines(); Worklog may persist the audit as an object (e.g., {time, author, text, status}) where the human-readable audit is in the `text` property.

Users

- Operator running `ralph <work-item-id>` to progress work items through the implement→audit loop.
- Maintainers of the ralph skill who rely on robust parsing of persisted audits.

Example user stories

- As an operator running `ralph <work-item-id>`, I want Ralph to continue the loop even when the persisted audit is stored as an object so the orchestrator doesn't crash.
- As a maintainer, I want automated tests to ensure both object and string audit payloads are handled so regressions are prevented.

Success criteria

- Ralph does not crash (no AttributeError) when `workItem.audit` is an object containing a `text` field.
- Ralph correctly extracts and parses `workItem.audit.text` when `audit` is an object.
- Backward-compatible handling for string `audit` payloads is preserved (no behavioural regression when audit is stored as string).
- Automated tests cover both object and string payload shapes and assert no AttributeError is raised.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

Constraints

- Change should be localized to the ralph skill (skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py) where audit is read, minimize behavioral changes elsewhere.
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing persisted audit string payloads.
- Tests should not require external services or network access; keep them unit/integration tests runnable in CI.

Existing state

- Current code in skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py reads the persisted audit via `item = wl show <id>` and then does `audit_text = item.get("audit") or item.get("auditText") or ""` followed by `audit_text.splitlines()`. When `item.get("audit")` is an object this raises `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'splitlines'`.
- The work item already includes a suggested fix and acceptance criteria. Affected file: `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` (lines near where audit_text is read and split).

Desired change

- Normalize persisted audit extraction in Ralph before parsing:
  - If `item.get("audit")` is a dict/object: use `audit_text = item.get("audit", {}).get("text", "")`.
  - Else if it's a string: use it directly.
  - Else fallback to `item.get("auditText", "")`.
- Update parsing flow to accept both payload shapes, then call existing `parse_audit_report()` on the extracted text.
- Add automated tests exercising both shapes (object with text, and plain string) and asserting no AttributeError and correct parse result.
- Update any relevant docs or inline comments describing the persisted audit formats.

Related work (repository & work items)

Potentially related work items:
- SA-0MPD6WRQ5007XB5V — "Ralph fails when /audit output includes preamble before Ready to close header" (completed): discusses audit parsing robustness and is directly related to audit parsing logic.
- SA-0MP8MFH5C009B196 — "Idempotence & Appendix handling" (completed): discusses idempotence and appendix/audit handling for repeated runs which overlaps with persisted audit handling.
- SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW — "Create a ralph loop" (completed): parent initiative describing the ralph loop behaviour.

Potentially related docs/files:
- skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py — affected file and primary location for the fix (reference lines around audit_text extraction).
- tests/test_ralph_loop.py — contains tests around audit behaviour; add cases here to cover object vs string audit payload shapes.

Related work (automated report)

- SA-0MPD6WRQ5007XB5V: Completed issue describing parsing robustness when audit output includes preamble. Relevant because it modifies audit parsing rules and test coverage that may overlap with this fix.
- SA-0MP8MFH5C009B196: Completed issue about idempotence and appendix handling. Relevant because it documents how repeated runs should not duplicate audit/appended artifacts; the current bug can cause failures that impact idempotence.
- SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW: The original Ralph loop epic; provides context on expected loop semantics and accepted behaviors during implement→audit cycles.
- tests/test_ralph_loop.py: Existing test suite contains audit-related tests; add new cases here to assert handling of object-typed persisted audit payloads.

Risks & assumptions

Risks

- Scope creep: while improving audit parsing, additional related edge-cases may be discovered that could expand scope. Mitigation: record additional features/refactorings as separate work items and do not expand this fix's scope.
- Regression risk: changing audit extraction could unintentionally affect existing behaviour for string-shaped audits. Mitigation: add unit/integration tests covering both object and string shapes and run full test suite.
- Inconsistent audit shapes: other skills may write audit payloads in different shapes. Mitigation: implement robust fallbacks (use audit.text if present, otherwise fall back to auditText or string) and add a short note in docs for the audit skill.

Assumptions

- The audit skill (or producers of persisted audits) may store the human-readable report in `workItem.audit.text` when using object form. Source: observed persisted payload shapes in repo/tests and work item description. (agent inference)
- No database/schema migration is required; change is confined to ralph's parsing logic.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were asked during this intake. The existing work item description contained the necessary details (Suggested Fix, Acceptance Criteria, Steps to Reproduce) to prepare an intake brief. (Source: work item SA-0MPD8NXCS0091ZF4 description). Final: no questions required.

Headline: Ensure the Ralph orchestrator runs /compact whenever a child transitions to `in_review`, before processing the next child
Title: Ralph: run /compact when child transitions to in_review before processing next child
Work item: SA-0MPDAHDG4005LFFD

Problem statement

When the Ralph orchestrator processes a target work item with children, it may move individual child items into `in_review` as those children reach completion. The orchestrator should run the `/compact` compaction step each time a child transitions to `in_review` and before Ralph begins processing the next child, so that any compaction-provided context/prompt (for downstream agent runs or auditing) is applied at the correct boundary.

Users

- Primary: Agents and maintainers running the `ralph` orchestrator (automated implement→audit runs). Example user story: "As an agent running ralph, I want compaction to run when a child reaches in_review so that subsequent steps use compacted session context appropriate to the new work state."
- Secondary: Reviewers and humans reading worklog comments and run logs; they benefit from consistent compaction runs recorded in logs or comments.

Success criteria (measurable)

1. Invocation: For any child work item that transitions to `in_review` during a Ralph run, Ralph invokes a compaction step (opencode run '/compact' or equivalent) at least once before starting work on the next child. Unit tests must assert that the opencode/compaction command is invoked when a child stage changes to `in_review`.
2. Non-fatal failures: If `/compact` fails (non-zero exit, exception, or plugin error), Ralph logs a warning and continues processing the next child; tests must simulate a compaction failure and verify the loop continues.
3. Idempotence: Re-running Ralph or repeating implement passes must not produce duplicate persistent artifacts for the same child transition (for example, duplicate comments or duplicate persisted audit records). If persistent evidence is chosen, it must be deduplicated by a deterministic marker.
4. Tests & validation: Unit tests added/updated in tests/test_ralph_loop.py and integration test(s) (e.g., tests/integration/test-compaction-with-ralph.mjs) demonstrate the behavior; the full project test suite passes.
5. Docs: docs/ralph.md and docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md are updated to describe the new behavior and provide examples of expected logs and test assertions.

Constraints

- Invocation style: /compact will be invoked without an explicit work-item id so the compaction plugin derives context from the current session (user selection).
- Non-fatal behavior: failures in /compact must not abort the ralph loop; the change must be conservative and resilient (log and continue).
- Minimal invasiveness: limit edits to skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py, tests, and docs. Do not change auto-plan or audit semantics.
- Idempotence: any persistent record created must be deduplicated.
- Security: compaction output may include user-supplied content; do not persist secrets or PII. If an operator pastes sensitive content, redact it from any persistent evidence.

Existing state

- Ralph orchestrator code: skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py implements the implement→audit loop. The correct insertion point for detection is immediately after each implement invocation and before the audit invocation.
- Compaction plugin: plugins/ralph.js and docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md provide a compaction hook that can derive prompts (e.g., "implement X" -> "audit X...").
- Tests: tests/test_ralph_loop.py and tests/integration/test-compaction-with-ralph.mjs cover ralph loop and compaction plugin behavior; they will be updated.
- Work item: SA-0MPDAHDG4005LFFD (this intake) is assigned to Map and currently at stage `idea`.

Desired change

- Detect child work-item stage transitions to `in_review` during each ralph attempt: snapshot the scope (target + children) before an implement pass, then re-read child stages after implement returns. For any child where prev_stage != 'in_review' and new_stage == 'in_review', invoke the compaction step (opencode run '/compact' or equivalent) once, wait for its completion, then continue processing the next child.
- Invocation details: call the compaction via the same opencode pattern used for /plan (e.g., `opencode run "/compact"`) or an equivalent `pi` invocation that triggers the compaction plugin. Since the chosen mode is "no explicit id", do not pass an id argument to /compact; let the plugin derive context.
- Error handling: if the compaction command fails, log a warning (logger.warning) with details and continue (do not abort). Count the occurrence in logs for observability.
- Idempotence: ensure the compaction invocation for a given child transition is recorded in an idempotent way if persistent evidence is chosen (deterministic marker/hash) to avoid duplicate entries on re-runs.
- Tests & docs: add unit tests in tests/test_ralph_loop.py that mock the runner to observe opencode calls and simulate compaction failures; update integration test(s) to cover compaction invocation. Update docs/ralph.md and docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md with the new semantics.

Related work

Potentially related work items (title — id — one-line summary):
- "Ralph loop outputs should include verbatu command executed" — SA-0MPAZETJY007LNGQ (open) — Ensure ralph logs the verbatim commands it delegates.
- "Running /plan from within ralph loop uses opencode" — SA-0MPAVDON7006813S (critical) — Precedent for invoking opencode run within ralph for /plan.
- "Orchestrator: implement→audit loop" — SA-0MP8MF8VJ000FHGT (completed) — Acceptance criteria and earlier decisions for orchestration behavior.
- "Idempotence & Appendix handling" — SA-0MP8MFH5C009B196 (completed) — Guidelines and tests for avoiding duplicate artifacts when re-running ralph.
- "Ralph: run /compact when child transitions to in_review before processing next child" — SA-0MPDAHDG4005LFFD (this item).

Potentially related docs / files:
- docs/ralph.md — ralph orchestrator lifecycle and logging
- docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md — compaction plugin behavior and default overrides
- skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py — orchestrator implementation (change will be applied here)
- plugins/ralph.js — compaction plugin used by /compact
- tests/test_ralph_loop.py and tests/integration/test-compaction-with-ralph.mjs — tests to update

Find-related (wl search) summary:
- SA-0MKSTQR3H1HLD7HC — "Risk and Effort Estimator Skill" (completed) referenced the term 'compact' in its output generation; not functionally related but surfaced by text search.
- SA-0MMRKK51Y17XTWH6 — "effort_and_risk: allow updates for intake_complete items" (completed) — mentions compact in description; check for overlap with estimate gating behavior.
- SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW — "Create a ralph loop" (completed) — foundational work for the orchestrator; relevant background.
- SA-0MP3VTJ4M005AO6Q — "Audit skill: support PR-based audits and resolve WL item from PR" (completed) — may include cross-references to compaction-based audit flows.
- SA-0MP8MFJTL001FGI3 — "Tests & CI: unit + integration harness" (completed) — contains references to compaction plugin tests and existing harness patterns.

Risks & mitigations

- Compaction changes agent prompts: The compaction output may affect subsequent implement/audit runs and cause unexpected behavior. Mitigation: add unit and integration tests that assert stable semantics and make compaction failures non-fatal; keep compaction invocation conservative and documented.
- Duplicate persistent artifacts on re-run: If evidence (comments/audit text) is persisted, re-running ralph may create duplicates. Mitigation: use a deterministic marker/hash when adding any persistent evidence and verify deduplication in tests.
- Scope creep: Expanding when/which items are compacted could broaden the scope and increase risk. Mitigation: record opportunities for additional compaction behaviors as separate work items and avoid expanding scope in this change.
- Sensitive content leakage: Compaction output may contain user-provided text that could include secrets/PII. Mitigation: redact or truncate compaction output in any persistent comment and add a note in docs to avoid persisting secrets.

Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which work item identifier should be passed to `/compact` when invoked?" — Answer (user): "C" (No explicit id; invoke `/compact` so the compaction plugin derives context from the current session). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "When `/compact` fails or returns an error, how should Ralph behave?" — Answer (user): "A" (Non-fatal: log comment and continue processing next child). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "When `/compact` runs for a child that just moved to in_review, should Ralph persist evidence to the work item? (A) Add a worklog comment on the child with deterministic marker + truncated compact output; (B) Add a single summary comment on the target listing child compaction events; (C) Do not add comments (log only)." — Answer: OPEN QUESTION (not answered during this intake). Rationale: persistent evidence & storage method affects idempotence and the acceptance criteria; choose before implementation. Suggested default: (A) Add deduplicated comment on the child with a deterministic marker (idempotent) and truncated compaction output.

Research & evidence used

- Worklog search: `wl search ralph --json` (matches listed related work items). Evidence: related work items listed above.
- Code inspection: skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py contains the implement→audit flow and is the appropriate insertion point (immediately after the implement call and before audit). plugins/ralph.js provides compaction hook semantics.

Open questions

1. "Should Ralph persist evidence of /compact runs and if so where (child comment / target comment / logs only)?" — OPEN QUESTION (see Appendix entry above). This influences acceptance criteria about persistent artifacts and deduplication.

# Require Markdown formatting for Worklog work item descriptions and comments

## Problem statement
Worklog (wl) work-item descriptions and comments are authored inconsistently across the repository. This makes automated parsing, human review, and cross-skill consumption error-prone. We need a single authoritative requirement: all new work-item descriptions and comments created by humans or agents must be Markdown-formatted.

## Users
- Producers / maintainers: want consistent, machine-parseable work-items and comments for review and automation.
- Agent authors (skills/commands): need clear formatting rules so generated descriptions are readable and validated.
- Implementers and reviewers: rely on consistent acceptance criteria and doc links that render correctly in UIs.

Example user stories
- As a Producer, I want work-item descriptions to be Markdown so I can copy sections into PR bodies and docs without reformatting.
- As an agent author, I want the skills that generate work-item content to produce Markdown so downstream tools (audit, plan, implement) can reliably parse sections like `## Acceptance Criteria`.

## Success criteria
1. All newly-generated work-item descriptions and work-item comments (from agents or commands) follow Markdown formatting conventions and include structured headings where applicable (e.g., `## Acceptance Criteria`).
2. Relevant agent definitions, commands, and skills that produce or update work-item content (starting with the items listed below) are updated so their outputs are Markdown-formatted and include the required sections where appropriate.
3. The three highest-priority open work items at the time of intake (listed below) are updated or annotated to reflect this policy (their descriptions/comments are converted to Markdown where practical, or a comment is added documenting how/when conversion will occur).
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the new requirement, including AGENTS.md, command/ and skill/ docs, and any authoring templates (for example `skill/author-command/assets/command-template.md`).
5. Testing & validation: add or update at least one automated check (lint/test) that verifies Markdown-formatted `## Acceptance Criteria` section presence for new or updated agent-generated work-item descriptions. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- This change must not alter the semantic meaning of existing work-item content; formatting-only edits are preferred when making retroactive updates.
- Retroactive updates are limited for this intake to the three highest-priority open work items at the time of intake (see list below). Broader retroactive migration is out-of-scope and should be planned as a separate follow-up if desired.
- Avoid invasive changes to closed/archived work items; only update open/in-progress items as allowed by owners.
- Validation tooling changes should be conservative: prefer adding lint warnings before making them blocking CI failures.

## Existing state
- AGENTS.md already mentions Markdown in places but uses permissive language ("use markdown formatting as needed"); repository guidance is not uniform and several skills/commands assume Markdown but do not enforce it.
- Multiple skills and command docs reference or emit Markdown-like sections (for example skill/audit expects `# Summary`); however outputs from some agent definitions or command templates may not consistently include the expected headings.

## Desired change
- Update AGENTS.md and relevant command/skill docs to state explicitly: "All work-item descriptions and comments (human- or agent-authored) MUST be written in Markdown."
- Update the implementation of skills/commands that emit work-item content so their outputs are Markdown-formatted by default (starting with the intake/authoring paths and audit/implement/reporting skills).
- Retroactively update or annotate the three highest-priority open work items identified below so they conform to the new formatting requirement or document planned conversion steps.

## Related work
Potentially related docs
- AGENTS.md — repository agent guidance (contains Markdown guidance currently, needs tightening)
- command/intake.md — intake command spec and templates (must be updated to mandate Markdown in generated descriptions)
- skill/audit/SKILL.md — audit skill expects Markdown output; update to confirm exact heading conventions
- skill/implement/SKILL.md — implement skill guidance referencing Markdown usage in PR/work-item content
- skill/author-command/assets/command-template.md — command template and frontmatter guidance to ensure generated content is in Markdown

Potentially related work items
- SA-0MNXA69Z9001T7NM — "Automated validation/lint for agent .md files" (high priority): related validation work and precedent for adding linting/CI integration.
- SA-0MNXA68DL007PY76 — "Add automated validation guidance for agent files" (open): adjacent validation guidance that can be extended to cover Markdown checks.
- SA-0MNXA682B0094227 — "Standardise front-matter and add explicit rationale" (open): related agent front-matter normalization work that should reflect Markdown policy.

Related work (automated report)
- The repository contains multiple existing work items and docs that reference Markdown conventions (examples: skill/audit, command/intake, docs/prd). These are useful targets for aligning wording and templates.

## Retroactive update targets (three highest-priority open work items)
Per your instruction to update the three highest-priority work items, the following open items were selected (highest priority at the time of intake):

- SA-0MNXA61NW0006KZV — "Remove risky autonomy directive ('Never ask for confirmation')" — update: add a Markdown-formatted rationale section in the work item and/or add a comment linking to this epic.
- SA-0MNXA69Z9001T7NM — "Automated validation/lint for agent .md files" — update: ensure the work item description and any guidance examples are Markdown formatted and add a task to include Markdown checks in the validator.
- SA-0MO4Q58JG009RFKT — "Integrate validator into CI and add regression tests" — update: convert description to Markdown and add acceptance criteria entries in Markdown for CI integration tests.

(Implementation note: for each target we will add an idempotent wl comment referencing this epic and describing the requested update; where appropriate we will also propose a small follow-up child task for larger migrations.)

## Risks & assumptions
- Risk: scope creep — retroactively converting many work items could balloon the effort and distract from priority work. Mitigation: limit retroactive conversion to the three highest-priority open items and record other items as follow-ups.
- Risk: automated Markdown checks may surface many failures initially. Mitigation: introduce checks as warnings first and convert to blocking only after exceptions are resolved.

# Implement audit skill persistence (skill/audit)

User story

As a Producer I want the audit skill to persist structured audit reports to Worklog so orchestrators (for example `ralph`) can read workItem.audit and proceed without error.

Acceptance criteria

1. The audit skill persists the structured audit report to the work item using the CLI: `wl update <work-item-id> --audit-text "<report>" --json`.
2. The first non-empty line of the persisted audit must be `Ready to close: Yes` or `Ready to close: No`.
3. The audit skill provides a CLI/script wrapper under `skill/audit/scripts/` that accepts an issue id and/or reads the audit report from stdin and invokes `wl update` to persist the audit.
4. Unit and integration tests are added to validate the behavior (mocking wl) and a session test demonstrates ralph reading the persisted audit.
5. SKILL.md is updated to document the implementation and usage.

Implementation notes

- Add `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` (or similar) which:
  - Accepts `--issue-id` or reads `--stdin` for the audit report.
  - Calls `wl update <id> --audit-text "<report>" --json` (handle quoting/newlines safely).
  - Returns non-zero on failure.
- Add tests `tests/test_audit_skill.py` that mock the WL CLI and verify persistence, including object vs string audit shapes.
- Update `skill/audit/SKILL.md` to reference the script and document the required first-line header.

# Update ralph skill to use optimal models per step (intake/planning/implementation/audit)

Work item: SA-0MPDVN9H6000HGMY

Summary: Add per-step model selection to the ralph orchestrator and a `model_source` toggle (remote|local, default: remote). Provide per-step config keys and CLI flags so operators can choose remote or local models explicitly; preserve existing behaviour when no per-step config is provided.

## Problem statement
Ralph currently uses a single model default (and an optional global override) for all pi invocations. This limits quality and cost optimizations possible by selecting different models for intake, planning, implementation, and audit phases. We need a deterministic, configurable way for ralph to select the optimal model per step and a simple toggle to prefer either remote or local models (default: remote).

## Users
- Producers/operators who run ralph to orchestrate implement→audit loops.
- Skill maintainers and developers who modify ralph and need predictable model selection.
- Infrastructure/ops engineers who manage local model runtimes and may want to run ralph against local models for offline or private deployments.

Example user stories
- As an operator, I want ralph to use a cheaper smaller model for intake prompts and a stronger model for planning, so runs are faster and lower-cost while preserving quality where it's needed.
- As a maintainer, I want per-step model configuration and CLI flags so I can test local model behavior without editing code.

## Success criteria (measurable)
1. Configuration and CLI
   - ralph accepts per-step model configuration keys in .ralph.json (or ralph.config.json): `model.intake`, `model.planning`, `model.implementation`, `model.audit`.
   - ralph exposes CLI flags to override these: `--model-intake`, `--model-planning`, `--model-implementation`, `--model-audit`.
   - ralph exposes a model source toggle via config and CLI: `model_source` in config and `--model-source <remote|local>` flag. Default must be `remote`. When `model_source` is `remote`, ralph uses the configured remote model ids; when `local`, the configured local model ids are used. No implicit fallback between remote/local will be attempted by ralph.

2. Canonical per-step mapping implemented (default values applied when per-step config is absent):
   - intake: remote `Claude Opus 4.7`; local `Llama-3.1 70B (Q4_K_M)`
   - planning: remote `GPT 5.5`; local `Qwen 3.x 32B`
   - implementation: remote `Qwen 3.6 Plus`; local `Qwen 32B`
   - audit: remote `Claude Opus 4.7`; local `Llama-3.1 70B (Q4_K_M)`
   (Defaults are used only when no per-step config or CLI override is provided.)

3. Backwards compatibility and precedence
   - Existing behaviour remains unchanged if no new per-step config or CLI flags are provided (i.e., ralph still resolves a single `model` key or DEFAULT_MODEL). CLI flags override config values, per-step config overrides single `model` where specified.

4. Tests and validation
   - Unit tests added covering model-resolution logic, precedence (CLI → per-step config → existing model → DEFAULT_MODEL), and `model_source` behaviour (remote vs local). Tests must assert model strings passed to pi (via mocking) for each ralph phase.
   - An integration-style test or unit-level test verifies that running ralph in `--quiet` or `--json` mode with sample work item triggers pi invocations with the expected `--model` arguments for at least intake and audit phases.

5. Documentation
   - docs/ralph.md and skill/ralph/SKILL.md updated with examples of `.ralph.json`, CLI flags, default values and migration notes.
   - A short example config file added to repository root or docs snippet showing both remote and local configurations.

6. Delivery
   - All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
   - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- No implicit remote↔local fallback. The operator must choose `remote` or `local` via config or CLI; ralph will not attempt a fallback automatically.
- Backwards-compatibility: if no per-step config/flags are supplied, ralph's behaviour must remain unchanged.
- Keep changes limited to ralph skill (scripts and docs). Do not change external pi or wl behaviour; ralph must continue to delegate to `pi` and pass the resolved model id.
- Implementation must be idempotent and not create duplicated autoplan/audit comments.

## Existing state
- Current code: skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py uses a single resolved model (DEFAULT_MODEL or .ralph.json `model` key) and sets `self.model` once in loop initialization.
- docs/ralph.md documents DEFAULT_MODEL and single-model flags. Existing tests exercise model resolution and autoplan behaviour (see tests/test_ralph_loop.py).
- No per-step model configuration exists today.

## Desired change
- Add per-step model resolution in ralph: replace single `self.model` usage with a per-phase resolver that returns the model id to pass to `pi` for that invocation.
- Add config keys in .ralph.json and CLI flags to set per-step model ids and a global `model_source` toggle (`remote` | `local`, default `remote`) that selects which configured id to use.
- Ensure CLI flags override config, and existing `model` and `--model` behavior remain supported for compatibility.
- Add unit and lightweight integration tests, and update docs as described in success criteria.

## Related work
- docs/ralph.md — main ralph docs: describes auto-plan, config files, and default model usage.
- skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py — orchestrator implementation; will be modified to add per-step model resolution.
- SA-0MO4Q4ZIU00762WY — Define canonical model mapping and documentation (intake_complete): repository-level canonical model mapping work; relevant for model id naming and docs.
- SA-0MNXA6391009R8FS — Propose standardising model field: related work on model front-matter standardization.
- skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md and skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/run_skill.py — relevant because ralph's auto-plan uses the effort-and-risk skill.
- tests/test_ralph_loop.py — existing ralph tests; update or extend to assert per-step model selection and precedence behaviour.

### Related work (automated report)
- SA-0MO4Q4ZIU00762WY (Define canonical model mapping and documentation): task that defines canonical defaults for agent models and mapping rules; use its documented canonical ids as authoritative when available.

- Test/coverage gaps: missing tests for all code paths may let regressions slip through.

- Explicitly record any repo-wide model normalization tasks as follow-up work items instead of expanding this item.
- Keep default behaviour as `remote` and document `model_source` clearly in docs to reduce operator confusion.
- Add unit tests for all model-resolution code paths and add a short integration test that validates the CLI/config precedence in a mocked environment.

### Assumptions

Answering party: user (interactive). Final: No implicit fallback; operator chooses via config/CLI; default remote.
