# Intake draft: ralph — skip redundant start-of-iteration audit when persisted audit is up-to-date

Summary: Prevent Ralph from performing a redundant start-of-iteration audit when the most recent `# AMPA Audit Result` comment already reflects the current state of the target and all recursive descendants. This reduces duplicate audits and unnecessary LLM/audit invocations when no scoped items have changed.

## Problem statement

Ralph currently runs an AMPA audit in situations that can produce duplicate work: when the target work item is already in_review Ralph may run an audit at the start of the iteration and then always runs the audit again at the end of each attempt. This results in redundant audits when nothing in the work-item scope has changed since the last persisted audit.

## Users

- Operators and Producers who run or monitor Ralph orchestrations and expect audits to reflect the current state of code and work items.
- QA/Compliance roles that rely on a single authoritative audit record per implementation pass.
- Developers and automation authors who rely on Ralph to avoid unnecessary LLM/audit invocations and to reduce cost and noise.

Example user stories

- As an operator, I want Ralph to avoid re-running an audit when no scoped work items have changed since the last audit, so the audit trail remains concise and system load is reduced.
- As a QA engineer, I want each audit comment to represent an audit of the current code and WL state so I can trust the most recent audit without filtering duplicate reports.

## Success criteria

1. Ralph skips the "start-of-iteration" audit when the most recent AMPA audit comment (a comment whose first non-empty line starts with `# AMPA Audit Result`) has a timestamp that is equal to or later than the most-recent `updatedAt` across the full scope (target work item + all recursive descendants). Measured by unit tests and an integration test that assert no `/skill:audit` call is made in this case.
2. Ralph runs the start-of-iteration audit when either (a) no `# AMPA Audit Result` comment exists, or (b) the latest audit comment timestamp is older than the most-recent `updatedAt` among scope items. Measured by tests that assert `/skill:audit` is invoked when these conditions hold.
3. Unit tests and one integration test cover both skip and run cases, including recursive-child updates causing a new audit. Tests must reliably mock or stub `wl` calls and pi invocations and assert the expected number of audit invocations.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the new behavior, including comments in `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py`, a short note in the ralph SKILL.md, and an entry in docs/workflow/examples documenting the skip behavior. (Measurable: docs files updated in the same branch.)
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The check for an existing audit must use the most recent Worklog comment whose first non-empty line starts with the exact header `# AMPA Audit Result` (case-sensitive match). The timestamp used is the comment's created/posted timestamp returned by `wl comment list` or similar API.
- Scope is defined as the target work item and all recursive descendants (child, grandchild, ...). Implementation must be efficient for deep trees and avoid excessive WL queries (prefer batching where possible).
- If no matching audit comment exists, the code must treat the persisted-audit timestamp as "missing/older" and run the audit (fail-open behaviour).
- Changes must be idempotent: re-running /intake or running Ralph multiple times must not create duplicate decision comments or duplicate audit markers.

## Existing state

- Implementation: `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` currently:
  - Determines scope with `_scope_ids(target)` which returns the target and immediate children only.
  - When target.stage == "in_review" Ralph currently skips an implement pass and runs an audit immediately (`/skill:audit <target>`), then reads the persisted audit from the work item (`workItem.audit` / `workItem.auditText`) and parses it.
  - Audit persistence helper: `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` writes the structured audit via `wl update <id> --audit-text` and agents may also add human-readable comments on the work item.
  - The audit skill produces structured text starting with `Ready to close:` which Ralph parses with `parse_audit_report`.

- Tests: Some ralph-related tests and ralph plugin tests exist under `tests/` but there are no current tests that assert skipping a start-of-iteration audit based on comment timestamps.

## Desired change

Implement a conservative pre-audit check in Ralph that prevents the start-of-iteration audit when it would be redundant. The implementation outline:

1. Add a helper to collect the full scope recursively (target + all descendants). Replace or extend `_scope_ids()` with `_scope_ids_recursive()` and use efficient wl queries to fetch children's ids.
2. Implement `_latest_audit_comment_ts(work_item_id)` which retrieves comments for the work item (`wl comment list <id> --json` or relevant API), filters comments whose first non-empty line starts with `# AMPA Audit Result`, and returns the most recent comment createdAt timestamp (ISO-8601) or None if no such comment exists.
3. Implement `_max_updated_at_for_scope(scope_ids)` which queries each work item (or a batched `wl show` if possible) to determine the most recent updatedAt across the scope.
4. In `RalphLoop.run()` where the code currently does the "skip_implement and audit first" logic for `in_review` targets, consult the two helpers above: run start-of-iteration audit only if latest_audit_comment_ts is None OR latest_audit_comment_ts < max_updated_at_for_scope. Otherwise, skip the start-of-iteration audit and proceed with the loop (i.e., do not invoke `/skill:audit` at the start).
5. Add unit tests for the helpers and integration tests for the end-to-end loop behaviour verifying the skip and run cases. Mock or stub `wl` and `pi` invocations in tests to assert audit invocation counts.

## Related work

- skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py — Ralph loop implementation; source of change.
- skill/audit/SKILL.md — Audit contract and structured report requirements.
- skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py — Persisting audits into the work item via `wl update --audit-text`.
- docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md — Audit flow examples and cooldown guidance useful for tests and examples.

### Related work (automated report)

> Auto-generated related-work report (seeded by title/description keywords: ralph, audit, audit result)

- SA-0MND1X0SJ0045JHV — "Audit skill needs automation": Open parent/related item; contains planning and tests for audit persistence. Relevant because changes to how Ralph reads audit persistence should be compatible with the automated audit runner.
- SA-0MP3Y2UF4005O0OW — "Create a ralph loop" (completed): Historical item that implemented the initial Ralph loop; reference for expected loop semantics.
- Files: skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py, skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py, skill/audit/SKILL.md, docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md — code and docs to review for compatibility.

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: audit comment header mismatch or inconsistent formatting (e.g., different header text). Mitigation: require exact header `# AMPA Audit Result`, add unit tests for parsing, and fall back to running the audit when ambiguity exists.
- Risk: timestamp format or timezone differences leading to incorrect comparisons. Mitigation: normalize parsed timestamps to UTC/ISO-8601 when comparing and add tests that simulate clock skew scenarios.
- Risk: performance impact for very deep or large recursive scopes. Mitigation: implement batched `wl show` calls, cache lookups where practical, and add a limit/timeout in the helper with a clear failure mode recorded as a follow-up work item if needed.
- Risk: race conditions — an item may be modified after the timestamp check but before the decision to skip the audit. Mitigation: this change is conservative (it only skips the *start-of-iteration* audit); Ralph will still run the audit at the end of each attempt, preserving safety. Document this behaviour in code comments.
- Risk: scope creep — additional features (e.g., including related/blocked items in scope, richer audit markers) may be proposed during implementation. Mitigation: record discovered enhancements as separate linked work items (use `discovered-from:<this-id>`), do not expand the scope of this item.

Assumptions

- Worklog comments expose a reliable `createdAt` timestamp accessible via the CLI (e.g., `wl comment list` returns created timestamps) that can be used for comparison.
- The authoritative audit marker is a visible comment starting with `# AMPA Audit Result`; the audit skill/persist path will continue to produce either the auditText field or a separate comment as part of its process.
- Recursive scope discovery is feasible via repeated `wl show --children` calls or a batched approach; implementers will choose an efficient query pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "How should Ralph determine the 'date/time of the audit' when deciding to skip the start-of-iteration audit?" — Answer (user): "D - the date on the most recent comment with the header \"# AMPA Audit Result\"". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes. Rationale: using a human/agent-visible comment avoids relying on implicit fields and makes the authoritative audit record explicit.

- Q: "What should 'scope' include when comparing modification times?" — Answer (user): "B" (Target + all recursive descendants). Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

(If any of the above answers need to be revised, please reply with the updated choice; an OPEN QUESTION will be recorded if not clarified.)

# Allow ralph to run on in_progress items

## Problem statement

Ralph currently enforces a stage precondition and exits with an error when invoked against a work item whose stage is `in_progress`. We need to allow the ralph orchestrator to be invoked on `in_progress` items so it can resume or continue the implement→audit loop for items that have already progressed through intake (and possibly planning).

## Users

- Producers and engineers who want to re-run or continue the ralph orchestrator on work items actively being implemented (status `in_progress`).

Example user stories:
- As an engineer, I want to run `ralph <id>` against an item in `in_progress` so I can resume the implement→audit loop after a manual interruption.
- As a release engineer, I want to re-run ralph on an in-progress item to verify remediation after fixes have been applied.

## Success criteria (measurable)

1. Code change: ralph accepts `in_progress` as a valid entrypoint stage (no precondition error raised) and proceeds with a deterministic run. (Verify: calling RalphLoop.run("<id>") for an item with stage `in_progress` does not raise RalphError.)
2. Behavior: For `in_progress` items, ralph behaves like an item at `plan_complete` (full implement→audit loop). (Verify: unit tests exercise a representative in_progress item and observe implement→audit cycle as appropriate.)
3. Tests: Unit tests updated (tests/test_ralph_loop.py) to reflect the new allowed stage and include at least one test that asserts successful run for `in_progress` targets. (Verify: updated test suite includes new/modified tests.)
4. Docs: skill/ralph/SKILL.md and docs/ralph.md updated to list `in_progress` among allowed precondition stages and to describe expected behavior for in_progress. (Verify: documentation files contain the updated precondition text and examples.)
5. Validation: Full project test suite passes after the change. (Verify: run `pytest -q` and ensure no regressions.)
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Preserve existing auto-plan semantics: auto-plan currently only runs for `intake_complete` items. An `in_progress` item is assumed to have already passed intake (and possibly planning); the change must not cause automatic re-invocation of the auto-plan step unless effort/risk fields are explicitly absent and the team requests otherwise.
- Minimise behavioral surface change: keep the loop semantics for `plan_complete` and `in_review` unchanged.
- Maintain idempotence: re-running ralph should not create duplicate comments or overwrite persisted audit content.
- Update only the minimum required code and tests to add `in_progress` acceptance and document the change.

## Existing state

- Current enforcement (skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py): the precondition check allows only `plan_complete`, `in_review`, or `intake_complete` and raises RalphError otherwise. (See `_assert_precondition`.)
- Tests: tests/test_ralph_loop.py includes a test `test_precondition_requires_plan_complete_or_in_review` that currently asserts a RalphError when target stage is `in_progress`.
- Docs: docs/ralph.md and skill/ralph/SKILL.md list preconditions but do not mention `in_progress` as an allowed entrypoint.
- Worklog: a parent work item exists: "Harden Ralph Loop" (SA-0MPDX3U1V006293J) and this intake will be created as a child (SA-0MPEN9ZJ4006G1PZ).

## Desired change

- Modify the ralph precondition to accept `in_progress` as a valid stage. Concretely: add `"in_progress"` to the allowed set in `_assert_precondition` in `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` and update the error message to list the allowed stages.
- Update unit tests (tests/test_ralph_loop.py): replace the expectation of a RalphError for `in_progress` with an appropriate test asserting successful invocation or expected run behavior. Add a targeted unit test asserting that ralph proceeds as for `plan_complete` when started on `in_progress`.
- Update docs (skill/ralph/SKILL.md and docs/ralph.md) to include `in_progress` in the "Preconditions" and provide a short note describing the assumed semantics (item has been through intake; auto-plan is not run by default).
- Run full test suite and fix any incidental failures caused by the change.

## Related work

Potentially related docs (file paths):
- skill/ralph/SKILL.md — ralph skill usage and auto-plan notes
- docs/ralph.md — orchestration loop design and precondition text
- skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py — implementation (precondition enforcement)
- tests/test_ralph_loop.py — unit tests that will need updates
- docs/ralph-compaction-plugin.md, plugins/ralph.js — ancillary ralph-related docs/tests

Potentially related work items (single-line):
- Harden Ralph Loop (SA-0MPDX3U1V006293J) — parent; this change will be a child.
- Ralph: run /compact when child transitions to in_review before processing next child (SA-0MPDAHDG4005LFFD)
- Update ralph skill to use optimal models per step (SA-0MPDVN9H6000HGMY)
- Ralph loop auto plan if necessary (SA-0MPAV1H9W001CCHJ)


### Related work (automated report)

- SA-0MPDX3U1V006293J — Harden Ralph Loop: Epic grouping and tracking of ralph hardening work; appropriate parent for this change and relevant for tests/docs coordination.
- SA-0MPDAHDG4005LFFD — Ralph: run /compact when child transitions to in_review: Adds an orchestration hook for compaction when children move to `in_review`; useful for deciding insertion points and additional tests.
- SA-0MPDVN9H6000HGMY — Update ralph skill to use optimal models per step: Related configuration/testing concern (model selection) but orthogonal to the stage precondition change.
- SA-0MPAV1H9W001CCHJ — Ralph loop auto plan if necessary: Documents and tests auto-plan behaviour for `intake_complete` items; reference for preserving autoplan semantics and idempotence.

(Report generated conservatively from `wl search ralph` and repository inspection. Only strongly-related items were included.)


## Risks & assumptions

- Risks:
  - Code/tests regressions: changing the stage precondition may cause unit tests or integration tests to fail. Mitigation: update tests and run full test suite; keep the change minimal and isolated.
  - Unexpected runtime behaviour on active items: resuming ralph on items that are mid-implementation could surface race conditions or partially-applied changes. Mitigation: do not change loop semantics; do not auto-run planning; log clearly and fail fast on unexpected states.
  - Operator confusion: operators may expect ralph to reject in_progress items. Mitigation: update docs and include a short note in the skill README and docs/ralph.md describing the new allowed stage and expected semantics.

- Assumptions:
  - An item in `in_progress` has already completed `intake_complete` and any required auto-plan step (if applicable). Source: seed intent / stakeholder note.
  - The desired change is limited to allowing invocation on `in_progress` and does not introduce new auto-plan semantics unless explicitly requested.

- Scope-creep mitigation:
  - Any request to run auto-plan for `in_progress` items or to change loop semantics should be recorded as a separate follow-up work item. This keeps the current change small and reviewable.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When ralph is invoked on a target with stage `in_progress`, should ralph accept that stage and proceed?" — Answer (agent inference): "Yes. The seed intent states: 'It is assumed that an item that is in_progress has been through the intake_complete and possibly plan_complete stages.' Therefore the agent infers ralph should accept `in_progress` as a valid entrypoint and proceed." Source: seed input (interactive) / agent inference. Final: yes.

- Q: "Should the auto-plan step run automatically for an `in_progress` item if effort/risk fields are not set?" — Answer (agent inference): "No. Per the assumption, in_progress items have passed intake and autoplan should ordinarily have been handled already. The conservative change is to accept `in_progress` as an entrypoint without invoking auto-plan. If the team prefers a different behaviour (e.g., run auto-plan when effort/risk missing), create a follow-up work item." Source: seed input and conservative safety assumption. Final: do not run auto-plan for in_progress.

- Q: "Should unit tests and docs be updated as part of this change?" — Answer (agent inference): "Yes — tests (tests/test_ralph_loop.py) that assert a precondition error for in_progress must be updated; docs and skill README must be updated to reflect the new allowed stage." Source: repository tests and docs discovered during intake. Final: yes, update tests and docs.

Agents should run tests in quiet mode

Headline

When agents run test suites as part of automation (implement/ralph/triage flows), they should run tests in a quiet mode that suppresses streaming of passing-test noise and only exposes failing test details and a short summary at the end. This preserves the agent context window and surfaces only actionable output.

Problem statement

Agent-driven test runs often stream the full test output into the agent's conversation/log. For large test suites this floods the agent context and operator view with non-actionable information. We need a consistent, auditable approach so agents run tests with reduced verbosity while still providing full failure details when tests fail.

Users

- Operators / Producers: want concise, focused test output to review CI/test failures and accept or triage results.
- Developers running or reviewing agent-produced changes: want to see failure details to debug, without scrolling through passing-test noise.
- Agent implementers (skills such as ralph, triage, implement): need a clear, shared contract for invoking test runners.

Success criteria (measurable)

1. Agent test runners (see "Scope" below) invoke tests using the standard quiet command: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` (or an equivalent wrapper) by default.
2. When tests PASS, agent output contains only a concise summary (e.g., "123 passed in 12.3s") and no per-test streaming output.
3. When tests FAIL, agent output includes the failing test names, full tracebacks (failure details) and the summary, but excludes unrelated passing-test lines.
4. Unit or integration tests are added that assert agent flows invoke the quiet flags or that output-filtering is applied (tests mock subprocess/runner invocations and verify flags and/or filtering behavior).
5. All related documentation is updated to describe the quiet-test behavior and the canonical command/flags to use.
6. Full project test suite passes after the change.

This epic replaces Worklog's fragile single audit field with a dedicated latest-only audit results table that becomes the sole source of truth for audit state.

## Problem statement

Worklog currently stores audit state in a fragile text field that depends on LLM-generated wording and ad hoc parsing. The model also loses important metadata such as timestamps and machine-readable output, which makes audit handling brittle across the codebase.

## Users

- **Operators and maintainers** who need reliable, queryable audit records when deciding whether a work item is ready to close.
  - User story: As an operator, I want the most recent audit to be stored in a structured table so I can trust audit state without parsing free text.
- **Developers working on audit consumers** who need a stable data shape and clear migration path.
  - User story: As a maintainer, I want audit reads and writes to use one canonical table so I can remove fragile field parsing.
- **Reviewers and Producers** who need a consistent, auditable record of the most recent closure decision.
  - User story: As a reviewer, I want the latest audit result and metadata available in a structured record so I can inspect the decision quickly.

## Success criteria

- A dedicated audit results table exists and stores the latest audit for each work item as the sole source of truth for audit state.
- The stored audit record includes, at minimum: work item id, `ready_to_close`, audit timestamp, machine-readable output, and human-readable summary.
- Existing Worklog data is backfilled from the current `workitems.audit` field into the new table during migration.
- Runtime reads and writes use the new table exclusively; no fallback or compatibility path continues to read from or write to the old audit field.
- The legacy audit storage path is removed, including the `audit` column on `workitems` and any code paths that depend on it.
- Automated tests cover migration, persistence, and read-path behavior for the new audit storage model.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No fallback or compatibility layers: the new table replaces the old audit storage model completely.
- Latest-only storage: each work item keeps only its most recent audit record in the new table.
- Migration input is limited to the existing `workitems.audit` field; do not reconstruct rows from existing audit comments.
- Keep the change scoped to audit storage and its immediate consumers; record any newly discovered work as separate linked work items.
- Preserve the ability to inspect the audit trail through the new structured record rather than through fragile free-text parsing.

## Existing state

- Worklog currently stores audit text in the `workitems.audit` column and exposes it through `wl show` / `--audit-text`-based paths.
- Ralph and related documentation still assume audit data can be read from the work item record or related comment-based conventions.
- The current implementation relies on parsing `Ready to close:` text and, in some paths, `# AMPA Audit Result` comments to infer audit state.
- The database schema already includes an `audit TEXT` column on `workitems`, which is the main legacy storage path to remove.

## Desired change

- Add a dedicated audit results table and write the latest audit there for each work item.
- Store structured audit metadata such as readiness, timestamps, machine-readable payload, and human-readable summary in the new table.
- Backfill the table from the existing `workitems.audit` values for the current Worklog database.
- Update readers and writers to use the new table only, then remove the old audit field from the schema and code paths.
- Update docs and tests to describe and verify the new storage model.

## Related work

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — defines the current persisted audit contract and the `wl update --audit-text` path that the new storage model will replace.
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — current helper that writes audit text via `wl update`; useful reference for the persistence boundary.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — current consumer of persisted audit state; it will need to read from the new table instead of the legacy field.
- `docs/ralph.md` — documents how Ralph interprets and reuses persisted audits today.
- `docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md` — shows the current audit trail and redundant-audit suppression behavior.
- `docs/triage-audit.md` — documents the `# AMPA Audit Result` flow that the new storage model replaces as a source of truth.
- `Ralph crashes reading persisted audit when workItem.audit is an object (SA-0MPD8NXCS0091ZF4)` — demonstrates fragility in the current field-based model and why structured storage is needed.
- `ralph: skip redundant start-of-iteration audit when persisted audit is up-to-date (SA-0MPE03RD0005NE0H)` — relies on existing audit persistence semantics and will need to align with the new table.
- `Harden Ralph Loop (SA-0MPDX3U1V006293J)` — broader Ralph hardening context that includes audit behavior changes.

## Related work (automated report)

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` document the current text-based audit persistence path. They are the best reference points for replacing the legacy field with structured storage.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` and `docs/ralph.md` are the main audit consumers. Both currently depend on persisted audit text and will need to switch to the new table.
- `docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md` and `docs/triage-audit.md` describe the current audit trail and `# AMPA Audit Result` conventions, which are useful when updating user-facing docs.
- `Ralph crashes reading persisted audit when workItem.audit is an object (SA-0MPD8NXCS0091ZF4)` is a direct precedent for this item because it exposes the fragility of the current audit field model.
- `ralph: skip redundant start-of-iteration audit when persisted audit is up-to-date (SA-0MPE03RD0005NE0H)` is related because it reads persisted audit state to make control-flow decisions; it will likely need to be updated to read from the new table.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Removing the legacy field can break consumers that still read `workitems.audit` or rely on comment-based audit detection. **Mitigation:** update all known consumers in the same change and add tests that fail if the old path is still used.
- **Risk:** The migration may lose audit data if the backfill logic is incomplete. **Mitigation:** keep migration limited to the existing field-only source of truth and verify backfill with tests.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into broader audit/comment redesign. **Mitigation:** record any additional ideas as separate work items instead of expanding this epic.
- **Assumption:** The current `workitems.audit` field contains the latest audit text that should be migrated into the new table.
- **Assumption:** The new table should retain only the latest audit per work item, not a historical audit chain.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the new table be the sole source of truth for audit state, or should `# AMPA Audit Result` comments remain as a human-readable trail?" — Answer (user): "Yes". Interpreted from the seed intent and response as: the new table is the sole source of truth for audit state, while comments are not used for state decisions. Source: interactive reply plus seed intent. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should the new table store only the latest audit per work item, or keep a history of audit rows with one marked as latest?" — Answer (user): "latest-only". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "For the initial migration, should we backfill from the current `workitems.audit` field only, or also reconstruct rows from existing audit comments when needed?" — Answer (user): "field only". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
data.title: Replace Worklog audit field with dedicated audit results table

# Ralph: Investigate missing user-facing text in Pi/LLM responses (no_text_extracted)

Summary

Ralph's implement→audit loop is repeatedly receiving Pi/LLM responses that contain structured JSON but no user-facing textual content. Ralph logs `ralph.cmd.pi.no_text_extracted` and cannot extract remediation instructions, which prevents audits from moving to "ready". This has been observed repeatedly after a machine crash and resume; there are ~14 occurrences in the current log.

Evidence / logs

- Primary log file: `/tmp/ralph-loop-continue.log`
- Relevant matches saved: `/tmp/ralph-debug/log_matches.txt`
- Context around first occurrence: `/tmp/ralph-debug/no_text_context.txt`
- Recent audit completions: `/tmp/ralph-debug/audit_complete_recent.txt`

Example log lines (from the live system):

```
$(sed -n '1,40p' /tmp/ralph-debug/no_text_context.txt)
```

Observed behavior

- Ralph logs `ralph.cmd.pi.no_text_extracted json_lines=...` when a Pi run returns JSON but no text.
- After these events, `ralph.loop.audit.complete` shows `ready=False` and unmet criteria remain (e.g. 9 unmet / 17 criteria).
- Ralph cycles through remediation attempts until reaching `ralph.loop.max_attempts` for the target.

Steps to reproduce

1. Start Ralph against the epic: `python3 /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py WL-0MP0E0M5500846SL --json`
2. Observe output in `/tmp/ralph-loop-continue.log` and search for `no_text_extracted`.
3. If available, reproduce by invoking Pi/LLM with the same model/proxy configuration used by Ralph and inspect the raw model output for text vs structured JSON.

Suggested debugging steps

- Capture the raw Pi/LLM payload for failing streams (see related task to persist raw outputs).
- Compare actual Pi output format to the expected format Ralph parses; check for missing fields (e.g., `text` or `content`).
- Check Pi proxy/model config (is it configured to emit JSON-only responses?) and revert to including plain text.
- If structured-only output is intended, implement a parser in Ralph that can extract remediation actions from the structured JSON (see separate task).

Acceptance criteria

- Root cause identified and documented (Pi config vs model behavior vs Ralph parsing bug).
- Unit/regression test added to replicate the behavior and cover the fix.
- Ralph either (a) accepts structured-only responses by extracting actionable content, or (b) Pi output is reconfigured to include human-readable text; no_text_extracted warnings are resolved for a representative run.

Related files & artifacts

- `/tmp/ralph-loop-continue.log`
- `/tmp/audit_WL-0MP0E0M5500846SL.md`
- `scripts/ralph_loop.py` in this repo: `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py`

Summary

An orchestrator/LLM error was observed during nested Pi runs: `pi run failed: Cannot continue from message role: assistant`. This appears to be an orchestration/resume logic bug when resuming or performing nested LLM calls from within the agent flow. It can cause the Ralph loop to fail or produce unexpected output.

Observed behavior

- The system reports `Cannot continue from message role: assistant` for a Pi run. This suggests that a message sequence in the Pi/LLM conversation is not being progressed correctly when resuming or making nested calls.
- Consequence: stream interruption, potential empty outputs, and failed remediation attempts.

Steps to reproduce

1. Run `ralph_loop.py` as usual; observe if nested pi.run is invoked (logs show `ralph.cmd.pi.stream_start`).
2. Attempt to simulate nested calls (e.g., an LLM call that triggers another LLM call) in a controlled test harness.

- Reproduce the exact sequence of Pi calls that lead to this error (capture message roles and content for each step).
- Inspect the Pi SDK / proxy usage to see how conversation state and message roles are managed during nested calls/resume.
- Add instrumentation to record the role and index of each message passed to Pi during nested runs.
- Add a unit test that creates the nested scenario and verifies correct role progression.

Acceptance criteria

- Root cause is identified and fixed such that nested/resumed calls do not raise this error for expected sequences.
- Regression tests added to prevent recurrence.

# Simplify ralph skill background execution and status reporting

Summary: Launch Ralph in the background with `nohup` and provide `ralph status` for live and post-exit monitoring.

## Problem statement
Ralph currently runs the deterministic orchestration loop synchronously. We need it to launch the loop in the background with `nohup`, then let operators request status updates while the run is still active.

## Users
- Operators running long-lived Ralph sessions.
- Engineers monitoring progress of active work items.

### Example user stories
- As an operator, I want Ralph to keep running in the background so I can continue using my shell while the loop executes.
- As an operator, I want `ralph status` to report recent activity without needing the original work item id.
- As an engineer, I want status output to show the active focus item and tracked Worklog status counts so I can understand progress at a glance.

## Success criteria
- Ralph starts the deterministic loop in the background using `nohup` rather than blocking the caller.
- `ralph status` reports the current process state while the loop is running.
- `ralph status` works without a work item id by using the current control-loop process context.
- Status output includes recent activity since the last status update, the currently active task, and a summary of parent/child Worklog `status` counts with deltas from the previous update.
- When the background process has exited, `ralph status` reports the exit code and the final summary snapshot.
- Automated tests verify both the background launch path and the status-reporting path.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints
- The last-status cursor is stored only in the control agent loop context; no persistence layer should be added for it.
- `ralph status` should not require a work item id because the control loop already knows the PID and log path.
- Worklog `status` values are the source of truth for parent/child summary counts.
- Active task detection should come from the latest log line that identifies a focus work item.
- Keep the change scoped to Ralph orchestration and status reporting; do not broaden into unrelated loop redesigns.

## Existing state

# Summary

`ralph status` can report an invalid `active_task` value such as `the` because `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py::_extract_active_task()` uses broad regular expressions that scan the raw log text for words after `implement` or `audit`. When the log contains natural-language assistant prose, the parser can capture an ordinary word instead of a work item id.

This was observed while debugging the active run for `WL-0MP0E0M5500846SL`.

`discovered-from:WL-0MP0E0M5500846SL`

## User story

As an operator inspecting a Ralph background run, I need `ralph status` to report a real work item id or nothing at all, never a stray word taken from assistant prose.

## Expected behavior

- `active_task` should come from structured Ralph control lines, not from arbitrary assistant text.
- If no valid work item id is present, `active_task` should be `null` / absent rather than a guessed token.
- Status output should never show obvious filler words such as `the`, `a`, `it`, or similar prose tokens.

## Evidence from the live run

The current runtime context saved for the live Ralph run shows:

- `last_active_task: "the"`
- the log includes streamed assistant prose after `ralph.cmd.pi.stream_start`
- there is no structured evidence that `the` is a real active work item

Relevant implementation area:

- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py::_extract_active_task()`
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py::inspect_status()`

## Steps to reproduce manually

1. Create a temporary Ralph runtime log file with these lines:

```text
INFO ralph.loop.start target=SA-TARGET scope=SA-TARGET,SA-CHILD max_attempts=10
INFO ralph.loop.child_focus parent=SA-TARGET child=SA-CHILD
INFO ralph.cmd.pi.stream_start model=Local Proxy/qwen3 cmd_len=8
Let me start by implementing the work item and checking the current state.
```

2. Save a matching `current.json` runtime state file that points to the log.
3. Run the status inspector, for example:

```bash
python3 skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py status --cwd <runtime-root> --json
```

4. Observe that the parser can incorrectly select a prose token such as `the` or another short word from the assistant text instead of the structured `child=SA-CHILD` marker.

## Repro test instructions

Add a regression test in `skill/ralph/tests/test_control_runtime.py` that writes a runtime log containing both:

- a structured `child_focus parent=... child=...` line, and
- one or more assistant-prose lines that include phrases like `implement the work item` or `audit the results`

Then assert that `inspect_status()` returns either:

- the structured child work item id, or
- `None`

but **never** a prose word like `the`.

The test should fail with the current implementation because `_extract_active_task()` simply searches for `implement\s+(\S+)` and `audit\s+(\S+)` in reverse log order, which allows natural-language text to win.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Restrict `active_task` extraction to explicit structured control lines only.
- Validate any candidate token against the work item id pattern before accepting it.
- Prefer `child=` or `target=` markers from Ralph control logs over any text in streamed assistant output.
- If no structured id can be found, return `None` rather than guessing.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ralph status` never reports obvious prose words as `active_task`.
- `active_task` is either a valid work item id or `null` / omitted.
- A regression test covers the bad parse case and passes.
- Existing `child_focus`-based status reporting remains intact.

# Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout

Ralph can hang indefinitely when the delegated `pi` subprocess keeps `stdout` open and never reaches a terminal stream event. The loop needs to fail fast with a clear, testable error path while preserving normal streaming behavior for finite runs.

## Problem statement

`skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py::_stream_pi()` currently iterates `process.stdout` to EOF before reading `stderr` and finishing the run. If `pi` never closes `stdout`, Ralph never logs `stream_end`, never reaches audit/check/merge steps, and the run stalls forever.

## Users

- Operators running long-lived Ralph sessions who need runs to complete or fail clearly.
- Engineers diagnosing orchestration failures caused by streamed Pi output.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I want Ralph to stop with a clear error if a streamed `pi` run never terminates, so the session does not hang silently.
- As an engineer, I want `stderr` and streaming output to be handled without deadlocking the loop, so failures are easy to debug.
- As a maintainer, I want a regression test that reproduces the stuck-stream scenario without hanging the test suite.

## Success criteria

- Ralph no longer hangs indefinitely when `pi` keeps `stdout` open or omits a terminal stream event.
- A regression test reproduces the stuck-stream scenario and fails before the fix.
- `stderr` is consumed safely without stalling the streaming loop.
- Normal streaming still emits `stream_end` and preserves user-facing `text_delta` output for successful runs.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing Pi JSON streaming protocol and additive `text_delta` console output.
- Keep scope limited to Ralph stream handling, failure reporting, and tests.
- Avoid introducing unrelated orchestration changes or broader session-management behavior.
- Existing resilience semantics for delegated commands should remain consistent with current Ralph behavior.

## Existing state

- `_stream_pi()` in `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` reads `process.stdout` line by line and only then waits for the child process to exit.
- The implementation already supports normal JSON streaming, verbose raw-line logging, and debug persistence for `no_text_extracted` runs.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` already covers JSON streaming, verbose logging, and raw payload persistence, but does not cover a hung `stdout` reader or a stalled `stderr` path.
- Related documentation already explains Ralph streaming behavior and the `--no-stream` / `--quiet` options in `docs/ralph.md` and `skill/ralph/SKILL.md`.

## Desired change

- Drain `stdout` and `stderr` without blocking the whole loop on an open pipe.
- Add a bounded timeout or watchdog path that terminates a stalled `pi` process and surfaces a clear error.
- Preserve the existing parsing and logging behavior for normal successful streams.
- Add focused regression coverage for the hanging-stream scenario.

## Related work

### Potentially related docs

- `docs/ralph.md` — canonical Ralph behavior, including streaming and `--no-stream` / `--quiet` options.
- `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — operator-facing Ralph launch and status guidance.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — implementation of the streaming loop that currently blocks on `process.stdout`.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — existing streaming, verbose logging, and debug-persistence coverage.

### Potentially related work items

- `Ralph: Persist raw Pi/LLM outputs for failed streams (debug logging) (SA-0MPFD4S79000J12K)` — established the debug-persistence path for streamed Pi failures and is the closest precedent for stream-handling hardening.
- `Ralph: Investigate missing user-facing text in Pi/LLM responses (no_text_extracted) (SA-0MPFD4RMU005NF9C)` — related to stream parsing outcomes when Pi output is structurally valid but user-facing text is absent.
- `Ralph: prevent CLI from exiting when delegated wl or other commands fail (add configurable fail-open & retry) (SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7)` — adjacent resilience work for long-running Ralph sessions; useful for error-handling conventions, but not a duplicate.
- `Ralph loop should be non-interactive (SA-0MPAVKVD4001DWBO)` — related orchestration hardening that shares the same Ralph control loop, but focuses on prompt suppression rather than stream termination.

## Related work (automated report)

- `SA-0MPFD4S79000J12K` is the closest precedent because it already hardened Ralph’s handling of failed streams by persisting raw Pi payloads for later analysis. That work proves the `_stream_pi()` path is the right place to make stream-failure behavior observable, but it does not address the hang caused by an open stdout pipe.
- `SA-0MPFD4RMU005NF9C` covers a nearby failure mode where Pi output is structured but yields no user-facing text. It is relevant because the same streaming parser and logging path are involved, but the current item is specifically about preventing indefinite blocking.
- `SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7` is adjacent resilience work for delegated commands. It is not the same bug, but it provides a useful pattern for clear failure reporting and bounded retries where appropriate.
- `docs/ralph.md`, `skill/ralph/SKILL.md`, `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py`, and `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` are the canonical references for how Ralph streams Pi output today and where the regression coverage should live.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** A timeout or watchdog may change the behavior of long-running but healthy streams.  
  **Mitigation note:** Keep the change narrowly scoped and preserve normal finite-stream behavior.
- **Risk:** Concurrent pipe handling can introduce subtle deadlocks or resource leaks.  
  **Mitigation note:** Add a regression test that exercises the stalled-stream path without hanging the suite.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into broader process supervision or session lifecycle management.  
  **Mitigation note:** Record any follow-up opportunities as linked work items instead of expanding this item.

### Assumptions

- A stalled `pi` stream can be reproduced in tests with a fake process object.
- Existing streaming parser behavior should remain unchanged for successful runs.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required. The existing work item description and repository context were sufficient to draft the intake brief. Source: `SA-0MPG1X6M2005CKKT`, `docs/ralph.md`, `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py`, `tests/test_ralph_loop.py`.

# Problem statement

Ralph can finish its work-item loop while a delegated Pi subprocess is still alive, which keeps the Ralph control process from exiting cleanly. The fix should make completion deterministic by ensuring Pi shuts down gracefully when work is complete and, if it does not, Ralph force-terminates the lingering process as a fallback.

# Users

- Operators who launch long-running Ralph sessions and expect them to finish and return control promptly.
- Maintainers and automation authors who need background runs to exit cleanly instead of hanging on an orphaned child process.
- Reviewers diagnosing stalled runs who need a clear shutdown path and reliable cleanup behavior.

## Example user stories

- As an operator, I want Ralph to end cleanly when all scoped work items are complete, so I do not have to manually kill the session.
- As a maintainer, I want Ralph to terminate a lingering Pi process if it does not exit on its own, so the control process cannot hang indefinitely.
- As a reviewer, I want shutdown behavior to be visible in logs, so I can tell whether Ralph exited normally or had to clean up a stray process.

# Success criteria

- Ralph exits normally when a run completes and Pi shuts down cleanly; no orphaned Pi process remains after completion.
- If Pi remains alive after completion, Ralph sends a graceful termination signal first and then escalates to a forced kill after the configured grace period.
- A regression test covers the clean shutdown path and a separate regression test covers the fallback kill path.
- Shutdown or cleanup behavior is logged clearly enough to distinguish normal completion from forced termination.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Constraints

- Prefer graceful shutdown over forced termination.
- Keep the change narrowly focused on Ralph/Pi lifecycle handling; do not expand into unrelated scheduler or worklog features.
- Preserve existing successful run behavior, including the final audit/merge flow and user-facing output.
- Use the same process-safety patterns already used elsewhere in the project, such as process-group cleanup and bounded grace periods.
- The cleanup path should be safe to run even if the process has already exited.

# Existing state

- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` launches Pi subprocesses and currently waits for them to exit as part of the streaming path, but there is no explicit end-of-run cleanup sequence for a stubborn child process.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py` records the background PID and status, but its role is observational rather than corrective.
- `docs/ralph.md` and `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` describe Ralph launch and status behavior, but they do not currently document a forced cleanup path at completion.
- `docs/delegation-control.md` already documents a broader process-group termination pattern elsewhere in the project, which is a useful precedent for this behavior.
- A related open issue already exists for a narrower hang scenario: `Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout (SA-0MPG1X6K2005CKKT)`.

# Desired change

- Add a deterministic shutdown step for Pi when Ralph reaches the end of a run.
- Prefer a graceful termination path first so a normal completion can close Pi cleanly.
- If Pi does not exit within the grace period, have Ralph terminate the lingering process or process group as a fallback.
- Make the cleanup outcome observable in logs and any final status output.
- Add tests that prove both the graceful and fallback paths work without leaving hanging processes behind.

# Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** A too-aggressive cleanup could terminate a valid Pi session that is still unwinding.  
  **Mitigation note:** Keep the cleanup bounded and only trigger it once Ralph has already determined the run is complete.
- **Risk:** Forced termination may behave differently across platforms or subprocess wrappers.  
  **Mitigation note:** Reuse the project’s existing process-group cleanup patterns and test the supported environment.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into broader lifecycle management or scheduler behavior.  
  **Mitigation note:** Record any extra process-supervision ideas as separate linked work items instead of expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** The most robust solution is a two-step approach: attempt graceful shutdown first, then force-kill only if the child remains alive.

# Related work

## Potentially related docs

- `docs/ralph.md` — canonical Ralph orchestration and status behavior; should describe the end-of-run cleanup path.
- `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — operator-facing Ralph usage notes; should mention what happens when a run completes.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — the main implementation target for Pi lifecycle handling.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py` — background run supervisor and status reporting; may need to surface cleanup state.
- `docs/delegation-control.md` — existing process-group termination pattern elsewhere in the project that can serve as a precedent.

## Potentially related work items

- `Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout (SA-0MPG1X6K2005CKKT)` — a narrower hang bug in the same Ralph/Pi streaming area; useful precedent but not the same failure mode.
- `Ralph: prevent CLI from exiting when delegated wl or other commands fail (add configurable fail-open & retry) (SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7)` — adjacent resilience work for delegated commands and failure handling.
- `Dispatch interface and opencode run backend (SA-0MLX8G4EK12N0B5S)` — broader process-spawning precedent with detached subprocess behavior.

## Related work (automated report)

- `SA-0MPG1X6K2005CKKT` is the closest precedent because it already addresses a Ralph hang caused by a Pi subprocess that does not finish cleanly. That item focuses on stdout streaming never reaching EOF, while this item is broader: it wants the end-of-run cleanup path itself to guarantee the control process can exit.
- `SA-0MPB0XUWY008IUA7` is adjacent because it hardens Ralph’s delegated command failure handling. It is relevant for logging and resilience patterns, but it does not address orphaned Pi lifecycle management.
- `SA-0MLX8G4EK12N0B5S` is a useful precedent for subprocess management because it documents detached process behavior and test coverage for fire-and-forget dispatch. The mechanics differ, but the process-safety and lifecycle lessons are relevant.
- `docs/delegation-control.md` is the best documentation precedent because it already explains SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation for delegated processes. That pattern should inform the Ralph shutdown behavior and any corresponding documentation updates.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Do you want both behaviors?" — Answer (user): "both". Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Summary
Move the recent-audit bootstrap into the `implement` skill itself and remove the separate command wrapper. The skill should first inspect the target work item for a recent audit, reuse it when present, and fall back to `/skill:audit <id>` when no recent audit exists. The command-level wrapper is out of scope for this change.

## User story
As an operator using the `implement` skill, I want the skill to reuse a recent audit when one already exists so that implementation starts from current work-item state, while still falling back to a fresh audit when needed.

## Expected behaviour
- The `implement` skill checks the work item for a recent audit artifact at startup.
- If the most recent relevant action on the work item is an audit record, the skill uses that audit output as the source of truth for what work remains.
- If there is no recent audit, the skill runs `/skill:audit <id>` and uses the resulting output to establish the work that needs to be done.
- The skill does not proceed to implementation planning until it has either reused a recent audit or completed a fresh audit.
- The separate command wrapper is removed so the skill doc is the source of truth for this behavior.

## Assumptions
- "Recent audit" means the most recent worklog action, comment, or audit entry associated with the work item is an audit record that is still relevant to the current work state.
- The audit output used by the skill must be the same output that would be used if the audit were run explicitly.

## Suggested implementation approach
- Keep the startup lookup logic in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Reuse the audit payload if one is current enough to satisfy startup requirements.
- Otherwise invoke the audit workflow explicitly with `/skill:audit <id>` and feed its result into the existing implementation planning path.
- Add tests for both branches: reusing a recent audit and performing a fresh audit when none exists.
- Remove the separate command wrapper file so the skill remains the authoritative implementation path.

## Acceptance criteria
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` first instructs the agent to inspect the work item for a recent audit before doing any other planning work.
- If the most recent work-item action is an audit, the skill reuses that audit output instead of running a new audit.
- If no recent audit exists, the skill invokes `/skill:audit <id>` and uses the resulting output.
- Tests cover both the audit-reuse and full-audit fallback paths.
- The implementation preserves the existing implementation workflow after audit selection.
- The separate command wrapper is removed from the repository.

- The implementation path resolves a model from CLI, per-step config, legacy `model`, or `DEFAULT_MODEL`.
- `model_source` selects the remote or local implementation id explicitly.
- No implicit remote/local fallback is attempted.
- Existing implement behaviour remains unchanged when no new config/flags are provided.

- Extend the phase resolver so the `implement` prompt receives a phase-specific resolved id.
- Keep remediation prompts and child-transition `/compact` behaviour unchanged.

- `implement` passes the resolved implementation model to `pi` via `--model`.
- Remote/local selection follows the configured `model_source`.
- Default behaviour stays on the existing single-model path when the new config is absent.

## Summary

Currently Ralph defaults to `model_source: remote` and there is no easy way to switch to local models via the `/ralph` command. Operators must either edit `.ralph.json` or run the Python script directly with `--model-source`.

## User Story

As an operator, I want Ralph to default to local models so I can run automation without requiring remote API access, and I want a simple shorthand to switch to remote when needed.

## Desired Change

1. Change the default `model_source` from `remote` to `local` in `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json`
2. Add a `--model-source` flag to the `/ralph` command (and the skill invocation) so operators can write:
   - `ralph <id>` → uses local models (default)
   - `ralph <id> remote` → uses remote models
3. The Python script already supports `--model-source`, so this is primarily about:
   - Changing the default
   - Exposing the flag in the command/skill wrapper

## Acceptance Criteria

- Default `model_source` in `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json` is changed from `remote` to `local`
- The `/ralph` command accepts an optional model source argument (e.g., `ralph <id> remote`)
- `ralph <id>` without a source argument uses local models
- `ralph <id> remote` uses remote models
- The model source is passed through to the underlying `ralph_loop.py` script
- Existing `--model-source` CLI flag on `ralph_loop.py` continues to work
- Documentation updated to reflect the new default and shorthand

## Summary

Ralph reports success (returncode=0) even when Pi **echoes back the input text** instead of actually executing commands. This creates a silent failure mode where no implementation work is done, but Ralph treats the run as successful.

## Root Cause

Two bugs combine to create this silent failure:

### Bug 1: Pi/Model returns input as output
When the configured model (e.g., `Local Proxy/gpt120`) is unavailable or broken, Pi returns the **input text echoed back** instead of an error. The exit code is 0, making it appear successful.

### Bug 2: Ralph trusts exit code without output validation
Ralph uses `returncode=0` as the sole indicator of success. It does not validate that the output:
- Is different from the input
- Contains a valid structured response
- Has non-zero `actions` count for implementation
- Contains actual work product (not skill file content for audit)

## Evidence from Execution

### Implement Phase - Input Echoed Back

**Command sent:**
```
pi -p --no-session --mode json --model 'Local Proxy/gpt120' 'implement CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89
Continue until the work item and all dependencies are completed, but do not merge.
Do not ask the producer questions or pause for interactive input.
If you cannot continue safely without explicit producer input, stop and return a structured no_safe_path response with the missing decision.'
```

**Response received (identical to input):**
```json
{
  "ts": 1779658458585,
  "level": "INFO",
  "logger": "ralph",
  "msg": "ralph.cmd.pi.structured_response actions=0 summary_len=319",
  "actions": [],
  "summary": "implement CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89
Continue until the work item and all dependencies are completed...",
  "text": "implement CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89
Continue until the work item and all dependencies are completed..."
}
```

**Key indicators of failure:**
- `actions=0` — No tool calls were made
- `text` is identical to the input prompt
- No git commits, no file changes, no worklog updates

### Audit Phase - Skill Content Echoed Back

**Command sent:**
```
pi -p --no-session --mode json --model 'Local Proxy/gpt120' '/skill:audit CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89'
```

**Response received (skill file content, not audit report):**
```json
{
  "ts": 1779658515562,
  "level": "INFO",
  "logger": "ralph",
  "msg": "ralph.cmd.pi.structured_response actions=0 summary_len=11442",
  "actions": [],
  "text": "<skill name=\"audit\" location=\"/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/SKILL.md\">
References are relative to...

# Audit

## Overview
..."
}
```

**Key indicators of failure:**
- `text` contains the raw SKILL.md content, not an audit report
- `actions=0` — No tool calls were made
- Final error: `"No persisted audit found for CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89 after running /skill:audit"`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a model that is unavailable or returns degraded responses (e.g., `Local Proxy/gpt120`)
2. Run Ralph on any work item: `ralph <work-item-id>`
3. Observe that Ralph reports success but no work was done

## Expected Behaviour

Ralph should detect when:
- The output is identical or nearly identical to the input
- The `actions` count is 0 for implementation runs
- The output doesn't contain expected structured content
- The output contains raw skill file content instead of skill execution results

When detected, Ralph should:
- Fail the attempt with a clear error message
- Retry with a different model (if configured)
- Log the failure reason for debugging

## Impact

- Silent failures waste compute resources
- Operators believe work is being done when nothing is happening
- No automatic retry or fallback occurs
- Trust in automation is eroded

## Suggested Fix

1. **Output validation in Ralph**: After Pi returns, validate:
   - `text` ≠ input prompt (for implement)
   - `actions.length > 0` or `text` contains expected markers
   - `text` does not start with `<skill` (raw skill content)

2. **Pi-level validation**: Detect when model returns input as output and return non-zero exit code

3. **Model health check**: Before running, verify model can respond to a simple test prompt

## Related Files

- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — Main Ralph loop (lines 2030-2145 handle args, stream processing)
- `skill/ralph/ralph` — Wrapper script that invokes ralph_loop.py

## Environment

- Ralph PID: 345127
- Pi PID: 345275 (during audit phase)
- Model: `Local Proxy/gpt120`
- Target work item: CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89 (SVG, Texture & Tooltip Helpers)
- Timestamp: 2026-05-24T21:33 UTC
- Log file: `.worklog/ralph/CG-0MP12WPCP008LW89.log`

# Ralph Pi Stream Stalls on Remote Models

> When Ralph runs with remote models, the Pi subprocess stalls on a hardcoded 60-second stdout timeout. Make the timeout configurable per model source so remote models can use a higher threshold while preserving local model behavior.

## Problem Statement

When Ralph runs with remote models (`--model-source remote`), the Pi subprocess frequently stalls with a 60-second timeout waiting for stdout to close. This causes Ralph to exhaust its retry budget without completing any work. The 60-second timeout was designed for local models but is too aggressive for remote models with higher network latency and variable response times.

## Users

- **AI Agent Operators** — Users running Ralph with remote models to orchestrate implement→audit loops across projects.
- **Developer Experience** — Anyone using Ralph automation who needs reliable remote model execution.

### User Stories

- As an operator, I want Ralph to complete full implement→audit loops with remote models so that I can use cloud-hosted models for my workflows.
- As an operator, I want the Pi stream timeout to adapt to model source characteristics so that I don't need to manually tune timeouts for each model.
- As a maintainer, I want existing local model functionality to remain unchanged so that the fix doesn't introduce regressions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Pi stream timeout is configurable per model source (remote vs local) in Ralph's configuration.
- Remote models use a timeout of at least 300 seconds (or configurable higher value) that accommodates network latency and variable response times.
- Local models continue to use the existing 60-second timeout by default.
- Ralph successfully completes a full implement→audit loop with at least one remote model (e.g., qwen3.6-Plus).
- The fix works for all current and future remote models without requiring per-model configuration.
- Existing local model functionality is not regressed.
- Unit or integration tests are added to verify the timeout behavior for both local and remote model sources.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix must be backward compatible with existing `.ralph.json` configurations.
- The default behavior for local models must not change.
- No new external dependencies should be required.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Additional remote model issues may be discovered beyond the timeout problem. Mitigation: record any new issues as separate work items linked to this one rather than expanding the scope of this fix.
- **Timeout value selection**: The 300s remote timeout is an initial estimate based on current provider latency patterns; real-world usage may reveal that a different value is needed.
- **Regression risk**: Changes to `_stream_pi` or RalphLoop initialization could inadvertently affect local model streaming behavior.
- **Config schema change**: Adding timeout fields to `.ralph.json` may conflict with user customizations. Mitigation: use nested `timeout` object under `model_source` sections.
- **Assumption**: Remote model stalls are primarily caused by the timeout being too aggressive, not by a separate Pi JSON streaming bug.

## Existing State

Ralph's `_stream_pi` method uses a hardcoded `pi_stream_timeout_seconds = 60.0` for all model sources. This timeout was added in work item `SA-0MPG1X6M2005CKKT` ("Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout") to prevent local model runs from hanging indefinitely. However, remote models have inherently higher latency, and the 60-second threshold is frequently exceeded during:
- Long-running commands (e.g., `npm test`, builds)
- Periods of model inactivity while processing
- Network variability between Ralph and the remote provider

The timeout is set in `ralph_loop.py` line 842 and used in `_stream_pi` at lines 1173 (stdout queue get) and 1230 (process wait).

## Desired Change

1. Make `pi_stream_timeout_seconds` configurable in Ralph's configuration system (`.ralph.json` and CLI flags).
2. Add a `model_source`-specific default timeout configuration in `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json`.
3. Update `_stream_pi` to resolve the timeout based on the active model source.
4. Update the RalphLoop constructor to read the timeout from config.
5. Add tests verifying timeout behavior for both local and remote sources.
6. Update documentation (`docs/ralph.md`, `skill/ralph/SKILL.md`) to document the new timeout configuration.

## Related Work

- `SA-0MPG1X6M2005CKKT` — "Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout" (completed): Added the 60s watchdog timeout that is now too aggressive for remote models.
- `SA-0MPK9DRLR000ZMTE` — "Change default model source to local and add remote shorthand" (completed): Changed default model source from remote to local and added shorthand syntax support.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — Core Ralph loop implementation containing `_stream_pi` and timeout configuration.
- `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json` — Default configuration file for model sources.
- `docs/ralph.md` — Ralph usage documentation.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — Test file for Ralph loop behavior.

## Related work (automated report)

- `SA-0MPG1X6M2005CKKT` — "Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout" (completed): This is the direct predecessor that introduced the 60-second `pi_stream_timeout_seconds` watchdog in `_stream_pi()`. The current work item extends that fix by making the timeout value configurable per model source, addressing the remote-model case that the original hardcoded timeout did not account for.
- `SA-0MPK9DRLR000ZMTE` — "Ralph: Change default model source to local and add remote shorthand" (completed): This work changed the default `model_source` from `remote` to `local` and added shorthand syntax. It is relevant because the current work item must respect the `model_source` selection when resolving timeout values.
- `SA-0MPFD4S79000J12K` — "Ralph: Persist raw Pi/LLM outputs for failed streams (debug logging)" (completed): Established the debug-persistence path for streamed Pi failures. Relevant because it hardened the same `_stream_pi()` path, but focused on observability rather than timeout configurability.
- `SA-0MPFD4RMU005NF9C` — "Ralph: Investigate missing user-facing text in Pi/LLM responses (no_text_extracted)" (completed): Related to stream parsing outcomes when Pi output is structurally valid but user-facing text is absent. Shares the same streaming parser path but addresses a different failure mode.
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — The primary file to modify; contains `_stream_pi()` and `pi_stream_timeout_seconds` configuration.
- `skill/ralph/assets/.ralph.json` — Default configuration file where model-source-specific timeout defaults should be added.
- `docs/ralph.md` and `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — Documentation files that should describe the new timeout configuration options.
- `tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — Existing test coverage for streaming behavior; new tests for source-specific timeouts should be added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Which remote models should the fix target for verification?" — Answer (user): "All remote models should work, including as yet undefined ones." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should the fix make the timeout configurable/dynamic, or address the underlying Pi stdout behavior?" — Answer (user): "(a) Make the timeout configurable per model source." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Are there constraints on changing the timeout or streaming architecture?" — Answer (user): "No." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

# Ralph status command produces inconsistent reports

## Problem statement

The `ralph status` command does not produce consistent reports because the LLM interprets and reinterprets the script output each time it runs. The current implementation instructs the agent to "review logs" and "summarize work completed," which causes non-deterministic formatting and content.

## Users

- **Operators** running long-lived Ralph sessions who need to monitor progress
- **Engineers** checking Ralph status to understand current focus and scope

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I want `ralph status` to produce the same markdown report every time I run it, so I can reliably compare outputs
- As an engineer, I want the status output to be a structured markdown report that I can copy-paste without the LLM reformatting it

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ralph status` produces a markdown-formatted report with consistent section ordering
- Running `ralph status` multiple times without state changes produces structurally identical output
- The report includes: state (running/stopped), PID, target ID, active task, last 20 log lines, status counts with deltas
- The SKILL.md instructions tell the LLM to output the script's markdown directly without reinterpretation
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes

## Constraints

- The last-status cursor must remain in the control-loop context (no persistence layer changes)
- Changes should be scoped to `ralph_control.py` formatting and `SKILL.md` instructions
- Backward compatibility with existing `.ralph.json` config

## Existing state

- `ralph_control.py` has a `format_status()` function that produces plain-text output
- SKILL.md instructs the LLM to "review logs" and "summarize work completed" - causing interpretation
- The `--json` flag exists but the LLM likely uses plain text and reinterprets it

## Desired change

1. **Update `format_status()`** in `ralph_control.py` to produce structured markdown with consistent sections
2. **Update SKILL.md** to instruct the LLM to output the script's markdown report directly without reinterpretation
3. **Add tests** verifying the markdown output structure is consistent across calls

## Related work

- **Simplify ralph skill background execution and status reporting (SA-0MPFKNRXD008BZNR)** — completed work that added background execution and status reporting
- **Ralph loop should be non-interactive (SA-0MPAVKVD4001DWBO)** — in-progress related Ralph orchestration work
- `skill/ralph/SKILL.md` — Ralph skill behavior and entrypoint documentation
- `skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_control.py` — Status implementation

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: Changing output format may break existing consumers expecting plain text. Mitigation: Check for downstream consumers; the `--json` flag already provides machine-readable output.
- Risk: LLM may still reformat even with updated instructions. Mitigation: Make the markdown output the canonical format and explicitly instruct "do not reinterpret."

### Assumptions

- The current `format_status()` plain-text output is the source of inconsistency
- The LLM's interpretation of "review" and "summarize" causes the non-determinism
- A structured markdown output with clear instructions will produce consistent reports
- Scope creep mitigation: Any additional features or refactorings should be recorded as separate linked work items rather than expanding this item's scope

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When you say 'identical report every time,' what does that mean?" — Answer (user): "Same snapshot of current state (process alive, log path, status counts) but deltas/recency still reflect current call." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should the command still show recent log activity?" — Answer (user): "Yes, always show last N lines (e.g. last 20)." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "Should deltas between status counts still be shown?" — Answer (user): "Yes, show how counts changed since last call." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q: "What is the root cause of inconsistency?" — Answer (user): "The LLM is interpreting the responses from the script output." Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
