- [ ] Detects placeholder tests (zero assertions, expect(true).toBe(true), TODO-only bodies)
- [ ] Detects self-referential simulations (no production imports / re-implemented logic asserted against itself)
- [ ] Detects duplicate coverage (same behaviour already covered via public API — may use heuristic + report)
- [ ] Verdicts are conservative: uncertainty returns report-to-user, never auto-remove
- [ ] Verdict reasoning is surfaced in structured output for the SKILL.md workflow and test-failure item comments

# Intake Brief: Audit skill Phase 2 (deep code analysis) — performance evaluation and improvement

## Problem statement

> **Headline:** The audit skill's Phase 2 deep code analysis frequently times out and is getting slower, because it makes N+1 sequential, unbounded tool-enabled Pi calls (parent + each child) that re-explore the whole repo; prior fixes only raised the per-call timeout (900→1200→1800s). Evaluate the Phase 2 call path, add per-call timing instrumentation for a baseline, and implement the top structural improvements (batching, scoping, reuse, parallelism) with tests.

The audit skill's Phase 2 (Deep Code Analysis) frequently times out and is taking longer and longer to execute. Historical fixes have been reactive — increasing `CALL_PI_TIMEOUT` from 900s → 1200s → 1800s (SA-0MS1SPGL3008G3BN, SA-0MS3FNIUA00385DE, SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9) — which masks the underlying inefficiency instead of reducing actual work. The runner needs a performance evaluation and structural improvements so audits complete reliably without ever-larger timeout bumps.

## Users

- **Release operators / producers** — run audits to gate work items for release; long-running or timed-out Phase 2 audits delay releases and require manual re-audits.
- **AI agents (e.g., Ralph, implement agents)** — invoke the audit runner programmatically in loops; a slow/timing-out Phase 2 stalls automated workflows.

User story: As a release operator, I want Phase 2 deep code analysis to complete reliably in bounded time so that audits do not time out and the release pipeline is not blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Evaluation report:** A written performance evaluation of Phase 2 (`_run_phase2_deep_analysis` and its call path in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) is produced, documenting how it works, where time is spent, and a prioritized list of improvement opportunities. Verified by: report exists in the work item (or linked child item) and is grounded in measured data from AC2 instrumentation.
- **AC2 — Timing instrumentation:** The audit runner logs per-call elapsed time (phase, call type — parent/child deep analysis — and issue id) to stderr/debug output, establishing a baseline for Phase 2 duration. Verified by: unit tests assert elapsed-time fields are emitted for Phase 2 calls, and a real or mocked run shows per-call timings.
- **AC3 — Improvements implemented:** At least the top-priority performance improvements identified in AC1 are implemented with tests written first (TDD), and Phase 2 wall-clock time is measurably reduced in tests/mocks (e.g., number of Pi subprocess calls reduced, or calls parallelized/batched, or exploration bounded). Verified by: unit tests asserting the new call pattern (e.g., reduced subprocess invocation count, scoped file manifest present in prompt, parallel execution where applicable).
- **AC4 — Regression safety:** The full audit test suite passes (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py`), including existing Phase 2 timeout/verdict behavior tests; no timeout increases beyond current 1800s default are required unless justified by the evaluation.
- **AC5 — Docs updated:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` documents any changed Phase 2 behavior, new flags/env vars, and the performance notes from the evaluation. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Model selection is out of scope** (per operator): keep the resolved audit model (default `Local Proxy/plan`, configurable via `.ralph.json` `model.audit`) fixed; focus only on reducing calls/exploration.
- The cumulative elapsed-time guard (hardcoded 110s) is being addressed in a separate open item (`Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable (SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X)`); changes here must not conflict with that work.
- Phase 2 verdict semantics are FINAL per the audit skill: verdicts "met" only when Phase 1 + Phase 2 both confirm; Phase 2 must not be skipped when the decision gate passes. Improvements may change *how* Phase 2 executes, not whether it executes or its authority.
- Use `wl` for all discovered sub-task tracking; create child work items for each improvement implemented (operator directive).
- All work-item descriptions/comments in Markdown; write tests before code; build → test → commit order.

## Existing state

- `_run_phase2_deep_analysis()` (audit_runner.py ~L1587) runs only when the Phase 1 decision gate passes.
- It makes **N+1 sequential agent-mode Pi calls** — one for the parent + one per active child — each a fresh `pi -p --mode json --model <m> --tools read,bash,grep,find,ls --exclude-tools ask_question` session.
- The Phase 2 prompt instructs the model to "read the actual implementation files" but provides **no file scope** (no Key Files manifest, no git diff, no repo index) → unbounded tool exploration (`find`/`grep`/`ls`/`read` across the whole repo) is the dominant cost.
- Per-call timeout: `CALL_PI_TIMEOUT = 1800` (raised 900→1200→1800 historically).
- Provider errors retried up to `_PI_MAX_RETRIES = 2` extra times with linear backoff; a provider error late in a long run restarts the entire call (worst case ~3 × 1800s).
- `cmd_issue` auto-triggers a **full child audit subprocess** for each child with a missing/stale audit (child gets its own Phase 1 + Phase 2), then parent Phase 2 re-runs deep analysis on those same children → duplicated child verification work.
- No per-call timing instrumentation exists today.

## Desired change

1. **Evaluate** — produce a measured analysis of Phase 2 (with AC2 instrumentation) and prioritize improvement levers.
2. **Implement** the top levers, with tests first. Candidate levers (to be confirmed by the evaluation):
   - **Batch**: fold active-child deep analysis into the parent Phase 2 call (single agent session, indexed AC list) instead of N+1 sessions.
   - **Reuse**: skip parent-Phase-2 child deep analysis for children whose own fresh child audit already produced a ready verdict (their Phase 2 already verified the code).
   - **Bound exploration**: inject a file-scope manifest (work-item Key Files + `git diff` / changed-file list + repo index) into the Phase 2 prompt and instruct the model to read only in-scope files; consider constraining `bash` to read-only commands.
   - **Parallelize**: run independent child deep-analysis calls concurrently with bounded concurrency (e.g., `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`).
   - **Feed Phase 1 evidence forward**: include Phase 1 file:line evidence in the Phase 2 prompt so the model verifies named files rather than re-exploring.
   - **Tune retries**: avoid full-call retries of provider errors on long agent-mode calls (retry once or degrade to partial instead).
3. **Instrument** per-call timing (AC2) so regressions are visible and the baseline is measurable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_phase2_deep_analysis`, `_call_pi`, `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, `cmd_issue` (child audit loop, elapsed guard); primary file for evaluation + changes.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — existing Phase 2/deep-analysis/timeout tests; new tests for instrumentation, batching, scope manifest, parallelism.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — documents Phase 2, timeout flags/env vars; must be updated for behavior changes (AC5).
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — persistence; only if report/child-persistence format changes.

## Related work

- `Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable (SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X)` (open) — sibling change to the same runner's time budget; related-to, avoid conflict.
- `Audit runner Phase 2 deep analysis timeout too short — Pi model call exceeds CALL_PI_TIMEOUT (SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9)` (completed) — prior timeout bump; context for why the bump pattern is insufficient.
- `Fix Phase 2 code review timeout (SA-0MS3FNIUA00385DE)` (completed) — graceful degradation + timeout increase.
- `Increase CALL_PI_TIMEOUT default from 900 to 1200 seconds (SA-0MS1SPGL3008G3BN)` (completed) — earlier timeout bump.
- `Audit Phase 2 instructs model to read files but runs in tool-less pipe mode (SA-0MS3HPN4I004KVNK)` (completed) — introduced tools-enabled agent mode that made Phase 2 slower; relevant history.
- `Find RCA and propose fix for audit_runner.py timeout (SA-0MQPQX57I0055ITT)` (completed) — earlier RCA attempt.
- Docs: `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (Phase 2, timeout configuration sections).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — verdict-quality regression:** Changing the Phase 2 call pattern (batching/parallelism/scope) could change verdict outcomes. Mitigation: preserve Phase 2 authority and verdict semantics; add tests asserting batched/parallel results match per-call behavior for the same ACs.
- **Risk — provider concurrency limits:** Parallel child calls against the local proxy may hit provider concurrency/rate limits. Mitigation: bounded concurrency (configurable cap), sequential fallback on failure.
- **Risk — oversized batch call:** Folding all children into one parent call increases prompt size and single-call duration. Mitigation: scope manifest keeps exploration bounded; instrumentation surfaces duration; fall back to per-child calls if the batch fails or times out.
- **Risk — scope creep:** Each improvement lever could expand into its own project. Mitigation: operator directive — create child work items for discovered sub-work; parent stays focused on evaluation + top-priority levers.
- **Assumption:** The dominant cost is (a) N+1 sequential agent-mode Pi calls and (b) unbounded repo exploration. To be confirmed by AC2 instrumentation.
- **Assumption:** The canonical audit skill is `skill/audit/` in this repo; the global `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` path is a symlink to it (verified identical, `diff -rq` clean).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Deliverable scope — investigation-only report, or investigate **and** implement the top improvements with tests?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "(b) implement; create child work items for work discovered." Source: interactive reply in intake session.
- Q: "Evidence anchor — do you have observed numbers, or should the item include timing instrumentation to establish a baseline?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "instrument" (add per-call timing instrumentation as part of the work). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should optimizing which model is used for deep verification be in scope?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "out of scope" (keep model fixed; focus on reducing calls/exploration). Source: interactive reply.

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSAAUJ1F0026BMN** – Create 'test' skill: run tests, triage failures, validate & fix test usefulness (open)
- **SA-0MS3G0D6A009TM81** – when running an audit the phase 2 code review doesn't always happen (completed)

## Summary

Audit agents (launched by `audit_runner.py` with `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls`) frequently run slow, recursive `grep -r` scans over `.worklog/` directories and project roots. On 2025-02-xx these scans consumed a full CPU core each for 7-20 minutes:

- `grep -l worklog-ref gate .worklog/audit_debug_WL-*.jsonl ...` — ran 17:54 at ~40% CPU
- `grep -rl CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR .worklog/` — ran 20:27 at ~36% CPU
- `grep -rln WL-0MS4FHW290053SH4 --include=*.jsonl --include=*.db .` — ran 7:55 at ~45% CPU

With many concurrent audits, this contributed to a load average of ~50-100 on a 16-core machine.

## Root cause

- `grep -r` recursively walks every file including huge `audit_debug_*.jsonl` files, node_modules, etc.
- No depth/prune limits, no binary skip, no use of faster tools (`rg`).
- Multiple audits run identical or overlapping scans concurrently.
- Agents sometimes scan from repo root (`.`) instead of the specific `.worklog/` path.

## Goal

Understand where these scans originate (audit prompt guidance in `skill/audit/`, agent tool usage patterns) and make audit scans **required and efficient only**:

- Only scan paths that must be scanned (avoid repo-root `grep -r .`).
- Use efficient scanning (e.g., `rg` with file-type/size filters, prune `node_modules`/git dirs, limit to `.worklog/` where appropriate).
- Avoid redundant concurrent scans when possible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A reproducible list of grep-scan patterns agents run during audits is documented (with origin file:line in the audit skill/prompt).
- [ ] Prompt/skill guidance updated so agents run targeted, bounded scans (specific paths, `rg` where available, prune filters) instead of unbounded `grep -r .`.
- [ ] No audit workflow step requires an unbounded recursive grep over the repo root or full `.worklog/` directory.
- [ ] Measurable: a representative audit (or set of audits) completes with significantly lower scan CPU-time than before (baseline: 7-20 min / ~40% CPU per scan).
- [ ] Tests/checks pass; no regression in audit evidence quality.

## Context

- Audit runner tool-enablement: `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (`--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls`), `audit_runner.py` lines ~499-515.
- Related: concurrent audit load also involves 100+ pi/vitest processes; this item is scoped to the grep scans only.
- discovered-from: resource-waste investigation on rgardler workstation (no originating work item).

# Intake Brief: Investigate concurrent audit fan-out causing extreme load (100+ pi processes)

## Problem statement

On the rgardler workstation, concurrent audits and agent sessions spawn a very large number of node processes. A snapshot showed **117 pi/vitest-related processes** plus ~6 concurrent `audit_runner.py` invocations (some with `--force`), multiple vitest worker pools (each spawning 15+ tinypool workers), and multiple `wl sync` runs. On a 16-core machine this drove load average to ~50-100 and pushed 2.7GB into swap.

## Users

- **Operator / workstation owner (rgardler):** wants the machine to stay responsive while multiple audits and agent sessions run in parallel.
- **Agents running batch workflows (implementall / audit batches):** want audits to complete in reasonable time without being serialized unnecessarily or thrashing the host.

User stories:
- "As an operator, I want concurrent audits to be bounded so my 16-core workstation stays responsive (load < 16, no swap) while several audits run."
- "As an agent, I want audits in a batch to finish quickly without contending with 100+ sibling processes."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Document the sources of concurrent pi/audit/vitest fan-out with origin file:line references.
- [ ] Introduce or document a concurrency control mechanism (e.g., audit queue/semaphore, vitest pool-size config, wl sync lock) that bounds concurrent heavy processes.
- [ ] Measurable: with the control in place, a typical batch of audits keeps load average under a defined threshold (e.g., < 16 on the 16-core machine) and avoids swap.
- [ ] No regression in audit throughput for normal workloads (batches still complete in reasonable time).
- [ ] Tests/checks pass.

## Constraints

- Changes must not serialize audits so aggressively that batch throughput regresses (AC: no regression for normal workloads).
- Concurrency control should be configurable (thresholds/limits as parameters), not hard-coded where practical.
- Scope is bounded: this item covers overall fan-out control; CPU sinks like grep scans are tracked separately (SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM).

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py` launches pi subprocesses with no obvious concurrency limit; multiple invocations run in parallel when multiple work items are audited concurrently (heartbeat/audit batch workflows, implementall-style loops, operator sessions, retries, `--force` reruns).
- Vitest runs spawn large tinypool worker pools (15+ workers per run) with no pool-size cap; ContextHub config currently sets `maxWorkers: 4` but this is per-project and not uniformly applied.
- `wl sync` runs concurrently from multiple sessions with no lock.
- Batch skills (implementall, intakeall, planall) process items sequentially by design, but each step can spawn heavy child processes; multiple batch runs can overlap.

## Desired change

- Identify and document each fan-out source with file:line references.
- Add a concurrency control mechanism (audit semaphore/queue, vitest pool-size config, wl sync lock) that bounds concurrent heavy processes and keeps load under a defined threshold.
- Validate measurably: run a typical batch and confirm load stays under threshold and no swap occurs, without throughput regression.

## Key Files

- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — launches pi subprocesses via `subprocess.Popen` (`_call_pi`, line ~527) and `--force` rerun path (~line 2303); no concurrency limit; primary candidate for an audit semaphore/queue.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/vitest.config.ts` — already sets `maxWorkers: 4`, `singleFork: true`; pattern reference for pool caps.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/vite.config.ts` — unit test project has NO worker cap (only replay-e2e uses `singleFork`); candidate for `maxWorkers`/`poolOptions` limit.
- SorraAgents — pytest-based (no vitest config exists); excluded from vitest capping.
- `wl sync` (Worklog CLI) — concurrent runs from multiple sessions; candidate for a sync lock. Source lives in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/cli.js` (globally installed as `worklog@1.0.6`, symlinked from `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog`).
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/process_semaphore.py` — planned new shared flock-based semaphore module for bounding concurrent heavy processes.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implementall/SKILL.md` — batch implementation loop; sequential by design but each step spawns heavy children; overlap can compound fan-out.
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/SKILL.md` — audit workflow doc; manages work item status to prevent concurrent audit attempts (status-based guard already exists — may be extendable to a concurrency guard).

## Related work

- **Optimize audit grep scans: only perform required and efficient scans (SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM)** — related-to: grep scans are one CPU sink; this item covers overall fan-out. Stage: idea/open.
- **Audit skill Phase 2 (deep code analysis): performance evaluation and improvement (SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D)** — in-progress; addresses N+1 sequential unbounded tool-enabled pi calls in Phase 2; related performance work.
- **Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable (SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X)** — open; extends parent-process timeout tolerance; adjacent audit_runner tuning.
- **Find RCA and propose fix for audit_runner.py timeout (SA-0MQPQX57I0055ITT)** — completed; prior audit_runner timeout RCA.
- **Fix mock-git processes stuck in infinite rev-parse CPU loop (SA-0MRO7C2S4002Y5DD)** — completed; prior CPU-loop/process runaway fix.
- discovered-from: resource-waste investigation on rgardler workstation (no originating work item).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The primary lever is bounding concurrent `audit_runner.py`/pi subprocesses; vitest pool and wl sync lock are secondary levers.
- **Risk:** A global audit semaphore could serialize batch audits and regress throughput — mitigated by configurable limits and per-workload tuning.
- **Risk:** Load spikes may come from operator-launched sessions (not agent code), which a semaphore cannot fully control — mitigation: document and cap automated sources; measure after control is in place.
- **Scope-creep risk:** grep-scan CPU sinks and Phase 2 performance are tracked in separate items; keep this item focused on fan-out bounding.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Was there an interview with the operator? — Answer (Map, from work item): No interactive interview was needed; the work item description already contains detailed evidence (process snapshot, PIDs, timestamps) and measurable ACs. Source: SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4 description, interactive reply at intake.
- Q: What is the desired concurrency ceiling? — Answer (Map, from work item): "e.g., < 16 on the 16-core machine" — threshold is defined as an example and expected to be finalized during implementation. Source: AC #3.
- Q: Should the concurrency control be a hard limit or documented guidance? — Answer (Map, from work item): AC #2 allows either "introduce or document" a mechanism. Source: AC #2.


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-08-01** — Planning completed by pi. Created 7 child work items (test-first ordering): fan-out source map + baseline harness, concurrency guard test suite, shared cross-process semaphore module, audit runner concurrency cap, wl sync serialization, vitest pool caps standardization, load validation & no-regression check. Decision: implement all three levers (audit semaphore, vitest caps, wl sync lock); minimize max-concurrency globally via a shared flock-based semaphore reused by audit_runner and wl sync; ceiling = concurrent invocations, configurable via env var. Dependency edges: F2→F1, F3→F2, F4→F3, F5→F3, F7→F4/F5/F6. Key Files section corrected (SorraAgents is pytest-based; wl sync source is ContextHub `dist/cli.js`).

## Summary

The ship release pipeline's audit gate blocks releases with work items from **other projects** that share the same worklog database. During the SorraAgents dev→main release, the gate flagged ContextHub (CG-*), Worklog/herdr (WL-*), and OSL-* items that are in_review or completed but belong to unrelated projects.

## Root cause

`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` → `getCandidateItems()` runs:

- `wl list --stage in_review --json`
- `wl list --status completed --json`

with **no project/prefix filter**. Worklog is a shared database (see `.worklog/config.yaml`: `projectName: Sorra Agents`, `prefix: SA`), and `wl list` returns items from every project. The same flaw exists in `check-critical-items.js` (`wl list --priority critical --json`).

Observed impact: the SorraAgents release was blocked by `WL-0MS9PL90F002MR8G` (global AGENTS.md path refs), `WL-0MSA9AM8S003UE7O` (herdr build failure), and `SA-0MSAAB9JL0016G1K` — items outside the SorraAgents project scope.

## User story

As a release manager running /skill:ship for the SorraAgents project, I want the audit gate to consider only work items belonging to the current project (prefix SA-), so that unrelated items in other projects' queues do not block my release.

## Expected behaviour

- Gate queries filter to the current project's items (by config prefix, e.g. `SA-`)
- Other projects' in_review/completed items never appear in the release gate report

## Suggested approach

1. Read the project prefix from `.worklog/config.yaml` (`prefix: SA`)
2. Filter `getCandidateItems()` results to ids starting with the prefix. Note: `wl list` exposes **no project-filter flag** (verified: only `--prefix` for overriding the default prefix, which is not a filter), so the filter must be applied in JS to the returned items
3. Apply the same filter in `check-critical-items.js`
4. Keep the transient-timeout warning behaviour unchanged

## Constraints

- Do not alter the existing audit-gate semantics beyond project scoping (readyToClose=true passes, genuine not-ready blocks, transient timeouts warn only)
- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` and `checkProducerReviewStatus()` consume `getCandidateItems()` output — the prefix filter in `getCandidateItems()` automatically scopes those downstream consumers too

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce: running `getCandidateItems()` in the SorraAgents repo returns only SA-* items
- [ ] Release gate report no longer lists CG-*/WL-*/OSL-* items from other projects
- [ ] check-critical-items.js is also scoped to the current project
- [ ] A release run (dry-run/gate-only) shows zero blocking items attributable to other projects
- [ ] Existing SorraAgents audit gating still works (readyToClose=true passes, genuine not-ready blocks, transient timeouts warn only)
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (including new unit tests for prefix scoping)
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems()`: add prefix filtering on the `wl list` results; also add unit-test support for injecting a project prefix
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-critical-items.js` — `checkCriticalItems()`: apply the same prefix filter to the `wl list --priority critical --json` results
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` — add tests asserting only items matching the current project prefix are returned
- `tests/unit/test-check-critical-items.mjs` — add tests asserting the critical-items gate ignores foreign-prefix items
- `.worklog/config.yaml` — source of the `prefix` value (read at runtime; not modified)

## Related work (manual)

- `SA-0MS4TJR2R0043UHO` — Extend getCandidateItems and add checkProducerReviewStatus: most recent change to the same `getCandidateItems()` function; the prefix filter must not break the `needsProducerReview` field extraction it added
- `SA-0MS21B5MP004AUUS` — Close work items after release only when readyToClose and producerReview conditions are met: depends on the same candidate set
- `SA-0MS4TXDPG003OFYO` — Filter closeWorkItemsAfterRelease by needsProducerReview: downstream consumer of `getCandidateItems()`
- `SA-0MS4TXDPB003EUKA` — Add producer-review gating step to run-release.js: gate-ordering context in `run-release.js`
- `SA-0MS95HJ0J004IDIW` — Increase audit gate timeout to prevent false release blocks: prior audit-gate fix; keep transient-timeout behaviour intact

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS0QF0Z4006MJPM** – Create shared status_lifecycle.py module with tests (completed)
- **SA-0MS3AVBGZ0040HH3** – [MEDIUM] lint: single `if` instead of nested (SIM102) (completed)
- **SA-0MS3AVB6D007BMKK** – [MEDIUM] lint: `key in dict` instead of `dict.keys()` (SIM118) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/docs/ralph.md` — matched audit/gate/ship keywords
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched audit/gate keywords
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/docs/workflow/engine-prd.md` — matched audit/gate/ship keywords

> Note: the automated report matches are keyword-based and low signal; the manual related-work list above carries the real dependencies.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the project prefix (`SA-`) is read from `.worklog/config.yaml` at runtime; if the config is missing/unreadable, the gate should fail safe (block rather than silently scan all projects).
- **Assumption:** filtering by ID prefix is sufficient to scope to the current project; no cross-prefix aliasing exists in the worklog data.
- **Risk:** a fix that filters inside `getCandidateItems()` changes behaviour for downstream consumers (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, `checkProducerReviewStatus`) — desired here, but must be covered by tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** unrelated audit-gate improvements (e.g., new gates, ordering changes) are out of scope; record them as separate work items rather than expanding this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does `wl list` support a native project/prefix filter we can pass to the CLI? — Answer (verification by agent Map): No. `wl list --help` shows `--prefix <prefix>` only overrides the default prefix used when creating new items; it is not a filter on the returned set. Source: `wl list --help` output, checked 2026-08-01. Consequence: the fix must filter returned items in JS.
- Q: Do the two gate scripts currently contain any project scoping? — Answer (verification by agent Map): No. `check-audit-gate.js` (queries `wl list --stage in_review --json` and `wl list --status completed --json`) and `check-critical-items.js` (queries `wl list --priority critical --json`) contain no prefix/project filter. Source: grep of `skill/ship/scripts/`, checked 2026-08-01.
- Q: Does the current repo state reproduce foreign-prefix items? — Answer (verification by agent Map): A direct run of `getCandidateItems()` in the SorraAgents repo currently returns only SA-* items (23 candidates, all SA). The shared-database foreign items are present in the worklog remote refs and were observed during the release run described in the issue; the gate remains unguarded against them. This reinforces the need for an explicit, testable prefix filter rather than relying on ambient data state.

## Summary

Add elapsed-time instrumentation to the Phase 2 deep-analysis call path in the audit runner so a performance baseline is measurable and regressions are visible. This is the measurement foundation for the parent item (Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement, SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D).

From evaluation report docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md (SA-0MSAHR63100415PM): duplicated child verification — cmd_issue auto-audits children, then parent Phase 2 deep-analyses the same children again.

Skip parent-Phase-2 child deep analysis for children whose own fresh child audit already produced a ready verdict (child_audit_ready=True). Children with child_audit_ready=False still require parent deep analysis.

# Phase 2: parallelize independent child calls (P3)

From evaluation report docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md (SA-0MSAHR63100415PM): child deep-analysis calls are strictly sequential (plain for loop); wall-clock = N x per-call.

## Goal
Run independent child deep-analysis calls concurrently with bounded concurrency (concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor), configurable cap via env var (default 2-3, implementer judgment per operator). Parent call stays first (defines scope). Sequential fallback on failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Child calls in _run_phase2_deep_analysis run concurrently with a bounded cap (default per implementer judgment, configurable via env var).
- AC2: Sequential fallback: if the executor path fails (provider error/timeout), child results degrade to partial exactly as today (no behavior regression).
- AC3: Parent call runs first and is not parallelized with children.
- AC4: Verdict/evidence semantics unchanged; per-child isolation preserved.
- AC5: skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py asserts bounded concurrency (e.g., max in-flight calls <= cap) and sequential fallback; full audit + project test suites pass.

# Phase 2: retry tuning for long agent-mode calls (P5)

From evaluation report docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md (SA-0MSAHR63100415PM): a provider error on a long Phase 2 call restarts the entire call (up to 2 extra attempts with backoff), worst case ~3 x 1800s per call.

## Goal
Cap or avoid full-call provider-error retries on long Phase 2 agent-mode calls: retry once, or degrade to partial with a provider-error diagnostic instead of restarting the entire call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Long Phase 2 agent-mode calls (phase2_deep / phase2_child) do NOT restart the full call on provider error beyond a bounded number of retries (1 max, per evaluation).
- AC2: On persistent provider error the ACs degrade to partial with the existing provider-error diagnostic evidence (unchanged semantics).
- AC3: Short calls (Phase 1 bare calls) keep existing retry behavior (_PI_MAX_RETRIES=2) unless the change is proven safe for them too.
- AC4: skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py asserts the retry count bound for agent-mode Phase 2 calls; full audit + project test suites pass.
- AC5: No increase to the default per-call timeout (CALL_PI_TIMEOUT remains exactly 1800s); operator overrides via --timeout / AUDIT_PI_TIMEOUT remain supported and documented in SKILL.md.

## Dependencies
- SA-0MSAHQZN4004ZFKQ (timing instrumentation) - complete
- SA-0MSAHR63100415PM (evaluation report) - complete

## Summary

Document every source of concurrent pi/audit/vitest/wl-sync fan-out with origin file:line references (AC #1) and provide a measurement script that captures process counts and load during a typical batch run, establishing the baseline for AC #3/#4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A markdown source map documents each fan-out source with file:line references:
  - `audit_runner.py::_call_pi` (L527) — unbounded `subprocess.Popen` of pi per model call.
  - `audit_runner.py` nested child-trigger path (L2290-2310) — parent audit spawns `audit_runner issue --force` per child via `subprocess.run`.
  - Vitest tinypool worker pools — ContextHub capped (`maxWorkers: 4`), Tableau-Card-Engine unit project uncapped (only replay-e2e uses `singleFork`).
  - `wl sync` — no lock, concurrent runs possible.
  - Batch-skill overlap (implementall/intakeall/planall) — sequential per item but each step spawns heavy children.
- [ ] A measurement script (e.g., `skills/shared/measure_fanout.py`) records: timestamp, per-type process counts (pi, vitest/tinypool, wl sync), load average, and swap usage.
- [ ] Script outputs machine-readable JSON and a human summary; runs non-intrusively (no side effects).
- [ ] A baseline run is captured (JSON artifact + comment on this item) documenting the observed 100+ process / load ~50-100 state.
- [ ] Source map lives with the audit skill docs (`skills/audit/` or `docs/`) and is linked from the parent.

## Minimal Implementation

- Inspect `audit_runner.py` (L489-560 `_call_pi`, L2290-2310 child trigger) and confirm exact line refs.
- Inspect vitest configs: ContextHub `vitest.config.ts`, Tableau-Card-Engine `vite.config.ts`.
- Write source-map doc with table of origin file:line + mechanism.
- Write `measure_fanout.py` using `psutil` (or `ps`/`/proc`) to enumerate `pi`, `node`, `tinypool`, `wl` processes and `os.getloadavg()`, `free` for swap.
- Run once to capture baseline.

## Dependencies

None (first).

## Deliverables

- Source-map doc (file:line refs).
- `measure_fanout.py` measurement script.
- Baseline JSON artifact + comment.

# Concurrency guard test suite

## Summary

Write tests (before implementation) that assert concurrent audit_runner and wl sync invocations are bounded to the configured maximum, driving the design of the shared semaphore.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test launches N (e.g., 8) concurrent `audit_runner.py issue` invocations and asserts active pi/audit process count never exceeds the configured maximum.
- [ ] Test asserts waiting invocations proceed once a slot frees (no deadlock, no starvation for a small bounded wait).
- [ ] Test asserts concurrent `wl sync` invocations serialize (max 1 active at a time).
- [ ] Test verifies configurable ceiling via env var (e.g., `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) takes effect.
- [ ] Tests are runnable via the standard test runner and pass after implementation features land.

## Minimal Implementation

- Use a lockfile-based counter or instrument the semaphore API to report active count.
- Spawn real subprocesses in a controlled test harness (temporary worklog dir / fake `wl` shim where needed).
- Keep test wall-time bounded (< 2 min) using small timeouts and short pi shims (mock pi binary).

## Dependencies

Depends on: Fan-out source map + baseline harness.

## Deliverables

- Test suite (Python, pytest) in `skills/shared/tests/`.

# Shared cross-process semaphore module

## Summary

Implement a flock-based counting semaphore in `skills/shared/` that bounds concurrent heavy processes across sessions, configurable via environment variable, and reused by audit_runner and wl sync.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Module provides `acquire()`/`release()` semantics with a configurable max-concurrency (env var, e.g., `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, default 2 concurrent audit invocations).
- [ ] Uses advisory file lock (e.g., `fcntl.flock` on a lockfile in `/tmp` or `.worklog`) so it works across independent processes and sessions.
- [ ] Lock released on normal exit, error, and signal (SIGINT/SIGTERM) — no stale locks.
- [ ] Configurable wait (block with timeout, or fail-fast option).
- [ ] Unit tests pass (acquire/release, max bound, timeout, cleanup).

## Minimal Implementation

- New module `skills/shared/process_semaphore.py` (or similar) — counting semaphore backed by a lockfile + flock.
- Export a small API: `Semaphore(name, max_workers, timeout)` with context-manager support.
- Config via env var with sane default; document override.
- Unit tests mirroring the guard test suite API.

## Dependencies

Depends on: Concurrency guard test suite (tests define the contract).

## Deliverables

- `process_semaphore.py` + unit tests.
- Env-var configuration documented in module docstring.

## Summary

The audit runner's status lifecycle (audit_runner.py) leaves work items stuck at `in-progress` status after an audit. The runner sets status to `in_progress` at audit start and restores the original status in a `try/finally` block, but the restore is best-effort and failures are silently caught. In the v0.1.9 release of llm-manager (2026-08-01), 7 child work items were left at `in-progress` after their audits completed.

## Impact

The release's `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` step calls `wl close`, which recursively closes children only when they are audit-ready/in a terminal state. Because 7 children were stuck at `in-progress`, the recursive close on affected parents did not complete, leaving 13 items in `completed`/`in_review` after the release finished. An operator had to manually restore the 7 children to `completed`/`in_review` and re-close the 13 items.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id>` on an item whose original status is `completed` (or any status other than `in_progress`).
2. Observe that on completion, the item's status is left as `in_progress` instead of the original status.
3. Attempt `wl close <parent-id>` where the parent has children audited this way — recursive close fails/skips because children are not terminal.

## Suggested investigation

- audit_runner.py: status lifecycle capture/restore logic (`cmd_issue` — capture original status, set `in_progress`, restore in `finally`).
- The restore step catches errors silently; it should log a warning when restoration fails so the operator is aware.
- Consider verifying restoration via `wl show` after audit and reporting failures loudly.
- wl close recursive-close behavior: consider whether it should fail loudly when children are non-terminal rather than silently leaving the parent open.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After running an audit on an item with original status `completed`, the item's status is restored to `completed` (not left as `in_progress`).
2. If status restoration fails, a visible warning/error is logged (not silently swallowed).
3. A release's `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` step closes all `completed`/`in_review` items, including parents with audited children, in a single pass.

## Related

- discovered-from: llm-manager release v0.1.9 (PR #16)
- Issue type: bug, priority: high
data.title: Audit runner status lifecycle leaves work items stuck at in-progress, breaking release close step

## Summary

During an implement run on ContextHub work item WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST (2026-08-01 17:01 +0100), the pi agent hit the implement safety gate for uncommitted changes and chose to run:

`git stash push -m "Stash unrelated changes" -- packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`

This stashed the USER's uncommitted, user-authored edits (herdr shortcuts dialog syntax for c/r/s/u+t) and never restored them. The edits were later recovered from stash@{0} by another session and committed (ContextHub commit 6491ec59), but the pattern is dangerous: an agent silently moved user work out of the working tree.

## Why it happened

- `implement.py start` safety gate (line ~943) reports: "Please stash, commit, or revert changes before proceeding." — the agent interpreted this as permission to stash on the user's behalf without asking.
- The stash message "Stash unrelated changes" with no follow-up restore or reporting.

## Desired behavior

- When uncommitted changes exist at implement start, the agent must STOP and ask the operator how to proceed (commit? stash? abort?) — never stash/commit/revert user changes unilaterally.
- If the skill script itself performs a stash, it must restore it on completion (or clearly report it to the operator with instructions to restore).
- Consider updating the safety-gate message to say "ask the operator" instead of listing stash as an option the agent may execute.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The implement skill guidance (SKILL.md and/or implement.py safety gate) instructs agents to ask the operator before touching uncommitted changes, and explicitly forbids stashing user changes without permission.
- [ ] No agent-initiated stash of user changes occurs in subsequent implement runs.

## Problem statement

The audit skill's canonical runner, `audit_runner.py`, fails immediately at the start of `cmd_issue()` with a status-lifecycle error:

```
RuntimeError: wl command failed (wl update OSL-0MSABC7SB001NVUN --status in_progress --json):
(empty stderr)
Command exited with code 1
```

The runner then crashes instead of producing an audit report. `wl update <id> --status in_progress --json` works when run manually from the project directory, so the failure is in how the runner invokes wl (likely cwd resolution of the worklog store, env, or argument construction).

## User story

As an agent running /skill:audit, I want the canonical runner to complete the audit lifecycle without crashing, so I don't have to fall back to the manual audit path.

## Repro

1. Run `python3 ./scripts/audit_runner.py issue OSL-0MSABC7SB001NVUN --do-not-persist` from the audit skill directory (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`).
2. Observe the RuntimeError above; no audit report is produced.
3. Run `wl update OSL-0MSABC7SB001NVUN --status in_progress --json` manually from the project dir — succeeds.

Note: the audit skill scripts live under `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/` (the ~/.pi path symlinks there); the runner resolves its own script dir as cwd, so `wl` resolves the wrong worklog store (SorraAgents instead of the target project) or fails for another reason.

## Root cause (verified during intake)

Confirmed by reproduction on 2026-08-01:

- `_run_wl` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 205) runs `wl` via the default runner, which is `subprocess.run(cmd, check=False, text=True, capture_output=True)` with **no `cwd`**. The subprocess therefore inherits the audit runner's cwd.
- When the runner is launched from the audit skill directory, wl resolves the **wrong worklog store** — `wl update` exits 1 with `Work item not found: OSL-...` printed to **stdout** (not stderr), which is why `_run_wl` reports `(empty stderr)`.
- `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` / `_detect_project_root()` already exist in the runner but are only used for the debug log path and code-quality invocation — **not** to set the cwd of `wl` subprocesses or to inject `--worklog-dir`.

Fix candidates (verified feasible):

- **Preferred:** route the runner's wl invocations through the shared `run_wl` helper in `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`, which already implements cwd-independent wl invocation by injecting `--worklog-dir` when the caller's cwd is not the target worklog root (see commit `53dee47` "Make skill wl invocations cwd-independent"). This also aligns with the previously-completed adoption of `StatusLifecycle` in the runner (commit `315e894`), which was later rewritten back to the inline `_run_wl` lifecycle.
- Alternatively, pass `cwd=TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` (or explicit `--worklog-dir`) in `_default_runner`/`_run_wl`.
- At minimum, when wl fails, surface the actual stderr/stdout diagnostic instead of `(empty stderr)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `audit_runner.py issue <id> --do-not-persist` completes the status lifecycle (capture → in_progress → restore) without crashing for an item in a different project's worklog.
- [ ] The runner either resolves the correct worklog store (target project cwd or explicit --worklog-dir) or produces a clear diagnostic instead of an empty-stderr RuntimeError.
- [ ] Full audit flow (Phase 1 + Phase 2 + persistence) works end-to-end from any cwd.
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover the status-lifecycle step from a non-project cwd.

## Constraints

- The runner must work when launched from the audit skill directory (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`, symlinked to `SorraAgents/skill/audit/`), auditing work items in *other* projects' worklogs.
- The `--do-not-persist` flag and the persist+readback invariant must be preserved.
- All work-item status transitions must go through the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (per framework rules); ad-hoc `wl update --status` in the runner is the current defect pattern.

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py` `cmd_issue()` captures `original_status` via `wl show`, sets `in_progress` via a direct `_run_wl(["wl", "update", ...])` call (~line 2309), and restores it in the `finally` block (~line 2873).
- `_run_wl` runs wl with inherited cwd → resolves wrong store when launched outside the target project.
- The shared helper `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` already provides `run_wl(cmd)` that injects `--worklog-dir` when cwd is not a worklog root — the same fix mechanism proven in commit `53dee47` (effort-and-risk skill).

## Desired change

- Make all `wl` invocations in `audit_runner.py` cwd-independent (shared `run_wl` helper or explicit `cwd`/`--worklog-dir`), and improve the failure diagnostic so empty-stderr RuntimeErrors cannot recur.
- Re-align the status lifecycle with the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (restore or supersede the inline capture/restore).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_wl` (~line 205, default runner with no `cwd`); `cmd_issue()` lifecycle (`wl update ... in_progress` ~line 2309; restore ~line 2873). Primary fix location.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — shared `run_wl` helper with `--worklog-dir` injection; reuse target.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — existing tests incl. `_detect_project_root` fallback; add cwd-independence tests for the lifecycle step.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — documents manual fallback audit path; update once runner is fixed.

## Related work

# Audit skill must write audit report files with unique names (audit_report_<id>.md) not a fixed /tmp/audit_report.md

## Problem statement

Audit report persistence is vulnerable to cross-work-item contamination: report content written to (or read from) a fixed/shared file path can be persisted to the wrong work item. The observed incident (2026-08-01): while auditing `OSL-0MSABC7SB001NVUN`, a stale `/tmp/audit_report.md` left over from a previous CG-synergy audit was read via `persist_audit.py --file /tmp/audit_report.md` and persisted, overwriting the correct audit for `OSL-0MSABC7SB001NVUN` with unrelated content. The contamination was detected only by manual readback comparison.

**Research note (intake, 2026-08-02):** The current audit skill code does NOT hardcode `/tmp/audit_report.md` — `audit_runner.py` passes report text directly to `persist_audit()`, and `persist_audit.py --file` accepts any user-supplied path. The vulnerability is therefore (a) an unguarded manual/agent workflow that can reuse a fixed file path, and (b) the absence of an identity check before persisting: nothing verifies that the report text actually belongs to the target work item. `audit_pr.py` already uses unique names (`.pi/tmp/audit-result-<wl_id>.json`).

## Users

- **Agents and operators running audits** across multiple projects or concurrently (e.g. project audits, CG-synergy workflows).
- **Release reviewers** who rely on `wl audit-show` returning the correct, work-item-specific audit content.

User stories:

- *As an agent running audits for multiple work items, I want each audit's report file to be uniquely named per work item, so audits never clobber each other.*
- *As an operator, I want the persister to refuse a report that clearly belongs to a different work item, so a stale report can never be persisted to the wrong item.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The audit skill never writes or reads audit report content via a fixed shared path (e.g. `/tmp/audit_report.md`); any file-based persistence uses a unique name per work item (e.g. `/tmp/audit_report_<id>.md`), and the unique-name convention is documented in `SKILL.md`.
- [ ] Concurrent or sequential audits of different work items never overwrite each other's report files.
- [ ] `persist_audit.py` (and the runner's persist path) performs an identity check: report text that clearly references a different work item than the target `--issue-id` is rejected with a clear error and a non-zero exit code, rather than persisted.
- [ ] Readback verification confirms the stored audit matches the intended work item after persistence (content identity check, not just non-empty storage).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: mismatched report rejected, matching report persisted, unique file naming, and readback identity verification.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the audit `SKILL.md`.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

> Note: CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the documentation list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken the existing readback-verification invariant (persist + verify is unconditional in the runner).
- The identity check must be conservative: it may reject clearly mismatched reports but must not reject valid reports (e.g. reports that legitimately mention other work items in passing, such as child-work-item audit sections).
- No changes to the `wl` CLI itself; the guard lives in the audit skill's Python code.

## Existing state

- `persist_audit.py` accepts report text via `--report`, stdin, or `--file` with no identity validation before calling `wl audit-set`.
- The runner's readback (`wl audit-show`) checks only that the stored audit is non-null and has non-empty `rawOutput`/`summary`; it does not compare the stored content with the report that was persisted.
- `SKILL.md` documents `--file report.md` usage without a unique-naming convention; the runner and persister do not share any fixed report file path today.

## Desired change

- Add an identity guard in `persist_audit()` (single choke point used by both the CLI and the runner) that checks the report text references the target work item ID before persisting; reject with a clear error otherwise.
- Optionally strengthen the runner's readback to compare the stored `rawOutput` with the persisted report text (content identity), per AC4.
- Document the unique file-naming convention (`audit_report_<id>.md`) for any file-based persistence in `SKILL.md`.
- Add tests for the guard, naming convention, and readback identity.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — Add the identity guard in `persist_audit()` (and expose a toggle for strictness if needed); validate `--file`/`--report`/stdin content before persisting.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Strengthen readback verification to confirm the stored audit matches the intended work item (content identity), and pass report text through the same guard.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Document the unique file-naming convention for file-based persistence and the identity guard behavior.
- `skill/audit/tests/` (e.g. `tests/test_persist_audit_identity.py`) — New tests: mismatched report rejected; matching report persisted; unique naming; readback identity verification.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRY2BKEA008XCWD` — Audit runner readback verification fails when rawOutput is null (completed): established the readback-verification invariant that AC4 builds on.
- `SA-0MRY4L8H7005X9HV` — Readback verification test expects wrong error message for null audit (completed).
- `SA-0MSAXHMZT009EHVV` / `SA-0MSAXHUMM002PMEW` — cwd-independent `wl` invocation and real diagnostics (completed): the worklog-dir plumbing used by the persister.
- `discovered-from: OSL-0MSABC7SB001NVUN` — wiki-tts-generate health check bug whose audit was contaminated in the incident.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The identity guard uses work-item-ID presence in the report text as the matching signal; a report that does not mention the target ID is treated as a mismatch candidate.
- **Risk:** Over-strict matching could reject valid reports (e.g. audits that reference only child IDs). Mitigation: make the guard conservative (reject only when the report references a *different* known work-item ID, or when the target ID is absent AND a different ID is present); log a warning otherwise.
- **Risk:** The runner persists child audits that legitimately focus on child IDs — the guard must not break child persistence.
- **Scope-creep:** Deeper audit-store integrity features (e.g. checksums, provenance fields) are out of scope and should be tracked as separate work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The ACs assume the skill currently writes to a fixed `/tmp/audit_report.md`. Research (2026-08-02) shows the current code does not hardcode this path — the incident came from a manual workflow using `persist_audit.py --file /tmp/audit_report.md`. Should the fix be (a) an identity guard preventing mismatched report persistence, (b) documentation of unique naming only, or (c) both?
  - Answer: Both (c) — the guard directly prevents the contamination class of bug and the doc convention formalizes the fix. Recorded by the intake agent; no user clarification requested because the item's intent (prevent cross-audit contamination, verified readback) is unambiguous and all options are compatible with the stated ACs.

# Intake Brief — Audit completion must transition work-item status: `open` (readyToClose: no) or `completed` (readyToClose: yes)

## Problem statement

The audit skill/runner currently forbids changing a work item's `stage` ("Do NOT change `stage`") and its status lifecycle only **restores the pre-audit status** (capture original → set `in_progress` → restore original in `finally`). As a result, a passing audit never advances the item into the producer-review queue, and a failing audit never returns it to the actionable queue. Items end up in inconsistent states that require manual reconciliation.

**Live example:** `wl sync lock storm (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E)` (ContextHub worklog) passed audit with `Ready to close: Yes` but was left at `status: in-progress` / `stage: in_review` — the inconsistent `in-progress`/`in_review` combination means the item is invisible to the herdr producer-review queue (which shows `completed`/`in_review` items), and its status must be fixed by hand. The audit verdict (`readyToClose: yes` in `audit_results`) is stored, but the item's lifecycle fields contradict it.

## Users

- **Producers/operators** reviewing audited work items — expect a passed audit to flow the item into the review queue (`completed`/`in_review`) and a failed audit to return it to `open`, without manual status fixes.
- **Agents and orchestrators** consuming audit verdicts — the item's `status`/`stage` should reflect the verdict so downstream tools (herdr worklist, `wl next`, review queues) behave correctly.

User story: "As an operator, I want the audit to leave the work item in a state consistent with its verdict, so that a passed audit lands in the review queue as `completed` and a failed audit returns to the queue as `open`."

## Expected behaviour

When an **item-level audit** completes:

1. **`Ready to close: Yes`** → the work item is left with `status: completed` (and `stage: in_review` when the stage is not already terminal e.g. `done`), regardless of the pre-audit status.
2. **`Ready to close: No`** → the work item is left with `status: open` and `stage: plan_complete` (fixed pre-review stage), regardless of the pre-audit status.

The audit must never leave an item stuck in `in_progress`/`in_progress` or `in-progress`/`in_review` after completing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id>` on an item whose stage is `in_review` and status `in-progress` (e.g. WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E in the ContextHub worklog).
2. Observe: audit persists `readyToClose: yes`, but the item remains `status: in-progress` — the runner's `finally` block restored the pre-audit status instead of setting `completed`.

## Suggested implementation approach

- **`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`**
  - Replace the "restore original status" `finally` block (~lines 2868–2881) with a **verdict-driven transition**: `readyToClose == yes` → `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (only when current stage is not `done`); `readyToClose == no` → `wl update <id> --status open --stage plan_complete`.
  - Failure/timeout/parse-error paths: never leave the item `in_progress` — restore a safe consistent state (e.g. original status, or `open` when the verdict could not be determined) and **clear the assignee** so the item returns fully to the actionable queue. If the verdict is unknown, do NOT blindly set `completed`/`open` based on an unparsed verdict.
  - Freshness-gate skip must continue to perform **no** lifecycle transitions.
  - Child audits (auto-triggered per child) get the same verdict-driven transition.
- **`skill/audit/SKILL.md`**
  - Remove the rule "Do NOT change `stage`" (line 78) and rewrite the "Status Lifecycle" section: capture → `in_progress` → verdict-driven terminal state (`completed`/`in_review` on yes, `open`/`plan_complete` on no), with failure fallback (safe state + assignee cleared).
  - Update the "Safety and prompt design" section accordingly.
- **AGENTS.md (both `SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` and `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`)**
  - Remove the second sentence from the parent-status rule (~line 106): "The parent's status should remain `in-progress` until formal post-release closure." — so that parents can reach `completed`/`in_review` consistent with the verdict-driven audit transition. (Decision: in-scope for this work item.)
- **Consider reusing `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`** (`StatusLifecycle`) — it already implements `completed`/restore semantics and clears the assignee on failure exit; the runner currently duplicates the lifecycle inline. Evaluate whether the verdict-driven transition should become a new option on `StatusLifecycle` (e.g. `terminal_status`) or stay in the runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an item-level audit completes with `Ready to close: Yes`, the work item is left with `status: completed` (and `stage: in_review` when not already `done`), regardless of its pre-audit status.
2. When an item-level audit completes with `Ready to close: No`, the work item is left with `status: open` and `stage: plan_complete`, regardless of its pre-audit status.
3. The "Do NOT change `stage`" rule is removed from `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and the runner; the status lifecycle documentation reflects the verdict-driven behavior.
4. On audit failure, timeout, or unparseable verdict, the item is never left `in_progress`; it is restored to a safe consistent state, its assignee is cleared, and the failure is reported.
5. Freshness-gate skips perform no status/stage transitions (unchanged behavior).
6. Re-auditing is idempotent: yes→yes stays `completed`; yes→no moves to `open`/`plan_complete`; no→yes moves to `completed`/`in_review`.
7. Audit persistence + readback verification still succeed (verdict stored in `audit_results`).
8. The parent-status rule in both `SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` and `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` no longer keeps parents `in-progress` until release (second sentence removed at ~line 106).
9. Runner tests cover verdict→status transitions (including failure and skip paths) and all `skill/audit` + project test suites pass.

## Constraints

- `wl` CLI validates `completed` status against stage (`in_review`/`done` only) — the runner must set a compatible stage together with `completed`.
- Verdict-driven transitions apply to item-level audits (`issue` subcommand) and their auto-triggered child audits only; project-level audits (`project` subcommand) have no single work item.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` captures `original_status` (~lines 2295–2309), sets `in_progress`, and restores the original status in a `finally` block (~lines 2868–2881) — no stage transitions ever occur.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` line 78: "Do NOT change `stage`" rule.
- Both AGENTS.md files contain: "The parent's status should remain `in-progress` until formal post-release closure." (~line 106).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (`StatusLifecycle`) already provides `completed`/restore/`restore_on_exit` semantics and clears the assignee on failure exit.

## Desired change

- Verdict-driven terminal state on audit completion: `completed`/`in_review` on yes, `open`/`plan_complete` on no; safe state + assignee cleared on failure; no transitions on freshness-skip.
- Remove "Do NOT change `stage`" rule from SKILL.md and runner; align AGENTS.md parent-status rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — verdict-driven status transition; capture original stage alongside status; failure fallback; assignee clearing.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — remove "Do NOT change `stage`" rule; rewrite Status Lifecycle section.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — candidate for reuse/extension (`terminal_status` option); runner currently duplicates lifecycle inline.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update/add lifecycle transition tests (yes/no/failure/skip/idempotent).
- `SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` and `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` — remove second sentence of parent-status rule (~line 106).

## Related work

- `wl sync lock storm (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E)` (ContextHub worklog) — the live instance of the bug: passed audit left the item `in-progress`/`in_review`; `related-to`.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — shared lifecycle helper with `completed`/restore/`restore_on_exit` semantics; candidate for reuse or extension.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` lines ~2295–2309 (entry lifecycle) and ~2868–2881 (restore `finally`).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` line 78 ("Do NOT change `stage`") and the "Status Lifecycle" section.
- Related completed work items: "Audit runner: manage work item status during audit execution (SA-0MQJONW3C007SZQY)", "Adopt shared lifecycle helper in audit runner (SA-0MS0QF0ZA00926GH)".

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Setting `completed`/`in_review` on a failing re-audit of an already-`completed` item must still allow demotion to `open` (AC 6) — the transition must not be gated on current status.
- **Risk:** `wl` CLI validates `completed` status against stage (`in_review`/`done` only) — the runner must set a compatible stage together with `completed`.
- **Decision (resolved):** For `Ready to close: No`, stage is set to a fixed `plan_complete` (not the captured pre-audit stage).
- **Decision (resolved):** On audit failure, the item's assignee is cleared.
- **Decision (resolved):** AGENTS.md parent-status rule update is in-scope for this work item (both copies).
- **Scope:** Project-level audits (`project` subcommand) have no single work item — verdict-driven transitions apply to item-level audits (`issue`) and their auto-triggered child audits only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Related opportunities (e.g. broader StatusLifecycle refactor) should be tracked as separate work items, not expanded here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "AGENTS.md conflict scope — should updating the AGENTS.md parent-status rule (remove 'The parent's status should remain in-progress until formal post-release closure.') be included in this work item?" — Answer (operator, interactive): **A — include updating both AGENTS.md files in this work item's scope/ACs.**
- Q2: "For 'Ready to close: No', should the stage revert to the pre-audit stage captured at entry, or a fixed pre-review stage (e.g. plan_complete)?" — Answer (operator, interactive): **Fixed `plan_complete`.**
- Q3: "Should a failed audit clear the item's assignee (returning it fully to the actionable queue) or keep the assignee?" — Answer (operator, interactive): **Clear it.**

Implement `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py`, a small CLI helper that replaces agent-decided recursive grep/find scans with bounded, required-and-efficient operations:

- `scan.py find-workitem <id>` — delegates to `wl search`/single-file `wl show` instead of grepping the 9.5 GB `.worklog/` tree.
- `scan.py search-code <pattern> [path]` — bounded rg wrapper with fixed prunes, size cap, and explicit path (never repo-root default).
- `scan.py list-files [path]` — bounded find with maxdepth + prunes.

## Why

Agents improvise slow `grep -r`/unbounded `find` during Phase 2. A first-class helper gives them a fast, safe, testable alternative the prompts can point to.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `find-workitem` returns the work item via `wl search`/JSON; never performs recursive grep over `.worklog/`; exits non-zero with a clear message when not found.
- [ ] `search-code` invokes rg with prunes for `node_modules`, `.git`, `.worklog`, `**/audit_debug_*.jsonl`; enforces a max file size and bounded match output; requires an explicit path argument (defaults to project root only when explicitly allowed).
- [ ] `list-files` applies maxdepth (default 2) and the same prunes; does not descend into node_modules/.git/.worklog.
- [ ] Degrades gracefully when rg is unavailable (falls back to bounded grep with same prunes, or clear error).
- [ ] No network access; stdlib + wl/rg only; `--help` documents subcommands and defaults.
- [ ] Tests from SA-0MSBR0E8Y0022Z4V pass against this implementation.

- Single module `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` (~150-200 lines) with argparse subcommands.
- Reuse `_default_runner`-style subprocess conventions from `audit_runner.py`.
- Wire nothing into prompts yet (that is the next item).

# Lower critical to high priority before persisting audit when readyToClose: Yes

## Problem statement

When a work item is audited as `readyToClose: Yes` and still carries `critical` priority, it remains marked critical even though the audit signals it is ready to be closed. This inflates the critical priority queue with items that are effectively resolved.

## Users

- **Operator / Release Manager:** Needs a clean critical queue that only contains genuinely urgent open items.
- **Agent (Map):** Benefits from consistent priority management — no manual priority adjustment needed after audits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **When `persist_audit()` is called with a report containing `Ready to close: Yes` and the work-item priority is `critical`, the priority is lowered to `high` before the audit is persisted.**
2. **When `persist_audit()` is called with a report containing `Ready to close: No`, the priority is NOT changed.**
3. **When the work-item priority is already `high` or lower, no change is made (idempotent for non-critical items).**
4. **The priority change is applied via a `wl update --priority high` call (or equivalent) before the `wl audit-set` call.**
5. **Both parent-level and child-level audit paths are covered (the single `persist_audit()` function handles both).**

## Constraints

- Must not alter any other audit behavior (report content, `wl audit-set` arguments, readback verification).
- Must not change the work-item stage, status, or any field other than priority.
- Must respect the existing `worklog_dir` parameter so the correct store is targeted.
- Priority update must be best-effort — if it fails, the audit should still persist (the priority update is not critical to audit correctness).

## Existing state

`persist_audit.py` (`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`) currently:
1. Extracts `Ready to close: Yes/No` from the report.
2. Calls `wl audit-set` with the report data.
3. Calls `wl update --audit-text` with the current stage preserved.
4. Returns the result code.

No priority check or adjustment is performed.

## Desired change

In `persist_audit()`, before calling `wl audit-set`, add logic that:
1. Detects `readyToClose: yes` in the report.
2. Fetches the current work-item priority via `wl show <id> --json`.
3. If priority is `critical`, calls `wl update <id> --priority high --json` (using the same `worklog_dir` if set).
4. Continues with the existing `wl audit-set` and `wl update --audit-text` calls.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — Add priority-lowering logic before the `wl audit-set` call.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — Add tests for the new priority-lowering behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** `wl update --priority` call fails (e.g., transient worklog error). **Mitigation:** Log a warning but continue with audit persistence; the priority change is non-critical to audit correctness.
- **Risk:** `wl show` returns unexpected JSON structure. **Mitigation:** Guard with try/except; only change priority if `critical` is clearly present in the expected field.
- **Assumption:** `wl show <id> --json` returns the priority in the `priority` field of the `workItem` object (verified in existing `persist_audit.py` code).

## Related work

- SA-0MSAWFTZX003T042: Audit completion must set status: open or completed — remove 'Do NOT change stage' rule (completed)
- SA-0MS21B5MP004AUUS: Close work items after release only when readyToClose and producerReview conditions are met (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the priority be lowered from any priority above high, or only from critical? — Answer (user): Only from `critical` to `high`.
- Q: Should this apply to child work items audited via `persist_single_child_audit()`? — Answer (user): Yes, because `persist_audit()` is the single persistence entry point for both parent and child audits.
data.title: Lower critical to high priority before persisting audit when readyToClose: Yes

## Summary

Deliverable for 'Optimize audit grep scans: only perform required and efficient scans (SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM)' — root-cause mitigation.

`.worklog/` holds 9.5 GB across 86 `audit_debug_*.jsonl` files (up to 1.4 GB each; a single entry embeds up to 738 MB of raw pi session stdout). They are written by `audit_runner.py` only on failure (parse_failure/provider_error) or explicit `--debug-log`, are never read back programmatically, and their presence in `.worklog/` is a scan trap for agents. This feature relocates the default debug-log location outside the worklog dir, adds lifecycle cleanup (retention sweep + delete-on-success), and documents them as transient forensics.

**Constraint (operator): do NOT truncate debug-file content.** Full `raw_stdout`/`raw_stderr` fidelity is preserved whenever a file is kept; we manage lifecycle (where, when, how long) only.

## Why

Removing the 9.5 GB bloat and moving new files out of scanned paths directly attacks the root cause of slow scans; complements the scan.py helper (SA-0MSBR0LLT006JCXN) and prompt guidance (SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Default debug-log path for audit runs is outside `.worklog/` and outside the repo tree (e.g., `~/.audit_debug/<project>/audit_debug_<id>.jsonl`) via `_default_debug_log_path` (which tests already monkeypatch); existing explicit `--debug-log` flag still wins.
- [ ] Kept debug entries preserve full `raw_stdout`/`raw_stderr` content — no truncation (test asserts lengths unchanged from source).
- [ ] Successful audit runs leave no debug file behind (run-completion cleanup removes any file for the run, including `--debug-log` runs); failed runs retain full-content files for forensics.
- [ ] Cleanup sweep script (`skill/audit/scripts/cleanup_debug_logs.py`) deletes debug files older than a configurable retention age (default >= 14 days), defaults to dry-run with a --apply flag; tests cover old-removed / young-kept / dry-run-no-change.
- [ ] Scan prunes (scan.py) exclude the new debug-log location; SKILL.md documents debug files as transient, non-scanned, full-content forensics.
