# Implement skill: gate implementation on Code Freeze status; ship skill sets/clears the freeze marker

## Problem statement

While a ship-it (dev→main release) process is running, new implementation work must not land on `dev`. The ship skill release pipeline currently sets no "Code Freeze" state, and the implement skill (and its single-item variant implement-single) will happily start a new implementation mid-release, racing the release merge. This item makes the ship skill set a Code Freeze marker while a release is in progress and makes the implement skills gate on that marker.

> **Update (2026-08-03, option A):** The batch skills `implementall`, `intakeall`, `planall` were removed from `dev` by commit `1b56b64` ("remove unused skills", no work-item ref). This plan now gates only `implement.py` (via the shared helper) and `implement-single` (which delegates to `implement.py`). The removal left broken references in `README.md` and `docs/dev/audit-fan-out-source-map.md`; that cleanup is tracked in a separate work item (SA-0MSBXQNDE008QBIW reconciliation + docs-fix item created during planning).

## Users

- **Producers / release managers** — they must be able to start a release knowing no agent will begin new implementation work until it completes.
- **AI agents running the implement skill** — they must receive a clear, early "Code Freeze in progress" refusal instead of creating worktrees/commits mid-release.
- **Developers** — they benefit from the same guarantee the herdr plugin enforces client-side (see WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR).

### Example user stories

- As a release manager, when I start `node scripts/run-release.js` (ship skill), I expect a Code Freeze marker to be set for the project immediately and cleared when the release finishes, fails, or is aborted.
- As an agent, when I invoke `implement.py start <id>` while the project is in Code Freeze, I expect an immediate refusal with a clear message, and I expect the work item NOT to be claimed (status untouched).
- As a developer, I expect `implement-single` to apply the same gate (it delegates to `implement.py`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Ship skill sets/clears the marker** — `run-release.js` (or the canonical `merge-dev-to-main.sh` it invokes) writes the Code Freeze marker to `<project-root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` at release start and removes it when the release completes, fails, or aborts (trap/`finally`-equivalent; also cleared on `--dry-run` exit and on gating failures). Marker format matches the contract defined in WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR: `{ "active": true, "reason": "ship release in progress", "startedAt": "<ISO>", "pid": <pid> }`.
- [ ] **implement.py gates on start** — `phase_start()` checks the marker before claiming the work item and before creating a worktree. If freeze is active, it refuses with a clear message ("Project is in Code Freeze — implementation blocked until the release completes"), exits non-zero, and does NOT change the work item status. `--force`-style bypass is NOT supported.
- [ ] **implement-single gates too** — `implement-single` honors the same marker check by delegating to `implement.py` (its documented orchestration path), so no separate gate logic is duplicated. (The `implementall` batch variant was removed from the repo — see update note above.)
- [ ] **Marker helper shared** — a shared helper (e.g. in `skill/shared/`) provides `is_code_freeze_active(project_root)` used by implement.py (and thus implement-single), with fail-open semantics (missing/invalid marker = not frozen).
- [ ] **No deadlocks with release** — the gate does not block `wl` commands or sync; it only refuses to start implementation work.
- [ ] **Tests** — tests cover: marker write/clear by ship scripts (set, clear-on-success, clear-on-failure), implement.py refusal when marker present (status untouched, non-zero exit), absence of marker allows start, and fail-open on corrupt marker.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Marker location and format are a cross-repo contract shared with the herdr plugin (WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR). Read that item's description for the authoritative contract; do not change it unilaterally.
- Fail-open: a missing/corrupt marker must never block legitimate implementation work.
- The gate must be checked BEFORE claiming the work item (no in_progress churn during a freeze).
- Ship-side marker lifecycle must be robust: cleared on success, failure, abort, and dry-run exit — use a trap/`finally` pattern in the shell/JS wrapper.
- Follow build → test → commit discipline (pytest suite).

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` runs the gated release pipeline (unmerged-branches, audit, critical-items, worklog-refs, producer-review gates) and then invokes `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`. Neither sets any freeze state.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` `phase_start()` claims the work item (status → in_progress) before creating a worktree; there is no project-state gate.
- `skill/implement-single/SKILL.md` documents delegation to `implement.py finish/abort`; no gate.
- `skill/implementall/` was removed from the repo (commit `1b56b64`); not in scope.
- The herdr plugin (ContextHub `packages/herdr/`) will read the same marker to show a banner and block implement commands client-side (WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR).

## Desired change

1. Add a small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/code_freeze.py`) with `is_code_freeze_active()` reading `<project-root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
2. Ship: in `run-release.js` (and/or `merge-dev-to-main.sh`), write the marker at the start of the release (after arg parsing, before gating) and remove it in a `finally`/`trap` so it is cleared on every exit path. Include `--dry-run` handling.
3. Implement: call the helper in `implement.py phase_start()` before the claim step; refuse with a clear message and non-zero exit when frozen. `implement-single` inherits the gate via its delegation to `implement.py`.
4. Tests for marker lifecycle and gating behavior.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — write/clear the marker around the release; add trap/`finally` cleanup.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — optional marker write/clear fallback (if JS wrapper is bypassed); `trap` cleanup on exit.
- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — New shared helper (`is_code_freeze_active(project_root)`).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — gate in `phase_start()` before claim.
- `skill/implement-single/SKILL.md` — document that the gate is inherited via delegation (no code change expected).
- `tests/` — marker lifecycle + gate tests.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR` (ContextHub) — "Code Freeze: herdr plugin blocks implement actions (banner + dialog) during ship-it process"; defines the marker contract this item consumes. This item is the dependent task raised for SorraAgents.
- `SA-0MS4TXDPB003EUKA` (completed) — precedent for gating steps in `run-release.js` (producer-review gate, exit code 9).
- `SA-0MSA1FC20005TCSC` (completed) — ship release script worklog-ref handling (context for the release script).
- `WL-0MSALIQJU0084V9U` (ContextHub) — herdr dispatch behavior context.
- Commit `1b56b64` — removed `skill/implementall/`, `skill/intakeall/`, `skill/planall/` from `dev` (untracked removal; docs cleanup tracked in a separate work item).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the marker lives in the project's `.worklog/` directory (same resolution as `wl --worklog-dir`); herdr, ship, and implement all agree on it. Documented contract in WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR.
- **Risk:** marker left behind after a crashed release blocks all implementation indefinitely. Mitigation: trap/`finally` cleanup plus fail-open on stale-marker handling discussion — a stale marker (pid no longer alive) MAY be treated as not-frozen, but that requires care; document behavior. Conservative default: treat presence as frozen, rely on robust cleanup.
- **Risk:** gate added only to implement.py but not implement-single → workaround exists. Mitigation: implement-single delegates to implement.py (documented orchestration path), covered by ACs and tests.
- **Risk:** scope creep — do NOT modify the herdr plugin (ContextHub) here; the plugin is a separate repo/work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the ship skill's marker write/clear be part of this SorraAgents task, or of the ContextHub task?" — Answer (operator): the ship skill lives in this repo, so the marker lifecycle belongs here; the ContextHub item (WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR) consumes the marker for the herdr UI. Source: user request + repo layout.
- Q: "Should there be a `--force` bypass?" — Answer (operator): not requested; default no bypass (gate is absolute during a freeze). Source: design decision, documented above.
- Q: "How is a stale marker (from a crashed release) handled?" — Answer (operator): not specified. Decision: rely on robust trap/`finally` cleanup; document stale-marker behavior in the work item. If a stale marker blocks work, the operator can delete `.worklog/code-freeze.json` manually. OPEN QUESTION marked for review.
- Q: "The batch skills (implementall/intakeall/planall) were deleted mid-session by commit `1b56b64` with no work-item ref, while this plan listed `skill/implementall/` as a key file. How should the plan treat the removal?" — Answer (operator): **A — treat the removal as authoritative**; drop implementall from this plan's ACs/Key Files, gate only `implement.py` + `implement-single`, and raise a separate work item for the broken docs references (README.md, docs/dev/audit-fan-out-source-map.md) and open implementall work-item reconciliation.

data.description:
# ContextHub (WL-) work items re-contaminated the SorraAgents worklog despite the cross-project sync guard

## Problem statement

The SorraAgents worklog is again contaminated with foreign ContextHub (`WL-`) work items. The Aug 1 cleanup (`WL-0MSAH2A71000MUA3` / `WL-0MSALMX61003VHQO`) removed 2132 foreign items (2131 WL + 1 OB) from SorraAgents and force-pushed a clean remote ref (`a3e8687`, SA-only). On Aug 2, the contamination returned: the local DB now holds **1607 WL- items** and the remote `refs/worklog/data` ref holds **2131 WL- items + 1 OB- item** — even though the cross-project sync guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, fix `WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST`) had been deployed to the installed `wl` 55 minutes earlier. The re-imported WL items are STALE (updatedAt ≤ 2026-08-01T16:26, matching the pre-cleanup snapshot), which matches the operator's observation that "the items appear to be out of date with the main Context Hub database, perhaps these have somehow been renewed, recovered or similar."

## Users

- **Project maintainers and agents** — a polluted worklog breaks `wl doctor prune`, inflates sync payloads, pollutes search/reporting, and leaks ContextHub's internal items (including deleted ones and test fixtures like `OB-0MN9CZ48N0053L9Q`) into unrelated projects.
- **ContextHub maintainers** — their internal work items (including test data) appear in other projects' worklogs.

User stories:
- As a SorraAgents maintainer, I want the worklog to contain only `SA-` items so that prune, search, and reporting operate on my data alone.
- As an operator, I want the cross-project guard to be effective even for long-running/daemon-spawned `wl` invocations so contamination cannot re-enter silently.

## Evidence (investigation 2026-08-02)

1. **Contamination timeline (git ref `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`):**
   - `a3e8687` 2026-08-01 20:53 +0100 — rewrite: SA-only (2035 items) ✓
   - Syncs 22:48→14:59 +0100 Aug 1–2 — clean (SA 2036→2051) ✓
   - `947a893` **2026-08-02 15:48:40 +0100 (=14:48:40 UTC)** — first polluted commit: `{'OB':1, 'SA':2051, 'WL':2131}` ✗
   - All subsequent commits polluted (current tip `b76e649`: OB 1, SA 2061, WL 2131).
2. **Guard deployment:** `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog` is a **symlink to the live ContextHub repo** (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`). Its `dist/sync.js` (with `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`) was rebuilt at **2026-08-02 14:53:20 +0100 = 13:53:20 UTC** — 55 minutes BEFORE the pollution was pushed. The guard is present and blocks the classic scenario today (verified live: `wl --worklog-dir <SorraAgents>/.worklog sync` from ContextHub cwd → "Cross-project sync blocked").
3. **The polluting sync did NOT log to the SorraAgents sync.log** (gap 14:14:17 → 14:51:44 UTC) — the guard in the *current* code throws BEFORE the log writer is created, but a blocked sync would not push either. A sync that both pushed WL items and left no log entry must have executed **code without the guard** — i.e., an already-running process that loaded pre-fix modules, or a worktree/dev process running pre-fix source.
4. **Pre-fix code paths confirmed running:**
   - Orphaned test-harness processes running the deleted `tests-code-freeze` worktree's `src/cli.ts` via tsx were alive (`PID 3623245/3623300`, env references the removed worktree path).
   - The `align-icons` worktree source (`wl-WL-0MS5URWJG000A6O5-align-icons`, commit `7fd95579` 2026-07-29) has **NO guard** in `src/sync.ts` (verified grep).
   - The ContextHub "wl process spawning" investigation (`WL-0MSB19J56006E87J`) documented 5 spawning sources (pi browse widget 5s polling, herdr worklist panes, test-harness orphans — 32 killed, etc.) and was committed at **14:48:22 UTC — 18 seconds before the pollution push**.
5. **Re-imported items are stale:** WL workitems in `947a893` have `updatedAt` in range 2026-02-10 → **2026-08-01T16:26:34Z** — a snapshot from before the Aug 1 cleanup, consistent with a process holding pre-cleanup state (e.g., a long-running daemon/pane or orphaned process with old data loaded).

## Existing state

- SorraAgents local DB: `{'SA': 1474, 'WL': 1607}` (3081 items; 1607 foreign).
- SorraAgents remote ref `refs/worklog/data`: `{'OB': 1, 'SA': 2061, 'WL': 2131}` (4193 workitems).
- Cleanup tooling exists: `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` (from `WL-0MSALMS6S0030X99`), used successfully Aug 1.
- Root-cause guard exists in the current `wl` source/dist but is ineffective against pre-fix long-running processes and was evidently bypassed.

## Desired change

1. **Clean up again:** run `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` in SorraAgents (and re-verify all four projects: ContextHub WL, SorraAgents SA, Tableau-Card-Engine CG, open_source_llm OSL) to remove foreign items from both the local DB and the remote ref; verify remote ref prefix distribution is own-only after the push.
2. **Make the guard effective for daemon/long-running spawns:** identify every wl-spawning process (herdr server daemon, herdr worklist panes, pi TUI browse widget auto-sync, test-harness orphans) and ensure they either (a) use the current binary/source, (b) are restarted after upgrades, or (c) are terminated if orphaned. Restart the running herdr server (currently an old build) so its panes pick up the guard.
3. **Defense in depth:** consider adding a project-prefix filter at merge time in `wl sync` (union currently has no prefix filter — the exact gap that let foreign items through even with repo-context checks), so items whose ID prefix does not match the configured project prefix are never imported.
4. **Prevent stale-data re-entry:** audit processes holding pre-cleanup state (old worktree sources, backups like `ContextHub/.worklog.bak`, orphaned tsx processes) that could push stale snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` in SorraAgents (run from the SorraAgents repo root), `wl list --json` contains only `SA-` items; `git ls-remote origin refs/worklog/data` content (item-prefix distribution of the ref JSONL) contains only `SA` (no `WL-`, `OB-`, or other foreign prefixes).
2. The same re-cleanup is executed and verified in ContextHub, Tableau-Card-Engine, and open_source_llm (own-prefix only in DB and remote ref).
3. All currently running wl-spawning processes are identified (herdr server + panes, pi TUI extensions, orphaned tsx/test processes) and either restarted onto the guarded build or terminated; no process runs pre-fix code that lacks `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`.
4. A `wl sync` from any foreign-project cwd with `--worklog-dir <SorraAgents>/.worklog` is blocked (guard effective) AND a normal `wl sync` in SorraAgents does not re-import foreign items (verified by dry-run after cleanup).
5. A recommended preventive fix (e.g., prefix filter at merge, or daemon restart procedure) is implemented and covered by tests; all related documentation updated.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Use `wl` commands / `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` (never edit `worklog-data.jsonl` by hand).
- Root-cause fix (`WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST`) is already in source; do not regress it.
- The installed `wl` being a symlink to the live ContextHub repo must be taken into account: rebuilding ContextHub's dist changes the "installed" CLI, and long-running processes must be restarted.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `wl doctor foreign-items` implementation (ContextHub repo, `src/commands/doctor.ts` + `src/sync.ts` `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`) — reuse for cleanup.
- `ContextHub/src/sync.ts` — `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `mergeWorkItems` (add prefix filter), `performSync`.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` cwd/spawn behavior (already fixed; verify running daemon uses it).
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `runWl` spawn args (already passes `--worklog-dir`).
- pi Worklog TUI extension (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog/`) — auto-sync trigger `wl sync --if-idle`.
- Orphaned processes / test harness (`WL-0MSB447TJ000R3N8` fixes) — ensure no pre-fix source remains running.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST` — root cause: cross-project merge in `wl sync --worklog-dir` (completed, in_review).
- `WL-0MSAH2A71000MUA3` — Remove foreign ContextHub (WL-) items from all project worklog DBs and git refs (completed, in_review).
- `WL-0MSALMX61003VHQO` — Execute cleanup across all four projects (completed, in_review).
- `WL-0MSALMS6S0030X99` — Rewrite and force-push remote worklog refs (`wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push`).
- `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` — document wl process spawning root cause (herdr/pi/test-harness spawns).
- `WL-0MSB447TJ000R3N8` — prevent orphaned wl processes from test harness.
- `WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` — wl sync lock storm.
- `OB-0MN9CZ48N0053L9Q` — shared leaked test fixture present in every project (to be removed as foreign).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the polluting sync executed pre-fix code (unlogged push at 14:48:40 UTC after the guard was deployed at 13:53 UTC). Evidence: no log entry in SorraAgents, guard present in dist, pre-fix sources confirmed running. If the exact process is not found, the guard may still have a bypass — the prefix-filter (AC5) is the defense-in-depth mitigation.
- **Risk:** cleanup without also fixing the process-level re-entry vector will re-contaminate again (this is the third occurrence: original pollution, cleanup, re-pollution).
- **Risk:** restarting herdr/pi daemons disrupts active sessions — coordinate with the operator.
- **Scope-creep guard:** preventive fixes belong to this item's AC5 but implementation should be minimal (prefix filter at merge + daemon restart procedure); broader refactors are separate items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Are the re-imported items current ContextHub items or stale copies?" — Answer (operator): "the items appear to be out of date with the main Context Hub database, perhaps these have somehow been renewed, recovered or similar." Verified: WL items in the polluted commit have updatedAt ≤ 2026-08-01T16:26Z — a stale pre-cleanup snapshot.
- Q: "How did it happen?" — Investigation (this intake): the guard was deployed 55 min before the push but the polluting sync ran unguarded code (no log entry; pre-fix sources confirmed running), re-importing a stale snapshot of the pre-cleanup ContextHub data. The installed `wl` is a symlink to the live ContextHub repo, so any process already running before the dist rebuild keeps pre-fix behavior.
- OPEN QUESTION: "Which exact process pushed commit 947a893?" — Not yet identified with certainty from logs (the push left no log entry). Candidates: orphaned test-harness tsx process from the deleted `tests-code-freeze` worktree, a herdr worklist pane/daemon started before the guard rebuild, or the `align-icons` worktree (pre-fix source, no guard). Investigation during implementation should confirm.

data.description:
## Problem

Audit jobs are failing with concurrency timeout errors from the shared semaphore: `semaphore 'audit' busy: no slot free within {timeout}s (max_workers=2)`.

## Existing State

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` provides a flock-based counting semaphore with default `max_workers=2` and `timeout=300s`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` uses `_acquire_audit_slot()` wrapping each `pi call` subprocess
- When the semaphore ceiling saturates past the timeout, `TimeoutError` is raised and caught at line 853, returning an "unmet" verdict
- Configuration via `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` env vars
- Semaphore slots live in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/audit/`

## Open Questions

- What is the actual concurrency level when these errors occur? (Is 2 workers the bottleneck?)
- How frequently do these errors occur? Are they intermittent or systemic?
- Is the 300s timeout too short for the current workload?
- Are there patterns — e.g., tied to specific times of day, specific audits, or specific agents running?
- Should the concurrency ceiling be increased, or is something else causing saturation?
data.title: Investigate audit concurrency TimeoutError errors

# Intake brief: triage helper creates duplicate test-failure work items

## Problem statement

The triage helper `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` always creates a **new** critical `test-failure` work item when run, even when an incomplete (open / in-progress) item with the same failing test already exists. This produces duplicate work items and duplicate triage effort.

## Users

- **Agents running the triage workflow** (via the `test` skill and `triage` skill). They rely on `check_or_create.py` to link a failing test to an existing work item, or create exactly one new item.
- **Producers/release managers** reviewing `test-failure` items, who are currently forced to reconcile duplicates.

User stories:
- As an agent running triage, I want the helper to match an existing open/in-progress `test-failure` item for the same test, so that I do not create duplicates.
- As a producer, I want at most one active work item per failing test, so that triage status is unambiguous.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `list_critical_issues()` parses the real `wl list --json` output shape (a dict with a `workItems` array) and returns the candidate items, not `[]`.
- [ ] Given an existing open or in-progress `test-failure` item whose title/body contains the failing test name, `check_or_create.py` returns `matched_existing` and does **not** create a new item (verified via a test using the real `workItems` wrapper shape).
- [ ] A regression test covers the `{"workItems": [...]}` response shape for `list_critical_issues()` (both unit test with mocked `run_wl` and, if feasible, the integration-style fake-`wl` test).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Do not change the `_is_incomplete()` semantics — it already normalizes `-`/`_` correctly via `_get_status()`.
- Keep the conservative matching heuristics (exact name → token+stacktrace → commit/CI URL) intact; only fix candidate discovery.
- Do not modify agent-framework tooling outside `skill/triage/`.

## Existing state

- `list_critical_issues()` (line ~57) parses `wl list --json` by checking for a dict key `"items"` or a bare list.
- Real `wl list --json` output is `{"success": true, "count": N, "workItems": [...]}` — the parser finds neither `"items"` nor a bare list, so it returns `[]`.
- With zero candidates, all three `match_heuristic_*` functions short-circuit (their `if not _is_incomplete(c): continue` loops never run), so `check_or_create` always falls through to `create_issue()`.
- Verified live: running the helper with `test_name=test_call_pi_default_retries_full_budget` created a duplicate (SA-0MSCEK7OT002APU5, since deleted) although an open item for the same test already existed (SA-0MSC2T9EK009MVNG).
- The original description blamed `_is_incomplete()` checking `in_progress` vs Worklog's `in-progress`. This is incorrect: `_get_status()` (line ~242) already does `status.lower().replace("-", "_")`, and `_is_incomplete('in-progress')` returns `True` (verified). The real root cause is the `workItems` parsing gap.

## Desired change

- In `list_critical_issues()`, also accept a dict with a `workItems` array (matching the shape other skills use, e.g. `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` does `data.get("items") or data.get("workItems")`).
- Add regression tests that mock `run_wl` to return `{"workItems": [...]}` and assert the parser returns the items; extend the integration-style test's fake `wl` `list` output to the `workItems` wrapper shape so the second-run-match path is exercised end-to-end.

## Key Files

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — Fix `list_critical_issues()` to handle the `workItems` key.
- `tests/test_check_or_create_critical.py` — Add/update unit tests to cover the `workItems` wrapper shape.
- `tests/test_check_or_create_integration.py` — Update the fake `wl` `list` output to the real wrapper shape so the match path is covered.

## Related work

- `[test-failure] test_call_pi_default_retries_full_budget — failing test (SA-0MSC2T9EK009MVNG)` — open critical item that was duplicated by this bug during verification.
- `Quality Improvement - Refactoring (SA-0MSCA5Z07008PYWZ)` — discovered-from; the duplicate `SA-0MSCDI77F006D6RM` was created while implementing this item.
- `[test-failure] test_batch_completes_with_ceiling_two (SA-0MSCCA3T9003SJCW)` — canonical item referenced in the original report; the helper created a duplicate `SA-0MSCDI77F006D6RM` for it (deleted).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `wl list --json` consistently returns `{"workItems": [...]}` across wl versions/plugins. Mitigation: prefer `data.get("workItems")` with fallback to `items`/bare list (defensive parse).
- Risk: other call sites inside `check_or_create.py` (e.g. `create_issue`, `add_dependency`) may rely on other output shapes — only `list_critical_issues()` was observed to be affected; keep changes scoped there.
- Scope-creep risk: the matching heuristics themselves (token overlap thresholds, recency sorting) are out of scope; fix only candidate discovery.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Is the described root cause (`_is_incomplete` status vocabulary mismatch) accurate? — Answer (Map, via code inspection): No. `_get_status()` at line 242 normalizes `-`→`_`, so `_is_incomplete('in-progress')` returns `True`. Verified by direct execution. Source: `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`, lines 239–257.
- Q: What is the actual root cause? — Answer (Map, via live reproduction): `list_critical_issues()` expects `{"items": [...]}` or a bare list, but real `wl list --json` returns `{"success": true, "count": N, "workItems": [...]}`; the parser returns `[]`, so the helper always creates a duplicate. Source: live run creating duplicate SA-0MSCEK7OT002APU5 for existing SA-0MSC2T9EK009MVNG (duplicate deleted after verification); confirmed by replicating the parse logic against real `wl list --json` output.
- Q: Why didn't the existing tests catch this? — Answer (Map, via test inspection): Unit tests mock `run_wl` to return bare JSON lists, and the integration test's fake `wl` also prints a bare list — neither exercises the `workItems` wrapper shape. Source: `tests/test_check_or_create_critical.py`, `tests/test_check_or_create_integration.py`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSCCA3T9003SJCW** – [test-failure] test_batch_completes_with_ceiling_two — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MLX8GXHI0L3VBY0** – Engine core orchestrator with dual invocation (completed)
- **SA-0MS0QF0Z4006MJPM** – Create shared status_lifecycle.py module with tests (completed)

# Fix broken references to removed batch skills (implementall, intakeall, planall)

## Problem statement

Commit `1b56b64` ("remove unused skills", pushed to `dev` 2026-08-03 00:01, author: Sorra the Orc, no work-item ref) deleted `skill/implementall/`, `skill/intakeall/`, and `skill/planall/`. The removal left dangling references:

- `README.md` — 29 references to the deleted skills (lines 22, 92–117: ImplementAll section with usage examples).
- `docs/dev/audit-fan-out-source-map.md` — 3 references (e.g. line 89 `skill/implementall/SKILL.md`).
- Open work items that referenced the deleted skills:
  - `Reference test skill in implementall workflow (SA-0MSBXQNDE008QBIW)` — open, stage idea; the target skill no longer exists → superseded/obsolete.
  - `Wire test skill into code-touching skills and master AGENTS.md (SA-0MSAC1IAS007I3K8)` — open, stage idea; may list implementall among code-touching skills.
- `AGENTS.md` workflow references (e.g. "See [implementall skill]" in the batch workflow section) — verify and update.

## User stories

- As a developer reading the docs, I want no references to skills that no longer exist, so the README and docs remain accurate.
- As a producer triaging open work items, I want obsolete implementall work items closed or re-scoped, so `wl next` does not surface dead work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn "implementall\|intakeall\|planall" README.md docs/ AGENTS.md` returns no references to deleted skills (excluding intentional historical notes).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Do NOT restore the deleted skills (removal is authoritative per operator decision, 2026-08-03, option A).
- Do NOT modify the herdr plugin (ContextHub).

**Problem:** The Phase 1/Phase 2 verdict intake in `audit_runner.py` records model verdicts verbatim (only lowercased). When the model returns a natural-language synonym like `pass` instead of `met`, the criterion fails the `all_ac_acceptable` check (`_ACCEPTABLE_VERDICTS = {met, adjusted}`) and the whole audit reports 'Ready to close: No' even though every AC is genuinely satisfied.

**Observed:** Audit of SA-0MSAHQZN4004ZFKQ (completed/in_review) on 2026-08-03: all 11 ACs across the item + 2 children are satisfied, code quality clean, yet verdict = No solely because child SA-0MSAIFWBC0048OVM's 3 ACs carry verdict `pass` (model's synonym for met).

**Fix:** Add a `_normalize_verdict()` helper mapping synonyms (pass→met, fail/failed→unmet, etc.) and apply it at every verdict intake point: Phase 1 parent AC review, Phase 1 child review, `_call_pi` single-object parse, Phase 2 `_apply_deep_verdicts`, and `_deep_analyze_child`.

**ACs:**
- AC1: `_normalize_verdict('pass') == 'met'` and `_normalize_verdict('met') == 'met'`; unknown verdicts pass through unchanged.
- AC2: Phase 1 parent AC review records normalized verdicts (a mocked parent batch returning 'pass' yields 'met').
- AC3: Phase 2 deep-analysis verdicts are normalized before merge (batch and per-child paths).
- AC4: `_call_pi` single-object parse normalizes the verdict field.
- AC5: Unit tests in skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py cover all of the above; existing verdict-semantics tests still pass.

## Summary

The Code Freeze marker at `.worklog/code-freeze.json` (contract WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR, set/cleared by the ship skill release pipeline) contains a `pid` field, but `skill/shared/code_freeze.py`'s `is_code_freeze_active()` only checks `active: true`. Nothing verifies whether the recorded process is still alive.

If a release is killed hard (SIGKILL, OOM, reboot, `kill -9`), the `finally`/EXIT-trap cleanup never runs and the marker stays behind, blocking ALL implement work (implement.py phase_start refuses) until someone manually deletes the file. This is the 'agents grind to a halt after Ship It' failure mode.

## User story

As an operator, when a release crashes or is killed, I expect agents to recover automatically once the release process is confirmed dead — not remain frozen until someone manually deletes `.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `is_code_freeze_active()` considers the marker stale (not frozen) when the recorded `pid` is no longer alive (e.g., `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises ProcessLookupError / ESRCH), with a grace period (e.g., N minutes since `startedAt`) so a live release is never prematurely unfrozen.
- Missing/corrupt marker stays fail-open (not frozen) — unchanged.
- `active: true` with a live pid → frozen (unchanged).
- A stale marker is optionally removed (best-effort) when detected, or at minimum reported via warning log.
- Tests cover: live pid → frozen, dead pid → not frozen, dead pid within grace period → frozen, corrupt/missing → not frozen.

## Related

- discovered-from: investigation of 'Ship It causes agents to grind to a halt'
- related-to: SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB (Code Freeze mechanism), SA-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR (marker contract — do not change contract unilaterally)
- Issue type: bug, priority: high
data.title: Code Freeze marker: validate pid liveness / auto-expire stale markers

## Summary

`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` invokes the canonical release script (`merge-dev-to-main.sh`) via `spawnSync('bash', [selectedScript, ...args])` with **no timeout**. If a git/gh operation inside the script hangs (network stall, credential prompt, hung SSH), the release blocks indefinitely — and because the Code Freeze marker is set for the entire run (cleared only in the `finally`), ALL implement work stays blocked for the duration. This is a 'Ship It → agents grind to a halt' contributor.

Related: `waitForPRMerge` already has a 600s timeout; the release-script spawn does not.

## User story

As an operator, when a git/gh operation hangs during a release, I expect the release to fail loudly after a bounded time and the Code Freeze to be lifted — not block all agents indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- `spawnSync` for the release script gets a timeout (e.g., 10–15 minutes, consistent with waitForPRMerge's 600s) and the child is killed on expiry.
- On timeout, run-release.js exits non-zero with a clear message (which operations hung is best-effort) and the Code Freeze marker is still cleared (existing `finally` covers this — verify with a test).
- Exit code for the timeout case is documented; no new undocumented exit code collisions with the existing table (1–9).
- Tests cover: normal completion unchanged, timeout path clears the marker.

## Related

- discovered-from: investigation of 'Ship It causes agents to grind to a halt'
- related-to: SA-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB (Code Freeze), SA-0MSDX3EYZ005SGIK (stale marker liveness)
- Issue type: bug, priority: high
data.title: run-release.js: add timeout to release script spawn (prevent indefinite freeze)

**discovered-from:** SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D (Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement)

## Problem

Measured audit runs (2026-08-04, see docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md / /tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md) show the Phase 2 performance bottleneck has MOVED to Phase 1. For a parent with 10 children, Phase 1 (parent + child AC review) consumed 13,483s = 88% of wall-clock (avg 1,348s/call, max 2,400s), while Phase 2 was reduced to a single bounded 1,817s call by P1-P6.

Phase 1 prompts (audit_runner.py L2985 parent, L3137 child) contain NO file-scope manifest, NO SCANNING bounded-helper block, NO parallelism for child AC review, and NO reuse of child_audit_ready. These are the exact deficiencies Phase 2 had before this epic fixed them.

**Additionally: Phase 1 sessions run WITHOUT tools** (`_call_pi_and_maybe_log` calls at L2997/L3147 do not pass `enable_tools=True`), yet the prompt asks the model to 'review the acceptance criteria against the codebase' with file:line evidence. The model cannot read, grep, or search the repo — it can only extrapolate from the description, AC text, and related-work report. Phase 2, by contrast, gets `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls` (L863). So the phase now dominating wall-clock is also the phase least able to verify code.

## User story

As a release operator, I want Phase 1 AC review to be as bounded and as tool-enabled as Phase 2 so that audit wall-clock is dominated by neither phase, multi-child audits complete reliably, and Phase 1 verdicts are grounded in actual code inspection.

## Proposed approach

1. Inject the same file-scope manifest (`_build_file_scope_manifest`) + SCANNING bounded-helpers block into Phase 1 parent and child AC review prompts.
2. Enable read-only tools for Phase 1 sessions (same `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls --exclude-tools ask_question` as Phase 2) so the model can inspect the files named in the manifest.
3. Parallelize Phase 1 child AC review with the existing `ThreadPoolExecutor` pattern (reuse `_resolve_phase2_parallelism` or add a sibling resolver).
4. Reuse `child_audit_ready=True` to skip Phase 1 child AC review for children whose own fresh audit already reviewed their ACs (mirror of P2).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Phase 1 parent and child AC review prompts include the file-scope manifest + SCANNING block; unit tests assert the manifest text is present in parent/child Phase 1 prompts.
2. Phase 1 sessions enable the read-only tool set (read,bash,grep,find,ls) with ask_question excluded; unit test asserts the tool flags are passed to `_call_pi` for Phase 1 contexts.
3. Phase 1 child AC review calls run with bounded parallelism (configurable, default >= 2) OR are skipped for children with child_audit_ready=True; unit tests assert the call pattern (parallel execution / reduced call count) without changing verdict semantics.
4. Existing Phase 1 verdict behavior tests still pass (met/unmet/partial/adjusted semantics unchanged); full audit test suite passes.
5. A mocked or instrumented run shows Phase 1 wall-clock reduced (e.g., call count reduced, parallelized, or fewer tokens via tool-grounded evidence); report per-call timings in the work item.
6. Audit skill documentation (skill/audit/SKILL.md and the audit_runner.py module docstring, if it describes Phase 1 behavior) is updated to reflect Phase 1 tools/parallelism/reuse behavior; `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` exists in the repo so the references above resolve.

## Constraints

- Verdict semantics must be unchanged: Phase 1 verdicts stay one of met/unmet/partial/adjusted with the same normalization and adjusted-verdict guidance (existing tests at `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` cover this).
- Tool enablement must remain read-only: the same `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls --exclude-tools ask_question` flag set used by Phase 2 (L863), and the prompt's existing [READ-ONLY AUDIT] guard language stays.
- Parallelism must be bounded and configurable, mirroring `_resolve_phase2_parallelism()` (default 2, env/CLI-overridable) — no unbounded concurrency; the audit-slot flock (`_acquire_audit_slot`) still bounds host-wide concurrent pi launches.
- The elapsed-time guard (PARENT_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT, L101) must keep working: Phase 1 child skipping under the guard must not be broken by parallelization or reuse.
- No timeout increases beyond the 1800s default (consistent with the Phase 2 epic's regression-safety rule).
- Phase 1 skip/reuse must not change `child_audit_ready`/audit-persistence behavior for children (P12 is blocked by this item and depends on verdict semantics staying stable).

## Existing state

- `cmd_issue` flow (verified 2026-08-05): Phase 1 parent AC review (single call, L2983–2997, no tools) → Phase 1 child AC review (sequential per-child calls, L3100–3147, no tools) → child persisted-verdict check (`_get_child_audit_verdict` via `wl audit-show`, L3239–3313, sets `child_audit_ready` at L3312) → Phase 2 (`_run_phase2_deep_analysis`, L3373).
- **Implementation note (verified):** `child_audit_ready` is currently computed AFTER the Phase 1 child AC loop. For approach step 4 (skip Phase 1 child review for fresh-audited children), the `_get_child_audit_verdict` lookup (L3312) must run BEFORE the Phase 1 child loop — either by moving the verdict-check block earlier or pre-computing the flag. The lookup reads persisted state only (`wl audit-show` with a freshness gate), so calling it earlier is safe.
- Phase 2 precedent (mirror target): skip-ready filter first (L2568), then ThreadPoolExecutor over the remainder (L2773, `_resolve_phase2_parallelism` default 2).
- Measurement report: `/tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (P7 finding, section 6.1). It is NOT yet committed to the repo; `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` is referenced but does not exist.
- Test precedents exist to extend: `test_command_includes_tools_when_enable_tools_true` (L295), `test_forwards_enable_tools_true_to_call_pi` (L388), `test_parent_deep_analysis_uses_enable_tools_true` (L487), `test_prompt_includes_file_scope_manifest` (L1059), `test_child_prompt_includes_file_scope` (L1152).

## Desired change

- Phase 1 parent/child AC review prompts gain the file-scope manifest (`_build_file_scope_manifest`) + SCANNING bounded-helpers block, exactly as Phase 2's deep-analysis prompt has (L2599–2604).
- Phase 1 sessions run with `enable_tools=True` (same read-only tool set as Phase 2).
- Phase 1 child AC review becomes: skip children with a fresh persisted audit verdict (child_audit_ready), then review remaining children with bounded parallelism; single remaining child falls back to the sequential path.
- Commit `/tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` to `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` so the doc references in this item resolve.
- Measured outcome: Phase 1 wall-clock for a 10-child parent drops from ~13,483s toward the Phase 2 estimate (~2–4k s, 50–70% reduction per the report's P7 estimate), verified by AC2-style per-call timing instrumentation.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 parent prompt (L2985) and call (L2997); Phase 1 child loop (L3100–3147); `_build_file_scope_manifest` (L1375); Phase 2 parallel pattern to mirror (L2758–2790); `_resolve_phase2_parallelism` (L670); tool flags (L863); `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` enable_tools forwarding (L1917–1946); `child_audit_ready` computation (L3312) and Phase 2 reuse (L2568); elapsed guard (L101, L2964).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — extend with Phase 1 manifest/tool-flag/parallelism/reuse unit tests (existing precedents at L295, L388, L487, L1059, L1152).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document Phase 1 tools/parallelism/reuse behavior and any new config flag.
- `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — commit the measured report (currently only in /tmp) so references resolve.

## Related

- docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md (P7 finding)
- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py (_build_file_scope_manifest L1375, Phase 1 prompts L2985/L3137, Phase 2 parallel pattern L2773, enable_tools L863, Phase 1 call sites L2997/L3147)
- SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D — parent epic (Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement); this item is a discovered P7 finding of that epic.
- SA-0MSF4TPCN0095MIB — P12 (eliminate duplicate child re-deep-analysis on 'not ready'), blocked-by this item.
- SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X — configurable cumulative elapsed-time guard (completed); the guard interacts with Phase 1 child skipping.
- SA-0MPXCHAEY002B8I6 — audit persistence/no-fallback issue (completed); related to AC5 measurement discipline.
- SA-0MS59TFER000IEKO — SKILL.md docs update for tools-enabled Phase 2 (completed); precedent for AC6 docs work.

## Risks & assumptions

- Tool-enabled Phase 1 calls may be slower per call than bare calls (agent mode overhead); the win comes from fewer calls (reuse), parallelism, and better-targeted evidence. AC5 measures per-call timings; if tool-grounded calls regress wall-clock, the bounded manifest still caps exploration and verdict quality improves.
- Moving the `child_audit_ready` verdict lookup before the Phase 1 child loop adds one `wl audit-show` subprocess per child before Phase 1 — minor overhead vs. the current post-Phase-1 lookup; reuse the computed value to avoid a second lookup.
- Parallel Phase 1 child calls with tools may raise provider-error rates under heavy concurrency (P10 finding: errors were rampant at 7 concurrent audits); bounded parallelism (default 2) + the existing audit-slot flock + unchanged retry behavior contain this. If needed, a Phase 1-specific lower default is acceptable within AC3.
- Assumption: verdict semantics, normalization, and the read-only guard language are untouched (AC4); only the prompt scaffolding, tool flags, and call scheduling change.
- Out of scope (separate P-items in the parent epic SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D): P8 persistence resilience, P9 parent-timeout guard right-sizing, P10 provider-error waste, P11 prompt-size trim. Do not expand scope into these; note them as discovered work if encountered.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "AC3 says 'bounded parallelism ... OR skipped for children with child_audit_ready=True' — which mechanism is primary?" — Answer (intake, Map): "Both, mirroring Phase 2." Evidence: Phase 2 applies the skip-ready filter first (audit_runner.py L2568) and then parallelizes the remainder (L2773); Proposed approach steps 3 and 4 list both. AC3's OR wording is preserved verbatim to avoid altering intent; the implementer should apply skip-then-parallelize.
- Q: "`child_audit_ready` is computed after the Phase 1 child loop today — is it feasible to reuse it before Phase 1 child review?" — Answer (intake, Map): "Yes." Evidence: `_get_child_audit_verdict` (L3312) reads persisted state via `wl audit-show` with a freshness gate, so the lookup can be moved/pre-computed before the Phase 1 child AC loop without changing semantics. Documented in Existing state above.
- Q: "`docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` is referenced but does not exist in the repo — how to resolve?" — Answer (intake, Map, recommended default, OPEN until confirmed): "Commit /tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md to docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md as part of this item (AC6)." The report is the primary evidence for the P7 finding; leaving it only in /tmp breaks traceability.
- Q: "Should Phase 1 reuse a new parallelism resolver or the existing `_resolve_phase2_parallelism`?" — Answer (intake, Map): "Reuse the existing resolver (default 2, configurable) unless a Phase 1-specific default is required; AC3 requires configurable default >= 2." Evidence: _resolve_phase2_parallelism (L670); Proposed approach step 3 says 'reuse ... or add a sibling resolver'.

- **SA-0MS3HPN4I004KVNK** – Audit Phase 2 instructs model to read files but runs in tool-less pipe mode (completed)
- **SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1** – Wire scan.py guidance into audit prompts and SKILL.md (completed)

# Intake brief: Audit skill — resilient audit persistence (P8)

Don't lose a completed audit run to a final JSON parse failure in the verdict persistence path.

**discovered-from:** SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D (Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement)

## Problem statement

Measured 2026-08-04: a full audit of SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D ran 11 pi calls / 15,299s (4.25h), then the final persistence step failed. `wl update --audit-text` returned rc=1 with a JSON parse error (`Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 28`) against the assembled verdict content, leaving the persisted audit text as a 43-char stub. The entire 4-hour run was effectively lost and the operator must re-audit manually.

## Users

Release operators and agents who run long multi-call audits and depend on the final verdict being persisted.

**User story:** As a release operator, I want an audit that completes its pi calls to persist its results even when the final verdict assembly hits a transient JSON parse error, so that no completed run is lost.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A unit test reproduces the malformed-JSON scenario and asserts the runner persists a usable audit (fallback markdown with a clear failure notice, or repaired JSON) instead of writing a 43-char stub.
2. No full pi-call re-execution is triggered by the repair; retry is bounded at ≤1 additional model call and tests assert the actual retry count is within that bound.
3. Existing persistence tests still pass; full audit test suite passes.

## Constraints

- The repair must never re-run the full audit pipeline (pi calls are unbounded cost). Only a bounded re-ask (≤1 additional model call) is acceptable.
- Persistence writes go through the existing `persist_audit()` / `wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` path; the fix must not bypass identity/readback guards already in place.
- Behavior must remain deterministic and testable with a mocked runner (no real pi/wl calls in unit tests).

## Existing state

- `cmd_issue` (audit_runner.py) assembles the markdown report via `_assemble_issue_report()` then calls `persist_audit(issue_id, report, worklog_dir=worklog_dir)` (audit_runner.py:3674).
- `persist_audit()` (persist_audit.py) first runs `wl audit-set` (raw-output store) then builds and runs `wl update <id> --audit-text <report_text>` (persist_audit.py:251). The latter failed with the JSON parse error; audit-set data alone was insufficient (auditResult field never updated → 43-char stub).
- The verdict itself is parsed from the report's `Ready to close:` line via `_parse_ready_to_close()`.

## Desired change

In the final persistence path (cmd_issue → persist_audit), on JSON parse failure of the assembled verdict:

1. Attempt a repair pass (extract valid JSON prefix / salvage per-AC rows already parsed).
2. Re-ask the model once with a bounded retry to re-emit the verdict array in valid JSON.
3. If still failing, persist the report as markdown (not JSON) with a clear failure notice, so partial results survive.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — builds and runs the `wl update --audit-text` command (line 251); primary location for the resilience fix and failure fallback.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `cmd_issue()` (line 3052) final persistence path; calls `persist_audit()` (line 3674) and handles the rc; also where `_assemble_issue_report()` / `_parse_ready_to_close()` live.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_identity.py`, `test_audit_runner.py`, `test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `test_audit_runner_worklog_dir.py` — existing persistence tests that must continue to pass.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_resilience.py` (new) — AC1 unit test reproducing the malformed-JSON scenario with a mocked runner.
- `/tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — Run A failure evidence (11 calls / 15,299s / 43-char stub).

## Related work

- SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D — Audit skill Phase 2 (deep code analysis): performance evaluation and improvement (discovered-from; still in-progress, plan_complete).
- SA-0MSAXHMZT009EHVV — cwd-independent wl invocation and real diagnostics (completed; established wl subprocess invocation pattern and diagnostics).
- SA-0MS8UI3H3007GPWX — audit runner: detect provider errors, retry transient failures (completed; retry patterns).
- SA-0MPD8NXCS0091ZF4 — Ralph crashes reading persisted audit when workItem.audit is an object (completed; audit persistence read-side).
- SA-0MRYWOTF9005OUXX — Audit runner: remove Ralph config dependency, keep --model flag (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** A repair pass that guesses at JSON structure could silently corrupt the verdict (e.g. wrong per-AC rows). Mitigation: bounded retry with a clear failure notice fallback; conservative salvage that never fabricates verdicts.
- **Risk:** Re-asking the model could hit another provider error / long generation. Mitigation: hard cap at 1 re-ask; if it fails, fall back to markdown persistence instead of looping.
- **Risk:** Fallback markdown persistence could bypass existing identity/readback guards. Mitigation: reuse `persist_audit()`; keep identity check and readback verification in place (AC3).
- **Assumption:** The JSON parse failure is transient/malformed-verdict in origin, not a persistent schema break; if a genuine schema mismatch is found, the repair should surface it rather than mask it.
- **Assumption:** Tests use a mocked runner — no real pi/wl calls in unit tests (existing test harness pattern).
- **Scope-creep risk:** P7 (Phase 1 performance treatment) and P9 (parent-timeout guard) were also identified in the Phase 2 report; they remain separate items — do not fold them into this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Where exactly does the JSON parse failure occur — in the runner or in the wl CLI? — Answer (intake, Map): The work item records the failure as `wl update --audit-text` rc=1 with `Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 28` against the assembled verdict. Exact mechanism is for the implementing agent to reproduce in the AC1 unit test; static reading shows the report is assembled as markdown in `_assemble_issue_report()` and passed to `persist_audit()`, which builds the `wl update --audit-text` command. Source: code reading (persist_audit.py:251, audit_runner.py:3674).
- Q: Is the bounded retry count specified? — Answer (intake, Map): Yes — "re-ask the model once", i.e. ≤1 additional model call; AC2 requires tests to assert the bounded retry count. Source: work item proposed approach + AC2.
- Q: Should the fallback persist via `wl audit-set` raw-output or `wl update --audit-text`? — Answer (intake, Map): Use the existing persistence path; fallback must still produce a usable audit (markdown report with failure notice) and pass the existing readback/identity guards. Source: constraints section + AC1/AC3.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** – Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable (extend parent-process timeout tolerance) (completed)
- **SA-0MSALRZ3B006FPI5** – implement skill: agents must not stash user's uncommitted changes without permission (completed)
- **SA-0MQEEOK5N003ILYB** – [CRITICAL] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py:963 — Local variable `file_paths_in_findings` is assigned to but never used (F841) (completed)

**discovered-from:** SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D (Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement)

## Problem

Measured 2026-08-04: running an audit with DEFAULT settings on SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D (a parent with 10 children) skipped ALL 10 child audits after the parent Phase 1 call (2,088s) because the default 110s cumulative parent-timeout guard tripped. A multi-child audit with defaults silently degrades to parent-only — children are never auto-audited — unless the operator knows to pass `--parent-timeout 14400`. The concurrent run only worked because it explicitly raised the timeout.

The guard (see audit_runner.py L86 docstring, L2963 'Track elapsed time so we can skip remaining child audits') was designed to protect against runaway audits, but its fixed 110s default is far too low for any parent with more than one active child.

## User story

As a release operator, I want multi-child audit runs with default settings to complete (or at least attempt) child auto-audits, so that a parent audit without explicit flags audits its children reliably.

## Proposed approach

1. Auto-scale the guard by child count: e.g., `110s + N_children × 600s`, so a 10-child parent gets a default guard ~6,110s instead of 110s.
2. Keep the guard as a hard ceiling only for pathological cases, and keep the skip diagnostic actionable.
3. Document `--parent-timeout` prominently in skill/audit/SKILL.md so operators know how to override.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Default guard for a multi-child parent scales with child count (unit test asserts the computed guard > 110s for N>1).
2. A mocked cmd_issue run with defaults no longer warns 'Approaching parent timeout' immediately after a single parent Phase 1 call; unit test asserts child auto-audits are attempted.
3. Existing timeout-guard tests still pass (guard still trips for pathological elapsed times); full audit test suite passes.
4. SKILL.md documents `--parent-timeout` and the new default behavior.
5. When the guard does trip, the skip diagnostic remains actionable — it names the computed guard budget and the `--parent-timeout` / `AUDIT_PARENT_TIMEOUT` override (existing '(110s budget)' diagnostic format retained, updated to report the computed budget).

## Implementation notes (handoff)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: `PARENT_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 110` (L107) becomes the base term of the scaled default; the guard resolution in `cmd_issue` (L3355-3358) computes `base + N_children × per_child_budget` when no explicit `--parent-timeout`/`AUDIT_PARENT_TIMEOUT` override is present. Explicit overrides keep current semantics unchanged.
- Existing tests that pin the old fixed default must be updated to match the new dynamic default (intent preserved — guard still trips for pathological elapsed times):
  - `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` `TestParentTimeoutResolution::test_default_guard_constant_preserves_behavior` (asserts `PARENT_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT == 110`; re-express as "base term" or computed-guard behavior).
  - `TestParentTimeoutGuardBehavior::test_default_guard_skips_child_after_110s` (expects skip at 120s elapsed for a 1-child parent; with `110 + N×600` the budget is 710s, so bump the fixture elapsed value into a genuinely pathological range).

## Related

- /tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md (finding: 110s default guard skips all children in Run B)
- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py (L86, L2963 elapsed tracking, L3238-3268 auto-trigger with guard)
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py (TestParentTimeoutResolution L2219+, TestParentTimeoutGuardBehavior L2333+)

**discovered-from:** SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D (Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement)
**blocked-by:** SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD (Audit skill: apply Phase 2 performance treatment to Phase 1 AC review / P7)

## Problem

Measured 2026-08-04 and confirmed in code: when an auto-triggered child audit completes with verdict 'not ready' (child_audit_ready=False), the parent's Phase 2 still re-deep-analyzes that child via a `phase2_child:<i>` call (audit_runner.py L2568 skips only children with child_audit_ready=True). The child's own audit already ran its own Phase 2 deep analysis on the same ACs — so this is duplicated deep-analysis work.

This is the remaining redundancy path after P2 (child verdict reuse). P2 eliminated the duplicate for children whose audit returned 'ready'; the 'not ready' path still pays for the child's full recursive audit AND a second deep analysis from the parent.

## User story

As a release operator, I want the parent audit to never deep-analyze a child's ACs twice, so that wall-clock is spent only on novel verification.

## Proposed approach

Coordinate with P7 (Phase 1 treatment): P7 will reuse child_audit_ready to skip Phase 1 child AC review for ready children. This item extends that to the 'not ready' case:
1. When a child's own audit returns 'not ready', determine the failing ACs from the child's persisted audit and feed ONLY those failing ACs to the parent's phase2_child call (instead of re-verifying all ACs).
2. Or: have the parent skip the duplicate phase2_child call and instead surface the child's own 'not ready' findings directly, letting the parent's Phase 1 screening decide blocking status.
3. Ensure the child's independent verdict (which gates its own closure) is preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For a child whose own audit returned 'not ready', the parent's Phase 2 either (a) deep-analyzes only the failing ACs or (b) skips the duplicate call and references the child's own findings; unit tests assert the reduced call payload or skipped call.
2. Verdict semantics unchanged: a child that is 'not ready' still blocks the parent's Ready-to-close evaluation.
3. Existing P2 reuse tests (ready children skipped) still pass; full audit test suite passes.
4. Instrumented run shows reduced phase2_child call count/duration for not-ready children.

## Related

- /tmp/audit-phase2-measured-report.md (remaining duplication path)
- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py (L2568 P2 skip, L2276 phase2_child call)

data.description:
# Only move an in_review to open if it actually fails audit

## Problem statement

The audit runner's `finally` status-restore block treats *all* failure modes identically: when the audit fails for infrastructure reasons (model timeout, provider error, `wl` command failure, unparseable verdict), a work item whose pre-audit status was `in_progress` is forced to `open`/`plan_complete` and its assignee is cleared. This demotes items that never genuinely failed audit — e.g., an `in_review` item being re-audited gets kicked back to the actionable queue purely because the model timed out. Only an explicit audit verdict of `No` is a genuine failure that should move an item to `open`.

## Users

- **Producers / release managers** — rely on audit status transitions to know which items genuinely failed audit vs. which need an audit retry.
- **Patch agents / implementers** — an `in_review` item that only hit a model timeout should not silently regress to `open`, erasing its review position.
- **Scheduler / automation** — needs a reliable signal that an infrastructure failure is transient and the item should be re-audited, not re-worked.

### User stories

- As a Producer, when an audit of an `in_review` item fails because the model timed out, I want the item to remain `in_review` so I can simply re-run the audit — not find it unexpectedly back in `open`.
- As a Patch agent, when my item is audited and genuinely fails (verdict `No`), I want it moved to `open` so I can pick it up for remediation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A work item is moved to `open`/`plan_complete` **only** when the audit produced an explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict.
2. On an infrastructure failure (model timeout, provider error, `wl` command failure, or unparseable verdict / no verdict line), the work item is restored to its **pre-audit** status and stage (e.g., `in_review` stays `in_review`); it is never forced to `open`.
3. The assignee is still cleared on infrastructure failure (per operator decision), so the item remains observable in the actionable queue for a re-audit.
4. Verdict `Yes` behavior is unchanged: `completed` / `in_review` (stage kept `done` when already terminal).
5. Existing freshness-gate skip performs no status transitions (unchanged).
6. Deterministic script logic only — the verdict/failure classification must never be delegated to the model or prompt.
7. New unit tests cover: infra failure on `in_progress`/`in_review` item stays at pre-audit state with assignee cleared; genuine `No` verdict moves to `open`; infra failure with an otherwise-parseable `Yes` report still does not advance (status restore takes precedence).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, SKILL.md, and any relevant docs entries.

## Constraints

- Status transitions use `wl update <id> --status <value> --stage <value> --assignee ""` via the injectable `runner` for testability.
- The verdict classification must remain deterministic: `script_failure is not None` or `not audit_completed` or unparseable verdict ⇒ infrastructure failure path (restore pre-audit state); only a parsed `Ready to close: No` triggers `open`.
- The `--do-not-persist` flag is preserved; status changes happen regardless of persist mode.
- Work-items are closed only post-release; this change touches the audit runner's terminal status transition, not the release/close logic itself.

## Existing state

- `cmd_issue()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` captures `original_status`/`original_stage` via `wl show <id> --json` before setting `in_progress`.
- The `finally` block (≈L3509–3560) computes a terminal transition: `Yes` → `completed`/`in_review`; `No` → `open`/`plan_complete`; failure/unparseable → "safe consistent state" where `was_in_progress = original_status in ("in_progress", "in-progress")` forces `open`/`plan_complete` and clears the assignee.
- Tests in `tests/test_audit_runner.py` (`TestStatusLifecycle`) currently assert the buggy behavior: `test_failure_on_in_progress_item_falls_back_to_open` expects an `in_progress` pre-audit item to land at `open` on failure.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` documents the failure fallback as "restore a safe consistent state (the captured original status/stage; `open`/`plan_complete` when the original status was `in_progress`) and clear the assignee".

## Desired change

1. In the `finally` block of `cmd_issue()`, split the failure branch from the verdict-driven branch:
   - **Infrastructure failure** (`script_failure is not None`, `not audit_completed`, or `audit_verdict is None`): restore the captured `original_status`/`original_stage` (fall back to `open`/`plan_complete` only when the original could not be determined), clear the assignee. Do **not** force `open` just because the pre-audit status was `in_progress`.
   - **Genuine failure**: only `audit_verdict == "no"` moves to `open`/`plan_complete` (unchanged).
2. Update `skill/audit/SKILL.md` status-lifecycle documentation to reflect: `open` only on explicit `No` verdict; pre-audit state restored on infrastructure failure.
3. Update/extend tests in `tests/test_audit_runner.py`:
   - Modify `test_failure_on_in_progress_item_falls_back_to_open` → infra failure now restores pre-audit `in_progress` state (assignee cleared).
   - Add: infra failure on `in_review` (status `completed`, stage `in_review`) keeps `in_review`.
   - Add: infra failure on a `Yes`-parsable report still restores pre-audit state (failure takes precedence over the verdict).
   - Keep existing `Yes`/`No`/freshness tests green.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the `finally` block in `cmd_issue()` (≈L3509–3560) where failure-vs-verdict classification lives.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — `TestStatusLifecycle` class asserting terminal transitions; update `test_failure_on_in_progress_item_falls_back_to_open` and add new infra-failure tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — status-lifecycle documentation section (≈L28–46, L58–63, L91) describing the failure fallback.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Intentional relaxation of the "never leave in_progress" rule:** SA-0MSAL2NQV0008HY5 added a safety rule forcing `open` on failure to avoid stuck `in_progress` children blocking release close. This item deliberately relaxes that rule for *infrastructure* failures (per operator decision) so a transient timeout does not demote an item. Risk: an item stuck `in_progress` after an infra failure could block a release close until re-audited. Mitigation: assignee is still cleared, and the existing status-restore retry/warning loop remains in place; a stuck item is now *visibly* in `in_progress` rather than silently demoted.
- **Ambiguous failure provenance:** a `Yes`-parsable report combined with a script failure must be treated as infrastructure failure (failure takes precedence) — the audit pipeline did not complete cleanly, so the verdict cannot be trusted. This precedence rule must be encoded in tests.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any extra opportunities discovered (e.g., further audit-persistence hardening) should be tracked as new work items, not folded into this change.
- **Assumption:** "pre-audit state" means the status/stage captured by `wl show` at the start of `cmd_issue()`; when capture itself fails, falling back to `open`/`plan_complete` remains acceptable since the original state is unknowable.

## Related work

- SA-0MQFFO6U8003ZUWL (completed) — "Change audit_failed state to use status=open"; established that a genuine audit failure lands the item in `open`.

Source: interactive reply during `/skill:intake SA-0MSF5PG1Y005P3AR`.
- Q2: "What counts as a 'genuinely identifiable failure' that should move the item to open?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "a) Only an explicit audit verdict of No (Ready to close: No)". Source: interactive reply.

# Problem Statement

The current AGENTS.md mandates test-driven development (TDD) as a hard requirement — agents must write tests before code. In practice, agents are getting "tied in knots" trying to follow this instruction rigidly, even in situations where it doesn't make sense. The requirement needs to be relaxed while still ensuring excellent test coverage with meaningful tests.

# Users

- AI agents implementing work items — they need clear, practical guidance on when to use TDD vs alternative testing approaches.
- Human operators reviewing agent work — they expect code to be well-tested regardless of the approach used.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **AGENTS.md no longer mandates TDD as a hard requirement.** The "Write tests before writing code" line and "Write tests first, then code" workflow language are removed. Agents are directed to the implement skill for testing guidance.
2. **The implement skill becomes the authoritative testing guide.** Its instructions express TDD as the preferred approach while explicitly permitting alternative testing strategies when TDD would complicate implementation.
3. **All documents emphasize test quality over process.** Language in AGENTS.md and both implement skills states that code must have excellent test coverage and every test must serve a meaningful purpose.
4. **The implement skill's Step 5 instructions are updated** to remove the "Write tests first (TDD)" mandate and replace it with guidance that TDD is preferred but alternatives are acceptable.
5. **The implement-single skill's testing instruction is updated** to match the implement skill's new language (TDD preferred, alternatives permitted).

# Constraints

- Must not weaken the overall testing bar — coverage and test quality must remain excellent.
- Changes should be consistent across AGENTS.md, the implement skill, and the implement-single skill.
- Test anti-patterns from test-writing-guidelines.md remain in force (no placeholders, no source-grep tests, etc.).

# Existing State

- AGENTS.md line 6: "Write tests *before* writing code."
- AGENTS.md workflow step 5: "Write tests first, then code."
- AGENTS.md links to "test-driven development, commit discipline" in the implement skill reference.
- AGENTS.md "Goal-Driven Execution" table includes "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass" example.
- implement skill "Best Practices": "Write tests before implementation code (test-driven development). Always create at least one test file before editing implementation code."
- implement skill Step 5: "Write tests first (TDD): create at least one test file before editing implementation code."
- implement-single skill line 123: "Write tests first (TDD): create at least one test file before editing implementation code."

# Desired Change

- AGENTS.md: Remove the hard "write tests before code" mandate. Replace with language that agents should ensure code is adequately tested, TDD is preferred but alternatives are permitted, and every test must serve a meaningful purpose. Remove the "Write tests first, then code" workflow line. Update the "Goal-Driven Execution" example to reflect flexible testing approaches.
- implement skill: Replace the hard TDD mandate in "Best Practices" and Step 5 with language that TDD is the preferred approach but agents may use alternative strategies (e.g., test-after) when it makes sense. Emphasize excellent coverage and meaningful tests.
- implement-single skill: Mirror the same change at its testing instruction.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — Remove TDD mandate, update testing guidance language
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md` — Update Best Practices and Step 5 to express TDD as preferred, not mandatory
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement-single/SKILL.md` — Update testing instruction to match

# Related Work

- Test Writing Guidelines (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`) — Anti-patterns remain in force regardless of approach.
- No other work items found with related TDD/testing guidance discussions.

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Agents might interpret the relaxation as permission to skip testing entirely. **Mitigation:** Both documents must explicitly require excellent test coverage and meaningful tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Do not expand this item to rewrite broader testing policy, effort-estimation processes, or test-writing guidelines. Extra opportunities should be recorded as linked work items.
- **Risk:** Inconsistent language between AGENTS.md and implement skill. **Mitigation:** Coordinate changes across both files.
- **Assumption:** The test-writing-guidelines anti-pattern list is sufficient guardrails — no additional policy changes needed there.
- **Assumption:** "TDD preferred" is clear enough for agents to self-direct without further procedural detail.

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What specific TDD requirement(s) should change?" — Answer (operator): "The code must be adequately tested, so alternatives are permitted but TDD is preferred." Source: interactive reply (2026-08-05).
- Q: "Should this change affect both AGENTS.md and the implement skill, or just AGENTS.md?" — Answer (operator): "Remove the TDD section from AGENTS.md and make the implement skill authoritative." Source: interactive reply (2026-08-05). Note: implement-single skill also contains the same TDD mandate and must be updated to match (verified via grep of `implement-single/SKILL.md` line 123).
- Q: "What does 'key features are tested' mean in practice?" — Answer (operator): "Agent discretion. The bar is that the code has excellent test coverage, but also that every test serves a meaningful purpose." Source: interactive reply (2026-08-05).

## Problem

**Discovered by audit of SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D (2026-08-05, deepseek-v4-pro):** P5 child SA-0MSAIXZB2007N0F0 AC2 is only partially met. In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `_deep_analyze_child()` (around lines 2277-2340) checks `_timeout` but NOT `_provider_error`. On a provider error (e.g. `finish_reason: error`), `_call_pi()` returns `{"_provider_error": True, "extracted_text": ""}`, so the child falls through to the empty-parse path and **keeps its Phase 1 verdicts unchanged**.

The parent `phase2_deep` path (lines ~2676-2710) DOES handle `_provider_error` by degrading all ACs to partial with the provider-error diagnostic. The child path is inconsistent.

## Impact

Violates the audit invariant "met only when Phase 1 + Phase 2 confirm": a child whose Phase 2 deep analysis hit a provider error is reported `met` (from Phase 1 alone), so the audit can emit a false "Ready to close: Yes" for a child that was never deep-verified.

Reproduction (confirmed):
- Mock `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` to return `{"_provider_error": True, "_provider_error_message": "finish_reason: error", "extracted_text": ""}` with a child whose Phase 1 AC verdict is `met`.
- `_deep_analyze_child` returns the child with verdict still `met` (expected: `partial` with provider-error evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `_deep_analyze_child()` detects `_provider_error` and marks all child ACs `partial` with evidence "Pi provider error: <msg> — manual review required." (mirroring the parent path).
- AC2: The provider-error path returns the same signal as timeout so `phase2_completed=False` propagates (caller must not treat Phase 2 as completed).
- AC3: A unit test in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` asserts a provider-error child result degrades to partial and Phase 2 is not completed.
- AC4: Full audit suite passes (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` 116+ tests, all green) and existing timeout/verdict-semantics tests unchanged.
