data.description:
## Summary
When auditing a PARENT work item that has active children, the audit runner auto-triggers a fresh audit for every child whose persisted audit is deemed stale. A child audit is stale unless auditedAt > child.updatedAt + 60s (AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS). But persisting an audit report itself bumps the child's updatedAt (via wl update/comment) to within milliseconds of auditedAt, so auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s can never hold. Result: every child is perpetually stale, the parent run re-audits all children (2-7 min each) in a loop, and exhausts the elapsed-time guard (default 110s + 600s/child) or the harness timeout before producing a verdict.

## Observed
- Epic LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F (llm repo): parent audit with 7 active in_review children re-audited all 7 (~35 min/pass), then auto-triggered more; runs aborted at 58 min and 90 min shell timeouts with no verdict.
- Measured: child LP-0MSGC26C4000W7XD auditedAt 2026-08-06T21:03:51.642Z vs updatedAt 21:03:51.852Z (210ms delta) — the audit's own persistence bumped updatedAt.
- Workaround used (valid): --do-not-persist skips the auto-trigger loop (persist=False), and children in in_review stage are exempt from blocking parent closure (_is_exempt), so the parent verdict was still computed correctly.

## Root cause
audit_runner.py _get_child_audit_verdict freshness check (approx lines 2263-2284) compares auditedAt against child.updatedAt + AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS. The auto-trigger loop (~3890-3930) re-invokes issue audits for stale children and then re-checks with the same unsatisfiable rule, so the re-check still returns (None, stale) -> child_audit_ready=False.

## Repro
1. Audit several children individually (each writes a report, bumping its updatedAt).
2. Immediately run: audit_runner.py issue <parent-id> --green-run HEAD
3. Observe repeated stderr lines: Auto-triggering audit for child <id> ... reason: stale, and the run continues re-auditing children until the elapsed guard or external timeout kills it.

## Expected behaviour
- A child whose own audit already reports Ready to close: Yes within the same session must not be re-audited by the parent run.
- Freshness should account for the audit's own persistence (e.g., record auditedAt at report write time and exempt that write, or compare against the child's updatedAt excluding audit-report writes), or the auto-trigger loop should trust the verdict it just triggered instead of re-applying the unsatisfiable freshness gate.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Given a parent with active children whose own audits report Ready to close: Yes, audit_runner.py issue <parent> --green-run HEAD completes without repeatedly re-triggering child audits (no redundant Auto-triggering ... reason: stale lines for children audited in the same session).
2. A child whose own audit says Ready to close: No still blocks parent closure (verdict semantics unchanged).
3. A regression test covers the freshness computation with audit-persistence timestamps (auditedAt ~ updatedAt within the freshness buffer).
4. Child audits for the reproduction case (LP-0MSGC26C4000W7XD etc.) keep returning Ready to close: Yes after the fix.

discovered-from:LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F
data.title: audit_runner parent flow loops re-triggering child audits; child freshness can never be satisfied

## Problem

Agents working with the worklog system need a way to track and recover their session logs. Currently, there is no standardized process for linking worklog comments to Pi session logs.

## Proposed Solution

Add a new instruction to `AGENTS.md` requiring agents to add a comment to the worklog item being worked on whenever:
1. A new session is started
2. A new work item is created

## Required Comment Format

The comment should be in the form:

`<agent_action> - Session ID: <pi_session_id> - <path_to_sessions_log>`

Where:
- `<agent_action>` is a short description of the action being taken (e.g., `/intake`, `/plan`, `/implement`)
- `<pi_session_id>` is the current Pi session ID (available via the `PI_SESSION_ID` environment variable)
- `<path_to_sessions_log>` is the path to the Pi sessions log file

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` contains a clear instruction about adding session comments
- [ ] The instruction covers both session start and new work item creation scenarios
- [ ] The comment format is clearly documented with examples
- [ ] The instruction specifies where to find `pi_session_id` and `sessions_log` path (e.g., environment variables)
- [ ] The instruction is placed in a logical location within `AGENTS.md` (likely in the workflow or critical rules sections)

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` hardcodes `npm run build` and `pytest`/`npm test` as its build and test steps. In repositories without Node.js tooling (e.g. bash-only repos like `dev-scripts`) or Python-only repos without pytest, these steps fail with `ENOENT` or missing test discovery, causing finish to abort — refusing to commit, push, or mark the work item `in_review`.

## Users

- **AI agents** implementing work items in non-Node, non-Pytest repos (bash scripts, Unity projects, etc.) who need `implement.py finish` to complete successfully.
- **Release managers** who rely on work items reaching `in_review` status for the dev→main release process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `implement.py finish` completes successfully (build and test steps no-op or skippable) in a repo without `package.json` and without pytest/npm test, when the repo-local verification passes.
- **AC2:** Existing npm-based repos are unaffected — `npm run build` still runs and a real build failure still blocks finish.
- **AC3:** Existing Python/pytest-based repos are unaffected — `pytest` still runs when available and a real test failure still blocks finish.
- **AC4:** The build and test steps are gracefully skipped (with informative log messages) when no applicable tooling is detected, allowing finish to proceed to commit → push → mark `in_review`.
- **AC5:** Unit tests cover both paths for build and test steps (tooling absent → skip; tooling present → run, failure blocks).
- **AC6:** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (SorraAgents pytest + Node + bats, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- Target file: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — lives in the SorraAgents framework repo.
- Precedent: SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ already covers the build-step fix (child SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1 is in progress). This item is the umbrella covering both build AND test steps.
- Precedent: DS-0MSI87WF6003DGTF had to complete finish manually due to this bug.

## Existing state

- `run_build()` (line ~813) unconditionally executes `["npm", "run", "build"]` with `check=False` but treats any non-zero exit as a hard failure.
- `phase_finish()` (line ~1336) treats build failure as fatal: logs the error, adds a comment, resets the work item status to open, and returns without committing/pushing.
- The test step also hardcodes `pytest` then falls back to `npm test` — neither exists in bash-only repos.
- There is no `--no-build` flag, no per-repo build-command configuration, and no fallback when the repo is not an npm/pytest project.

## Desired change

1. **Build step:** Detect absence of `package.json` with a `scripts.build` entry. Skip gracefully with an informative message when no build script exists.
2. **Test step:** Detect absence of `pytest` and `package.json` with a `test` script. Skip gracefully with an informative message when no test tooling exists.
3. **Config option (optional):** Consider adding a `--no-build` / `--no-test` flag or per-repo config for explicit overrides.
4. **Tests:** Unit tests covering all skip/run paths.
5. **Docs:** Update `skill/implement/SKILL.md` to document the skip behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ:** the build-step fix is already being implemented in child SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1; this item must not duplicate that work — coordinate to avoid conflicts.
- **Scope-creep risk:** skipping verification steps can mask real failures (e.g. a repo with a build script that fails). The skip must be narrowly scoped to repos where tooling is genuinely absent, not where tooling exists but fails. Record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding scope.
- **Test discovery gaps:** Python-only repos may have pytest unavailable in the venv; detection must be robust (not just `shutil.which`).
- **Assumption:** skip behavior (informative log + return success) is acceptable for both build and test steps; real failures still block finish.
- **Assumption:** no regression in existing npm/pytest repos — verified by AC2/AC3 and the full test suite.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_build()` and test step logic in `phase_finish()`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the skip behavior
- `tests/test_implement_*.py` — add unit tests for build and test step skip/run paths

## Related work

- **SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ** — "implement.py finish aborts on npm run build for repos with no build script (llm project)": Same root cause, narrower scope (build step only). Already has a plan with child SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1 in progress. This item is the umbrella covering both build AND test steps.
- **SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1** — "Fix run_build() to skip when no build script in package.json": Child of SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ, covers the build-step fix. Implementation work is in progress.
- **DS-0MSI87WF6003DGTF** (dev-scripts project) — Discovered this bug; finish had to be completed manually.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions — the work item description is comprehensive with clear problem statement, steps to reproduce, root cause, suggested fixes, and acceptance criteria.

## Summary

The audit runner's acceptance-criteria extractor (`_extract_acs` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) truncates AC extraction at the first wrapped continuation line of a bullet item. For descriptions whose ACs are markdown bullets with wrapped/indented continuation lines (common formatting), only the FIRST (and often truncated) AC is extracted and passed to the audit model — the remaining ACs are never machine-evaluated, yet the runner can still emit 'Ready to close: Yes' based on that single criterion.

## Bug behaviour

`_extract_acs` iterates description lines after the '## Acceptance Criteria' heading:

- a line matching `^[-*]\s+(.*)` appends the bullet text and `continue`s,
- any subsequent non-empty line that is neither numbered nor bulleted hits `if acs and stripped: break`.

So a description like:

```
- [ ] Criterion one wraps onto
      a continuation line.
- [ ] Criterion two.
- [ ] Criterion three.
```

extracts exactly one AC: `[ ] Criterion one wraps onto` (truncated mid-sentence).

## Evidence

- Work item OSL-0MSCCFH10001E59N defines 6 ACs (all `- [ ]` bullets with wrapped continuation lines). The audit runner (run 2026-08-07) extracted exactly 1: '[ ] Opening the podcast editor via the replacement workflow (ContextHub' and reported 'Ready to close: Yes' covering only that criterion. The other 5 ACs were never evaluated by the Phase 1/Phase 2 models.
- Standalone repro against `_extract_acs` with the item's actual AC block returns `['[ ] Opening the podcast editor via the replacement workflow (ContextHub']`.
- The same truncation applies to 'Success Criteria' headings.

## Impact

- **False-positive closure signal:** items with multiple wrapped-bullet ACs can pass audit ('Ready to close: Yes') with most ACs unverified — a QA-gate correctness issue.
- Truncated criterion text is also fed to the Phase 1/2 models, so even the 'first' AC is evaluated from a partial sentence.

## Suggested fix (not yet authorized)

- Treat indented continuation lines as part of the current bullet: only `break` on a blank line or a new heading, not on any non-bullet line.
- Strip `[ ]` / `[x]` checkbox markers from the extracted text.
- Add a unit test with a multi-AC wrapped-bullet description (e.g. mirroring OSL-0MSCCFH10001E59N's AC block) asserting all 6 are extracted.

## References

- discovered-from: OSL-0MSCCFH10001E59N
- Related audit-skill docs: docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md, docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_extract_acs` returns all wrapped-bullet ACs from a markdown description (continuation lines folded into their bullet; checkbox markers stripped).
- [ ] A unit test covering a multi-AC wrapped-bullet description (including the OSL-0MSCCFH10001E59N AC block shape) passes.
- [ ] Existing single-line and numbered-AC extraction behaviour is unchanged (all prior tests pass).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSFZO24P005H6I4** – Audit: _deep_analyze_child does not degrade ACs to partial on provider error (completed)
- **SA-0MM31CLR91LMIZ8H** – Fix audit poller _query_candidates missing shell=True (completed)
- **SA-0MSAK33NN008NS95** – Load validation & no-regression check (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, acs, actual, add, also (+98 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: acceptance, acs, actual, add, also (+91 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: 2026, acceptance, acs, actual, add (+85 more)

## Problem

`find_related.py` defaults `--repo-path` to `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`. Because `~/.pi/agent/skills/find-related` is a symlink into the SorraAgents repo (`skill/find-related`), this always resolves to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents` — even when analyzing a work item from another project (e.g. OSL-0MSI0GUP20014RA4 in open_source_llm).

## Impact

- Repository file matches are scanned against the wrong project (framework files like `skill/audit/SKILL.md` match instead of target-project files).
- Sidecar full report is persisted under the wrong project's `.worklog/tmp/`.
- Running find_related twice (once with wrong default, once with explicit `--repo-path`) can append duplicate `## Related work (automated report)` sections to the target item description instead of replacing the existing one.

## Repro

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm
python3 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/find-related/scripts/find_related.py --work-item-id OSL-0MSI0GUP20014RA4 --verbose 2>&1 | grep 'Repo path'
# -> [find-related] Repo path: /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents   (WRONG)
```

With explicit `--repo-path /home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm` the scan is correct.

## Suggested fix

Derive the default repo path from the target work item's resolved worklog store / project config rather than the script's own location (e.g. reuse the prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution), or require `--repo-path` for non-framework items. Also ensure the automated-report replacement logic removes ALL existing automated report sections before inserting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running `find_related.py --work-item-id <item-of-project-X>` from any cwd scans project X's repo files, not SorraAgents'.
- [ ] Sidecar full report is persisted under project X's `.worklog/tmp/`.
- [ ] Re-running the script replaces prior automated report sections without duplication.
- [ ] No framework repo files (`skill/**`, `.pi/**`) appear in repo file matches when analyzing a non-framework project's item.
- [ ] Existing behavior unchanged for SorraAgents items.

# Reduce audit skill initial session context size

## Headline

Every `pi` subprocess spawned by the audit skill loads ~49KB (~12.3K tokens) of static context at session start — 40KB of it is a byte-identical AGENTS.md loaded twice (global + project) plus a ~7KB skills section — for prompts that are fully self-contained and never use either. Adding `--no-context-files --no-skills` to the runner's pi invocation cuts per-call static context by ~96% (~49KB → ~2KB).

## Problem statement

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` spawns many `pi -p --mode json` subprocess calls per audit (Phase 1 parent + N child screenings, Phase 2 deep + N child analyses, plus recursively auto-triggered child audits — 8 call sites, several in per-child loops). Each fresh pi session starts with a large static context:

| Component | Size | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (global) | 20,086 B | Always loaded by `loadProjectContextFiles()` |
| `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` | 20,086 B | Loaded from ancestor chain — **byte-identical to global** (verified `diff`) |
| `<available_skills>` XML block | ~7,130 B | 17 skills; injected whenever `read` tool available (all audit calls use `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls`) |
| Base system prompt | ~2,000 B | Fixed |
| **Total** | **~49,300 B ≈ 12.3K tokens** | per pi call |

A typical audit with a few children = 10–14 pi calls → **~150K tokens of pure startup overhead per audit**, repeated for every audit run. Session logs confirm the volume: audit-skill sessions grow to 0.5–0.8 MB each, and ~4,300 session files exist.

Crucially, the audit prompts are **fully self-contained**: they carry the read-only mandate, JSON output format, FILE SCOPE manifest, SCANNING block, and criteria (verified at call sites ~L2435, ~L2729, ~L3390). They never reference AGENTS.md workflow instructions (worktree lifecycle, implement skill, wl CRUD procedures) or the skills section — that content is irrelevant to a JSON-only, read-only model, and the workflow instructions could even conflict with the audit's read-only mandate.

## Users

- **Release operators / audit model operators** — audits become cheaper, faster, and less likely to hit token limits on large work items.
- **The pi Local Proxy / model backend** — less input-token load per call across the N+1 audit fan-out.

User story: *As a release operator, I want audit pi sessions to start with minimal static context so each of the many per-audit model calls is fast, cheap, and within token limits.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_call_pi()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` adds `--no-context-files` and `--no-skills` to the pi command for both `enable_tools=True` and `enable_tools=False` paths; unit tests assert the flags are present in the constructed command.
2. Measurable context goal: across a random sampling of **5 re-audited work items**, each audit pi session starts with **fewer than 10K input tokens** of static context (previously ~12.3K tokens per call); verified by capturing each sampled session's initial context/token usage. (Expected static context after the change: ~2KB ≈ 500 tokens; the 10K ceiling is the hard AC bound.)
3. Verdict spot-check: the same random sampling of 5 work items is re-audited and yields **the same verdicts before and after** the change (no verdict regressions).
4. Full audit test suite passes (`skill/audit/tests/`).
5. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` scripts section documents that pi calls run with context/skills disabled and why (prompts are self-contained).

## Constraints

- Audit prompts must remain self-contained — no prompt may start depending on AGENTS.md content that `-nc` now removes. (Currently none do; this is an invariant to preserve.)
- Verdict semantics unchanged; the runner's two-phase pipeline and status lifecycle must not be altered.
- `-nc`/`-ns` are loader toggles, compatible with `--mode json` and `--tools`.

## Existing state

- `_call_pi()` builds `cmd = [pi_bin, "-p", "--mode", "json", "--model", model, prompt]` (+ `--tools read,bash,grep,find,ls --exclude-tools ask_question` when `enable_tools=True`). No context-reduction flags are passed.
- pi provides `--no-context-files`/`-nc` and `--no-skills`/`-ns` CLI toggles (verified in `dist/cli/args.js`).
- Tests already assert command construction by mocking `Popen` (`test_audit_runner.py` ~L295–370, concurrency tests) — new flags are testable the same way.

## Desired change

1. In `_call_pi()`, append `--no-context-files --no-skills` to `cmd` (alongside the existing `enable_tools` block).
2. Add unit tests asserting both flags present in both tool modes.
3. Add a `# Context reduction` note in `_call_pi`'s docstring and a short paragraph in `SKILL.md` scripts section.
4. (Optional, low priority) `--no-session` to stop writing ~0.5–0.8 MB session files per call; consider separately as it changes debuggability.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** `-nc` removes all AGENTS.md guidance; if a future prompt relies on it, the model loses instructions. **Mitigation:** prompts are currently self-contained; AC 1/5 keeps this explicit and documented. Only tool-enabled calls read files, driven by FILE SCOPE, not AGENTS.md.
- **Risk:** `-ns` removes skill descriptions; audit prompts never invoke skills. **Mitigation:** verified — no skill references in audit prompts.
- **Assumption:** the two AGENTS.md files are meant to be identical (project copy mirrors global). If not, deduplication at the file level is out of scope; the runner flag works regardless.
- **Scope-creep risk:** de-duplicating AGENTS.md globally, adding `--no-session`, or trimming prompt content (see P11, SA-0MSF4AFX9007INSP — completed) are separate items, not part of this change.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` (~L1040–1075) builds the pi command; add the flags here. `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` (~L2143) forwards; docstrings updated.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — command-construction tests (~L286–372) extended for the new flags.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — scripts section documents the flags.
- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` + `projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS.md` — the duplicated 20KB context files (root cause; not changed here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MSF4AFX9007INSP` — Audit skill: trim prompt size — summarize auto-appended related-work report in child/parent prompts (P11). **Completed.** Complementary: reduces *prompt* content; this item reduces *static system context*.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2: performance evaluation and improvement. **Completed.** Parent of the performance work; this item is a further lever.
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7). **Completed.** Prior wall-clock reduction; context reduction stacks with it.
- `SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL` — Audit concurrency limit. **Completed.** Related to per-call cost economics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What makes up the initial context, and where does the duplication come from?" — Answer (analysis): pi's `loadProjectContextFiles()` always loads the global `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` AND walks the ancestor chain from cwd. The project AGENTS.md is byte-identical to the global (verified via `diff`, both 20,086 B), so 40KB of the same content is sent. Skills (~7KB) are appended whenever the `read` tool is available. Source: code inspection of `dist/core/resource-loader.js`, `dist/core/system-prompt.js`, `dist/core/skills.js`; `diff` of the two AGENTS.md files; session-log inspection under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
- Q: "Are the audit prompts dependent on AGENTS.md or skills content?" — Answer (analysis): No. All Phase 1/Phase 2/project prompts are self-contained (read-only mandate, JSON format, FILE SCOPE manifest, SCANNING block, criteria). Source: `audit_runner.py` prompt construction at L2435, L2729, L3390; session log first-message inspection.
- Q: "Which skills invoke pi subprocesses with the same pattern?" — Answer (analysis): Only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`. Implement/plan/others do not spawn the pi binary (they run through the harness). Source: grep of `~/.pi/agent/skills/*/scripts/*.py` for pi subprocess invocations.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS3AT8ZM006C5HY** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/scripts/agent_frontmatter_lint.py:109 — Use a single `if` statement instead of nested `if` statements (SIM102) (completed)
- **SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM** – Optimize audit grep scans: only perform required and efficient scans (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-reduce-audit-context-SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U.md` — matched: agents, audit, context, duplicate, initial (+6 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: agents, audit, context, duplicate, initial (+4 more)
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — matched: agents, audit, context, duplicate, placeholder (+4 more)

## Problem

Every pi session injects an `<available_skills>` XML block into the system prompt whenever the `read` tool is available (which is the default and in all audit calls). Measured 2026-08-07: **17 skills loaded**, rendered block **~6.4KB ≈ 1.6K tokens** (top contributors: audit 508B, author-command 406B, refactor 399B, ship 360B, cleanup 353B, plan 340B, speak 323B, effort-and-risk 333B). The block includes full absolute `<location>` paths (~50B each) and verbose trigger-heavy descriptions.

The block is part of the static session-start context identified in SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U. Unlike the AGENTS.md duplication (40KB), skills are a smaller but still meaningful slice, and pruning is independently valuable for every session.

## User story

As an operator, I want the available_skills block to be compact so every session (interactive and audit) starts with fewer input tokens without losing discoverability.

## Desired change

Investigate why the block is large and reduce it:

1. **Measure** the rendered block precisely (all 17 skills, including multi-line descriptions for implement/test) and record the baseline.
2. **Prune descriptions** — trim trigger-phrase bloat and verbose prose from skill descriptions (they only need to enable matching/discovery, not full instructions). pi validates `description` ≤ 1024 chars; the goal is much shorter.
3. **Remove unnecessary skills** — identify skills that are never invoked or redundant (e.g. orphan/duplicate dirs `code_review`, `owner_inference`, `proxy-usage-analysis`; candidates like `speak`, `cleanup`, `git-management` if unused). Use `disable-model-invocation: true` frontmatter for skills that should exist but not bloat the model prompt (pi already excludes those from the block).
4. **Shorten location paths** — if pi supports relative locations or the loader could emit them, evaluate; otherwise accept the ~50B/skill cost.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Measured rendered `<available_skills>` block drops by **≥50%** from baseline (~6.4KB → ≤3.2KB) while every still-available skill remains discoverable by its name and a short description.
2. Rationale recorded for every pruned description and every removed/disabled skill (comment on this work item); no skill that is actively used is lost — verify by checking each skill's invocation history/trigger mentions before removal.
3. Orphan/duplicate dirs (`code_review`, `owner_inference`, `proxy-usage-analysis` vs canonical names) are resolved (removed or documented as intentional).
4. Skills excluded via `disable-model-invocation` remain invocable via explicit `/skill:name`.
5. Full audit + skill test suites pass; no skill's tests break.
6. Documentation (pi skills doc references, this repo's skill docs) updated to match.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/*/SKILL.md` — frontmatter `description` (trim), `disable-model-invocation` (add where appropriate).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/` — orphan dirs `code_review/`, `owner_inference/`, `proxy-usage-analysis/` (cleanup candidates).
- `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/skills.js` — `formatSkillsForPrompt`, `disableModelInvocation` handling (read-only reference for how the block is built).

## Related work

- related-to:SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U (audit session context reduction — skills block is a component)
- related-to:SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G (AGENTS.md dedup — the larger context slice)

# Audit: execute test suite read-only to verify full-suite ACs automatically

## Problem statement

The audit skill's read-only mandate forbids the runner and Phase 1/2 models from executing state-modifying commands, including running the project test suite. Acceptance criteria that are inherently execution-dependent — e.g. 'Full project test suite passes with the new changes' — therefore always return partial inside the audit, producing 'Ready to close: No' even when the suite is verifiably green.

Current mitigation: the operator-attested green run (--green-run flag, SA-0MSGLAVCZ002LVZ4, completed) lets an operator attest that they ran the suite green at the audited commit. This requires a human to run the full suite and pass the attestation — a manual step that blocks automated/read-only pipelines (e.g. the herdr downtime worker's auto-audit dispatches).

Real case: ContextHub WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX (Herdr downtime worker: find work items in the tab's working directory; 60-min pause when none found) — audit returned 'Ready to close: No' with 8/9 ACs met/adjusted and the ONLY partial AC being the full-suite criterion, which could not be verified read-only.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the audit to verify execution-dependent acceptance criteria (e.g. 'full project test suite passes') automatically — by executing the test suite in a read-only/side-effect-free manner or by consuming an existing green test-run result — so work items don't get stuck at 'Ready to close: No' solely because the audit cannot run tests, and no manual attestation is required.

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Investigate making the test run side-effect-free (or near enough): the audit's read-only concern is that vitest writes node_modules/.vite cache, spawns workers, and repo tests have real side effects. Options: run the suite in a disposable worktree/copy, redirect caches (--cache-dir, TMPDIR), or reuse the existing per-repo test cache module (SA-0MSGNUWQ9002LSMS / SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY) which caches full test-suite results for reuse across ship/audit/implement workflows.
2. Wire the verified green-run evidence into the audit runner so execution-dependent ACs can be marked met without an operator attestation (extending or replacing the --green-run manual path).
3. Keep fail-closed behavior: any test-run failure, timeout, or infra error must never crash the audit or fabricate a green verdict.
4. Tests + docs for the new verification path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The audit runner can mark execution-dependent ACs (e.g. 'full project test suite passes') as met using an automatically-obtained green test-run result, without requiring manual operator attestation.
- [ ] The verification path is fail-closed: a failing, timed-out, or infra-error test run never yields a green verdict and never crashes the audit.
- [ ] The read-only mandate is preserved wherever the suite cannot be executed side-effect-free (or the tradeoff is explicitly documented and gated).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the new verification path (success, failure, timeout, cache reuse if applicable).
- [ ] Documentation updated (audit SKILL.md + scripts docs) describing the automatic full-suite verification path.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] The existing operator-attested `--green-run` path (SA-0MSGLAVCZ002LVZ4) remains functional; the automatic path augments it rather than replacing it.

## Constraints

- Must not modify files outside the SorraAgents framework repo boundaries as defined by AGENTS.md.
- Existing fail-closed audit boundaries (wl failure, provider error, timeout) must be preserved.
- The green-run attestation path (SA-0MSGLAVCZ002LVZ4) remains valid; this item adds/automates the evidence source rather than removing the operator path.

## Related work

- discovered-from: WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX (ContextHub — the audit that surfaced this gap)
- related-to: SA-0MSGLAVCZ002LVZ4 (operator-attested green run — completed; this item automates its evidence source)
- related-to: SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY (Cache full test-suite results — completed)
- related-to: SA-0MSGNUWQ9002LSMS (Implement: per-repo test cache module — completed)
- related-to: SA-0MSAAUJ1F0026BMN (Create 'test' skill — completed)

## Problem

Running the plan skill's `plan-if-needed` helper (or `check-effort-risk`) from a directory where the project worklog cannot be resolved silently corrupts the target work item's effort/risk fields.

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` shells out to `wl` WITHOUT `resolve_worklog_flags`, unlike `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` which uses it. When the skill runs from a non-project cwd (e.g. the agent skill install dir), `_wl_show()` fails to find the work item and returns `{}`. `make_autoplan_decision()` does not distinguish "not found" from "fresh item with no effort/risk": it proceeds to `run_effort_and_risk()`, which invokes `orchestrate_estimate.py` with a zeroed placeholder payload (O=M=P=0, certainty=100). Because orchestrate_estimate.py resolves the project worklog correctly, it finds the real item, overwrites its genuine effort/risk (e.g. Small/Medium) with the zeroed placeholder (Extra Small/Low), and posts a bogus effort-and-risk report comment.

### Observed impact (real incident)

While running `/skill:plan OSL-0MSGCVSDH002656S` in the open_source_llm project (2026-08-07), the plan pre-check (`plan-if-needed` run from the global skill directory) overwrote the item's genuine intake estimate (effort=Small, risk=Medium) with a zeroed placeholder (Extra Small/Low) and posted a bogus "Effort and Risk Report" comment. The same corruption was previously documented in that item's changelog (occurred twice on 2026-08-07). Once corrupted, `is_effort_risk_computed()` returns True for the placeholder values, so subsequent autoplan decisions compute `decision: "skip"` — masking a genuinely Medium-risk item from planning.

### Contributing factors

1. **Silent proceed on fetch failure** — `_wl_show()` returns `{}` on failure and `make_autoplan_decision()` proceeds to the effort-and-risk orchestration path (which writes data) instead of failing fast with an actionable error.
2. **Inconsistent worklog resolution** — plan_helpers' `wl` calls don't use `resolve_worklog_flags` (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py:228`, resolves `--worklog-dir` by work-item-id prefix), while orchestrate_estimate.py does — so the failed lookup and the subsequent successful write target the same real item.
3. **Confusing CLI output** — `plan_if_needed` returns `"effort": stage` (stage mislabeled as "effort"; `"risk"` is actually the boolean decision), which made the failure mode harder to diagnose.

## Expected behaviour

- Running plan/autoplan helpers from any cwd must never modify a work item it could not read.
- When `wl show` fails or the item is not found, the helper returns an explicit, actionable error result and does NOT invoke the effort-and-risk orchestration (no writes, no comments).
- plan_helpers' `wl` subprocess calls resolve the project worklog consistently via `resolve_worklog_flags`, matching orchestrate_estimate.py.
- Genuine effort/risk estimates are never overwritten by zeroed autoplan placeholders.

## Suggested approach

- Fail fast in `make_autoplan_decision()` when the work item fetch fails: return a distinct error/not-found result and skip `run_effort_and_risk()` and `append_autoplan_decision_comment()`.
- Apply `resolve_worklog_flags()` to all `wl` calls in plan_helpers (`_wl_show`, `_wl_comment_list`, `_wl_comment_add`).
- Optionally guard `run_effort_and_risk()` (or add a read-only/diagnostic mode to `orchestrate_estimate.py`) so zeroed autoplan checks never persist to the work item.
- Fix the `plan_if_needed` CLI output field semantics (stop mislabeling stage as "effort").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Regression test reproduces the bug: `plan-if-needed <id>` with a failing `wl show` currently overwrites the item's effort/risk; after the fix the item's effort/risk and comments are unchanged
- [ ] When `wl show` fails / item not found, `make_autoplan_decision` returns an explicit error result and does not call `run_effort_and_risk`
- [ ] plan_helpers' `wl` subprocess calls include resolved `--worklog-dir` flags (parity with orchestrate_estimate.py) and succeed from a non-project cwd
- [ ] A genuine existing estimate (e.g. Small/Medium) is never overwritten by the zeroed autoplan placeholder
- [ ] `plan-if-needed` CLI output no longer mislabels the stage as "effort"
- [ ] All existing tests in `skill/plan/tests` pass; new regression tests cover the above

## References

- discovered-from:OSL-0MSGCVSDH002656S (open_source_llm — the incident that exposed this bug)
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — buggy code (`_wl_show`, `make_autoplan_decision`, `plan_if_needed`, `run_effort_and_risk`)
- `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` — writes the corrupted estimate (steps 8/10) and uses `resolve_worklog_flags`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py:228` — `resolve_worklog_flags`
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — existing suite; `test_failed_fetch_defaults_to_approval` covers the approval gate's conservative default but no test covers the plan-if-needed fetch-failure path
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLWQI6DC09TF7IY** – Audit integration & lifecycle updates: call audit skill and update work items (completed)
- **SA-0MSFZO24P005H6I4** – Audit: _deep_analyze_child does not degrade ACs to partial on provider error (completed)
- **SA-0MSAXHUMM002PMEW** – CLI --worklog-dir flag, docs, and end-to-end verification (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, acceptance, actionable, actually, add (+147 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 100, acceptance, actionable, actually, add (+133 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, 2026, acceptance, actionable, add (+122 more)

## Problem

The global `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this repo's `AGENTS.md`, which holds generic agent-workflow content. Every project copies that same generic content into its own local AGENTS.md, so there is no clean separation between global guidance and project-specific guidance, and pi loads the same content twice per session (see SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U).

## Goal

1. New file `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in the repo root containing the generic agent guidance (copy of the current, deduplicated AGENTS.md from SA-0MSIU09J4005KU1R) — becomes the canonical global source.
2. `scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` -> `<SRC_DIR>/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (instead of AGENTS.md).
3. This repo's `AGENTS.md` becomes project-specific: only a reference to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` plus SorraAgents-specific content.
4. The global file is in use, so the transition must keep global content byte-identical (no disruption): AGENTS_GLOBAL.md = exact copy of current AGENTS.md at commit time; symlink re-pointed only after AGENTS_GLOBAL.md exists in the main checkout.
5. Operator instructions for propagating the new layout to the other projects (ampa, dev-scripts, Tableau-Card-Engine, open_source_llm, ContextHub, llm-manager) are documented on this work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` exists in repo root and is byte-identical to the pre-rewrite AGENTS.md.
2. `scripts/install_pi.sh` targets `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (`AGENTS_SRC`), and install is verified: `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink resolving to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
3. Global content served at `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is unchanged (same bytes as before the restructure).
4. `AGENTS.md` contains only the global-file reference plus project-specific content (no generic workflow duplication).
5. All sections/heading anchors preserved in AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (workflow, work-item tracking, coding disciplines, etc.).
6. Build and full test suite pass; changes committed and pushed to dev.
7. Work item documents the operator steps (per-project AGENTS.md update + install script run) for the other six projects.

## Out of scope

- Updating the other projects' AGENTS.md files (operator action, documented here).
- SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U (audit skill context reduction).

## Summary

implement.py finish (the implement skill orchestrator at `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`) runs a hardcoded `npm run build` as its Step 2 Build (run_build()). Repos whose root package.json has no build script (e.g. Python-only projects like llm: proxy + skill scripts) make npm run build exit 1 with Missing script: build, so the finish phase aborts and resets the work item to open — every implementation in such a repo is blocked at the build gate.

discovered-from:LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL (the proxy-usage-report archival item, completed via the manual path because of this).

## User stories

- As an agent running implement.py finish in a repo without a build script, I want the build step to be skipped/reported as a no-op, so finish proceeds to tests → commit → push instead of aborting.
- As an agent running finish in a repo WITH a build script, I want real build failures to still block finish, so broken builds are never committed.

## Expected behaviour

- The finish flow should tolerate a repo with no build script (like the manual fallback in SKILL.md: npm run build 2>/dev/null || echo No build script skipping rebuild), or support a configurable/overridable build command (e.g. skip when package.json has no scripts.build, or a --skip-build flag / project-level config).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: implement.py finish completes for a repo whose root package.json has no build script (build step reports skipped/no-op instead of failing).
- AC2: Repos WITH a build script are unaffected — npm run build still runs and a real build failure still blocks finish.
- AC3: Unit tests cover both paths (no build script → skipped; build script present → runs, failure blocks) in tests/test_implement_*.py.
- AC4: Documented in implement SKILL.md (build-step behavior for repos without a build script).
- AC5: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (SorraAgents pytest + Node + bats, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- The target file lives in the SorraAgents framework repo (/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents). Per repo-boundary rules, the change is implemented in SorraAgents via its own implement flow.
- The llm repo already received a workaround (commit f19339f: root build script byte-compiling proxy/); the root-cause fix remains needed for all other repos without a build script.
- The manual fallback pattern is already documented in implement SKILL.md (npm run build 2>/dev/null || echo No build script skipping rebuild).

## Existing state

- run_build() in implement.py unconditionally runs npm run build and treats any non-zero exit as a hard failure that aborts finish.
- llm repo package.json now has a build script (workaround commit f19339f); other Python-only repos remain blocked at the finish build gate.

## Desired change

- Detect absence of a build script in the root package.json (or make the build step tolerant/overridable) and report the build step as skipped/no-op instead of failing; keep the current behavior for repos with a build script (real failures still block).

## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py — run_build() and the Step 2 build gate in phase_finish().
- skill/implement/SKILL.md — document the skip behavior (AC4); manual fallback already present in the worktree-cleanup section.
- tests/test_implement_*.py — add unit tests for the build-step skip/run paths (AC3); precedent: tests/test_implement_worktree_enforcement.py.

## Related work

- SA-0MSHQIADG003PBC4 — implement.py finish refuses to remove worktree when run from inside it (repo-root misdetection): same file/phase fixed via the standard SA implement flow; precedent for how implement.py bugs are tracked and shipped.
- LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL — Archive proxy usage reports: discovered-from; hit this bug and was completed via the manual path.
- commit f19339f (llm repo) — workaround adding a root build script (compileall proxy) so the llm repo passes the finish build gate.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the fix be implemented and tracked in the SorraAgents framework repo (where implement.py lives) rather than the llm repo? — No blocking question needed: the change target is in SorraAgents, and precedent SA-0MSHQIADG003PBC4 confirms framework bugs are implemented there via the SA worklog. Recorded as an assumption; no ambiguity blocks intake.

## Plan (generated by /skill:plan)

Decomposition: single implementation task — this is a small, well-defined bug fix (effort: Small, expected 2.33h; risk: Medium). Vertical-slice phasing not required (item too small to warrant phases).

### Child work items

1. **Fix run_build() to skip when no build script in package.json (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1)** — implement the root-cause fix in run_build(): detect absence of a scripts.build entry in the root package.json and skip the build step (report no-op, return success), keeping npm run build and fail-on-error for repos that have the script. Includes unit tests for both paths and SKILL.md documentation. Covers all parent AC1-AC5.

### Implementation notes for the child

# Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill

## Problem statement

Every skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, ship, etc.) currently ends its session with an ad-hoc, inconsistently formatted summary. Producers must re-scan raw output to extract status, acceptance-criteria verdicts, and next actions. This work standardizes the end-of-session report into a single, quickly scannable format produced by a shared helper skill that other skills call.

## Users

- **Producers/operators** who review the end of every skill session and need to quickly scan: what was done, are acceptance criteria met, what state is the work item in, what actions (if any) are required of them.
- **Agents/skills** that need a canonical, reusable report template with deterministic metadata (avoiding each skill inventing its own format).

### User stories

- As a producer, I want every skill session to end with the same report structure, so I can scan results quickly without re-reading raw session output.
- As a skill author, I want a helper skill that provides the canonical report template and metadata (type, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, children, audit), so my skill produces compliant reports with minimal effort.
- As a producer, I want to see the acceptance criteria with per-criterion met/unmet verdicts, so I can tell at a glance whether the work item is ready.
- As a producer, I want an explicit "Producer Actions" section, so I know exactly what (if anything) I need to do next.
- As a producer, I want a freeform Notes section, so the agent can surface context, caveats, or assumptions that don't fit the structured sections.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new helper skill (e.g., `skill/report/` or `skill/session-report/`) exists with a SKILL.md defining the canonical end-of-session report format exactly as specified: header `# Completed <skill_name>`, work-item title + id, headline summary, `## Acceptance Criteria` table, `## Meta-Data`, `## Producer Actions`, `## Notes`, `## Conclusion`.
- [ ] The report template matches the requested layout: AC rows are `|<ac#>|<Description>|<Metric>|<met|unmet>|`; Meta-Data lists Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit each as `<icon> <text>`; Producer Actions defaults to `None needed`; Notes is freeform; Conclusion states `<This completes the <skill_name> process for <id> (<title>). Ready for <next_action>.`
- [ ] The report includes the `## Notes` section between `## Producer Actions` and `## Conclusion` for freeform agent commentary.
- [ ] Meta-Data values (Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit) are populated deterministically from the work item (via `wl show <id> --json`), so the report reflects the current worklog state rather than the agent's memory.
- [ ] **Icon mappings match the canonical ContextHub set** (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`, the set used by the `wl` CLI itself): priority 🚨/⭐/📋/🐢, status 🔓/🔄/✔️/⛔/🗑️/💬, stage 💡/📥/📋/🛠️/🔍/🏁, risk 🌱/⚠️/🔥/🚨, effort 🐜/🐇/🐕/🐘/🐋, audit ✅/❌/❔, with bracketed text fallbacks (`[CRIT]`, `[OPEN]`, `[IDEA]`, `[LOW]`, `[XS]`, `[YES]`, etc.) when icons are unavailable. The helper documents the full mapping table and its ContextHub source so the sets cannot drift. (ContextHub already provides this shared helper — `src/icons.ts` + `docs/icons-design.md` — so no new ContextHub work item is required; see Related work.)
- [ ] The helper skill documents a clear invocation contract (how another skill calls it at the end of its session — e.g., a short embeddable instruction block) that skills embed as their final step.
- [ ] **All existing skills that work on work-items are wired to invoke the helper** at the end of their session, each with its SKILL.md updated to reference the helper: intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, and author-command (any skill whose flow creates/updates work items). Verification: grep across `skill/*/SKILL.md` shows every work-item skill ends with the standardized report instruction.
- [ ] A test validates the report renderer: given a work item + AC verdicts, it produces the expected report structure (sections present, AC table rows, metadata icons/values, defaults for empty fields).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including the new skill's SKILL.md, README, and any references in migrated skills.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The helper skill is invoked by other skills; it does not replace a skill's own workflow or status lifecycle management.
- The report is produced at the end of a skill session; it should not require new work-item state changes beyond what the calling skill already performs.
- Report must remain scannable: prose sections (headline, Notes) are concise; structured sections carry the details.
- Keep it simple: a single template + metadata renderer (script or documented wl command) is sufficient; no orchestration framework.
- Icon mappings are sourced from ContextHub's canonical set — do not invent new icons in individual skills.

## Existing state

- Skills currently end sessions with ad-hoc summaries: e.g., implement closes with `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary> / Work committed to dev`; intake ends with an Objective/AC/Effort-Risk summary; audit has its own persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status`).
- No shared report template or helper skill exists (`grep` for `## Producer Actions` / `## Meta-Data` / `## Conclusion` across `skill/*/SKILL.md` returns nothing).
- Worklog exposes all needed metadata via `wl show <id> --json` (issueType, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, childCount, auditResult/audit status).
- Effort/risk use t-shirt sizes (XS–XL) from `skill/effort-and-risk/references/t-shirt_sizes.json`; risk levels are low/medium/high.
- **ContextHub already provides the canonical icon set**: `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` (spec) and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (TypeScript implementation), consumed by the `wl` CLI (`dist/icons.js`). Mappings cover priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, and producer-review flags, each with emoji + bracketed text fallback + accessible label.
- Skills live in `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional `scripts/` and `tests/`; global install symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` → this repo's `skill/` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Desired change

1. Create `skill/report/SKILL.md` (or `skill/session-report/`) defining:
   - The canonical report template (exact section order and layout as specified, including `## Notes` before `## Conclusion`).
   - Icon mappings per Meta-Data field sourced from ContextHub's canonical set (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`), with bracketed text fallbacks.
   - Instructions for populating each section (AC verdicts from the calling skill's own evaluation; Meta-Data from `wl show --json`).
   - A short "how to invoke" contract that other skills embed (e.g., a call-out block to add to a skill's final step).
2. Provide `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (or a documented `wl show` + template recipe) that renders the Meta-Data block deterministically from `wl show <id> --json` — helpers to extract/format metadata, icons (reusing ContextHub mappings), and defaults.
3. Wire the helper into **all** work-item skills: update each `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) so the final step invokes the standardized report.
4. Add tests (e.g., `skill/report/tests/`) validating the template and metadata rendering.
5. Add an example rendered report in the SKILL.md so agents can copy the pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — new helper skill defining the canonical report format, ContextHub-sourced icon mappings, and invocation contract.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — metadata renderer reading `wl show --json`, reusing ContextHub icon mappings.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — tests for template structure, metadata icons, defaults.
- `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` for every work-item skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) — final step invokes the helper report.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — its existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, AC status table) is the closest precedent; reconcile its end-of-session summary with the new template.

## Related work

- `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` + `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` — **canonical icon set** (priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, producer-review) with emoji + text fallbacks + accessible labels; consumed by the `wl` CLI. The report skill reuses these mappings. (This is the shared helper the requirement asks for — no new ContextHub work item needed.)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table, `## Variance Decisions`, `## Children Status`); the closest existing structured-report precedent to reconcile/align with.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — defines risk (low/medium/high) and effort t-shirt (XS–XL) values used in the Meta-Data section.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — example helper skill with scripts + tests + a "compact report" pattern.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — skills' shared status/stage transitions; the report's Status/Stage metadata reflects these.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** wiring the helper into every work-item skill is broad; the requirement is explicit, so all work-item skills are in scope for this item. Skills that do not touch work items (e.g., speak) are excluded.
- **Icon consistency:** icon mappings must come from the ContextHub canonical set (single source of truth) to avoid per-skill divergence; the helper documents the mapping table + source. Unknown values fall back to a neutral marker; icons are decorative — the textual value always accompanies them, so reports remain readable in non-emoji terminals/views.
- **Metadata drift:** report reflects the worklog at render time; if the calling skill changes state after rendering, the report may be stale. Mitigation: render the report as the final step of the session.
- **Audit reconciliation:** audit's existing persisted format differs (it is machine-verified). Its end-of-session summary is reconciled with the template; its persisted machine-verified report format is preserved.
- **Assumption:** Meta-Data is rendered deterministically from worklog where possible; the agent supplies only prose (headline, Notes, Producer Actions, Conclusion next-action).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which skill should be the first adopter / what is the migration scope?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Add an AC that wires the helper into all existing skills that work on work-items." The migration scope is therefore ALL work-item skills, not just 1–2 adopters. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What icon mappings should be used?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Icon mappings should be the same as those used in ../ContextHub. If that project does not have a shared helper you can use then create a work item in that project to do so and make this work item dependent upon it." Research: ContextHub provides the canonical icon set in `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (consumed by the `wl` CLI), covering all Meta-Data fields. No new ContextHub work item is required — the helper references that set. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- Q: "Should the report be persisted (e.g., work-item comment) or stdout only?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: stdout only for v1; persistence as follow-up). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).
- Q: "Should Meta-Data be auto-generated from `wl show --json`?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: yes, via a small renderer script). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).

## Summary

Fix `_extract_acs` in skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py so that markdown acceptance criteria (and Success Criteria) written as bullets with wrapped/indented continuation lines are fully extracted, with checkbox markers stripped. Today the extractor stops at the first indented continuation line, so only the first (often truncated) AC is passed to the audit model while the runner can still report 'Ready to close: Yes' — a false-positive QA-gate signal (parent SA-0MSIDPN1N001BEQO).

Approved behaviour (user-confirmed during planning):
- Only **indented** (whitespace-prefixed) continuation lines are folded into the current bullet.
- Extraction still terminates on a heading or a **non-indented** non-list line (e.g. trailing prose after the list).
- Blank lines between bullets keep being skipped (current behaviour preserved).
- Checkbox markers are stripped from bullet ACs only; numbered ACs are left untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_extract_acs` returns all wrapped-bullet ACs from a markdown description, with continuation lines folded into their bullet and checkbox markers stripped (per parent AC 1).
- [ ] Extraction terminates on a heading or a non-indented non-list line (trailing prose after the AC list is not swallowed).
- [ ] Blank lines between bullets are still skipped; single-line bullets, numbered ACs, `Success Criteria` headings, and the no-AC `"No acceptance criteria defined."` fallback behave exactly as before.
- [ ] All tests in skill/audit/tests pass, including the new wrapped-bullet tests added by the test-first child.

## Minimal Implementation

- Modify the line loop in `_extract_acs`: a whitespace-prefixed non-list, non-heading line (when ACs already collected) appends to `acs[-1]` instead of breaking.
- Add a small checkbox-strip helper (`[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]`/`[~]`/`[-]`) applied to bullet text; numbered items untouched.
- Keep heading detection, numbered matching, blank-line skipping, and the no-AC fallback as-is.

## References

- Parent: SA-0MSIDPN1N001BEQO
- Evidence item: OSL-0MSCCFH10001E59N
- Test-first prerequisite: child `_extract_acs wrapped-bullet unit tests`

## Summary

The effort-and-risk skill's workflow instructs agents to capture the orchestrator's JSON output via a shell redirect to a repo-relative path:

```sh
python3 ./scripts/run_skill.py --issue <id> <<'JSON' > final-<id>.json
```

The `final-<id>.json` target is resolved against the *current working directory*. Because the workflow also references scripts as `./scripts/...`, agents run it from inside `skill/effort-and-risk/`, so the artifact lands at `skill/effort-and-risk/final-<id>.json` — an untracked file inside a **tracked skill directory**.

## Problem caused (discovered-from: SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W)

During the SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W implementation session, `skill/effort-and-risk/final-SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W.json` appeared in the main checkout. It:

1. **Dirtied the working tree** and blocked `implement.py start` (its dirty-tree safety gate aborts with exit code 2), forcing a manual worktree bootstrap.
2. **Vanished later in the session** — an untracked file in a skill dir is at the mercy of cleanup processes (e.g. `git clean`), so any retained output there is unreliable.
3. Is a **transient report artifact**, not a deliverable that belongs in the repo — it should live outside the repository entirely (e.g. `/tmp`).

## User story

As an agent running the effort-and-risk skill, I want the orchestrator's JSON output written to a location outside the repository (e.g. `/tmp`), so that the working tree stays clean, `implement.py start` is never blocked by a stray untracked file, and no skill directory accumulates repo pollution.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The effort-and-risk SKILL.md workflow and example redirect the orchestrator output to a path outside the repository (e.g. `/tmp/effort-risk-final-<id>.json`), never to a repo-relative `final-<id>.json`.
2. No invocation documented in SKILL.md can leave an artifact under the repository tree (checked by a test that asserts the documented output path resolves outside the repo, mirroring the audit skill's SKILL.md-validation test pattern at skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py).
3. The skill's scripts/tests remain unchanged unless a genuine path bug is found; the fix is documentation-level (the file is produced by shell redirection, not by any script).
4. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Notes

- Verified the file is created purely by the shell redirect in SKILL.md (grep of `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/` shows no programmatic `final-` output path handling).
- Effort/risk estimates are best-effort; re-run the skill if the report is needed again.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** – Reduce audit skill initial session context size (duplicate AGENTS.md + skills section) (completed)

## Problem statement

Agents working on one project (e.g. ContextHub) routinely discover bugs in **related projects' tooling** — e.g. the SorraAgents framework's `find_related.py` resolving the wrong worklog/repo store (SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI, discovered during ContextHub intake on 2026-08-07). Today bug reporting is ad-hoc and inconsistent: the agent must know to search the target project's worklog, decide whether to add evidence vs create an item, and structure the report — and no code-touching skill systematically does this. Bugs discovered while working get lost or duplicated.

## Goal

A reusable helper skill (e.g. `report-related-bug`) that standardizes reporting bugs discovered in related projects, based on the process followed when reporting SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI.

## Process (based on the observed workflow)

1. **Detect** — while working on item X in project A, a suspected bug is found in project B's code/tooling/skills.
2. **Validate** — search project B's worklog (`wl search <keywords>`, incl. completed items) for an existing item covering the bug; inspect matches with `wl show --format full` to confirm. **Careful: resolve project B's store correctly** (prefix-to-sibling scan can hit the wrong store — see SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI; verify `wl show <candidate>` resolves in B's store).
3. **If a matching item exists** → add the new evidence as a comment: reproduction commands, observed output, impact, any extension of the bug beyond the original description, `discovered-from:<X>` traceability, session id. Never create a duplicate.
4. **If no item exists** → create a `bug` work item in project B's store with structured sections: Problem, Impact, Repro (exact commands + expected vs actual), Suggested fix, Acceptance Criteria, `discovered-from:<X>`.
5. **Traceability & session logging** — always record the reporting action (comment or creation) with `discovered-from:<current-item>` and the PI session id per AGENTS.md conventions.
6. **Non-blocking** — bug reporting must never block the primary task (fire-and-forget or deferred step).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The skill documents the validate → evidence-or-create → traceability workflow above and is runnable via `/skill:report-related-bug <details>`.
- [ ] When a matching open item exists in the target project's store, the skill adds evidence as a comment and does NOT create a duplicate (idempotent, like the triage skill's `check_or_create.py` pattern).
- [ ] When no matching item exists, the skill creates a bug work item in the **correct** target store (prefix-resolved, avoiding the wrong-store pitfall of SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI) with Problem/Impact/Repro/Suggested fix/ACs and `discovered-from` traceability.
- [ ] **The helper skill is wired into ALL skills that work on code** (initial set: implement, audit, test, refactor, code-review, triage, resolve-pr-comments) so that any bug discovered while working is reported through this process — wiring verified by tests/docs per skill.
- [ ] Reporting is non-blocking: discovery never blocks or fails the primary work-item workflow.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the validate/evidence-or-create decision logic (match → evidence, no-match → create, wrong-store detection).
- [ ] All related documentation updated (skill READMEs, AGENTS.md cross-references).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Existing state

- The **triage skill** (`skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`) already implements this pattern for test failures (search existing `test-failure` item → link/update, else create critical item). The new skill generalizes it to arbitrary bugs in related projects.
- The **find-related skill** has the store-resolution bug (SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI) that motivated this work.
- AGENTS.md defines session-logging and work-item reporting conventions to build on.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report-related-bug/SKILL.md` — NEW: the helper skill definition.
- `skill/report-related-bug/scripts/report_bug.py` — NEW: validate/evidence-or-create orchestration (mirroring `triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`).
- `skill/report-related-bug/test_*.py` — NEW: decision-logic tests.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `skill/code-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/triage/SKILL.md`, `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — wire the helper into each code-working skill.
- `AGENTS.md` — cross-reference the new skill in the workflow/guidance sections.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI` — the bug whose reporting process this skill formalizes (open).
- Triage skill `check_or_create.py` — existing validate/evidence-or-create pattern for test failures (precedent).
- Find-related skill — the store-resolution pitfalls the new skill must guard against.
- OSL/ContextHub intake item WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ — where the bug was discovered (`discovered-from`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cross-project store resolution is fragile** (the very bug being formalized): the skill must verify resolution and fail safely (report to operator) rather than creating items in the wrong store.
- **Noise/duplicate risk**: conservative matching required — prefer adding evidence to an existing item over creating a new one.
- **Wiring adoption**: "wired into all code-working skills" requires touching several skill files; each wiring must be minimal (a step + script call), not a rewrite. Assumed acceptable to gate wiring verification per skill via docs/tests.
- **Scope-creep guard**: this item builds the skill + wiring; it does NOT fix SA-0MSIKRXUA003XRXI (separate bug item) and does NOT audit every existing bug for retroactive reporting.
data.title: Create helper skill to report bugs discovered in related projects (validate → evidence-or-create process, wired into code-working skills)
